title: Was great...not so much now.
text:
UPDATE November, 2019:
I think it's time to put my money into a different subscription. Each month, there are fewer and fewer full and "deluxe sample" size products. Those that are full size aren't worth much money. There's no point of me putting my money into so many samples.

OVERVIEW:
I just received my first Cocotique box. I was a little nervous, as I'm new to subscription boxes, but I'm actually quite satisfied with the products. Most of them are full-size, and others are large enough to get quite a few uses out of. The month's box (the actual cardboard box the products are in) is absolutely beautiful! Included is a card with extensive information about all of the products, including prices and where to find them should you decide to purchase them. I absolutely love that they included this because I can easily find the products if I want to order them, and I can see the value of the products versus the cost of the box ($25/month).

PRODUCTS:
With that being said, the value of the products in the box is well worth the cost of the subscription (in this box, at least). The price of the products come up to about double the cost of the box (approximately $47). So, I'm happy with the value. You get more than 2 or 3 items, and they're pretty large.

CUSTOMER SERVICE CONTACT:
One item (eyeshadow) was broken (still sealed). I emailed them on a Saturday and they responded within 2 or 3 hours to apologize and let me know that a replacement was on the way. I greatly appreciate the quick and polite customer service.

SHIPPING:
Shipping was EXTRA fast, but...things are not safely secured in the box. I'm not sure if this is how the eyeshadow box was broken or not, but the products definitely need to be better secured. The products are packaged with pretty crinkled paper, but not enough to hold the products in place. Some products are heavier than others, which may cause some issues in some boxes. This is reason for the 4-star review. All of the products were strewn throughout the box in an unorganized way. Unfortunately, mail carriers don't (and sometimes can't) always take the time to ensure that things aren't thrown around during shipping, so more secure packaging may make things a little better.

BILLING:
I have to be honest and say that the way they do their billing is a bit...odd to me. They bill on your anniversary date, even if the box isn't due to be shipped for weeks. I signed up in early to mid-March, and I just received my first box, the April box. This, of course, depends when you sign up, but when you initially sign up determines if you receive your first box for the CURRENT month or the month after. I was just now charged for next month's box, even though I just received this month's (April) box today. Again, I'm fairly new to subscription boxes and the other ones that I'm subscribed to charge on your anniversary and send your box when you're charged. YES, this is stated in multiple places on Cocotique's website and other places, so I was aware of it, but again, it's just a bit odd to me because it seems like you're waiting for a very long time for something you've paid for. But, that's the way they work and I'll more than happily deal with it to see what they have in store.

BOTTOM LINE:
I will be continuing my subscription. I'm fairly new to the makeup world, so being able to try a wide variety of products (again, these products are large, so you can do a lot more than "try" them) without having to buy all of them one-by-one comes in handy. It saves both money and time. I've definitely told my friends about this subscription box, and I'm excited to see what will be in future boxes. I think I'll be ordering some of the past boxes, also.

As time goes by and I receive more boxes, I'll update my review.

title: Outsized value and variety for under $50
text:
Let me start by saying I was looking for a unique birthday gift for my wife. During my research, Amazon sent me an email with info about subscription box services. I became intrigued and went to Amazon's site to learn more. I came across the Thera Box listing and knew this was the direction. The wife is into health/beauty/spa products, and the listing for TheraBox described everything that she would like, so seemed like a win-win.

Unfortunately the TheraBox arrived too late for her birthday, but would arrive in time for a great Christmas gift.

My wife absolutely freaked when she opened it. Best gift ever. She marveled at the assortment of different items (full size bottles of creams & lotions, a beanie, a neck wrap, plus other goodies) contained in the box. She pressed me about the cost, as were agreed to keep gifts under $100. She couldn't believe the amazing value of items provided for under $50.

She's now recieved her third box and still is amazed every time she gets one. She's so impressed by it that she purchased a TheraBox as a birthday gift for her best friend. And she's working on purchasing a few more for select friends & family.

I'll probably stop the subscription in a month or 2, but I don't regret for one moment in pulling the trigger on that first purchase.

title: They must put crack into this
text: Ok, so I got the first box here half price with the rare Black Friday sale.  I figured I’d get one box then cancel before the full price subscription starts (make sure you do this as soon as it ships if you plan that).  Well, I did that, then got the box... finished it in 3 days and haven’t stopped thinking about it since!  Like any uncustomizable service, you might find some percentage of the set not to your tastes.  However, if you are a true connoisseur of Japanese snacks,  I think you will be impressed by the quality and variety of the offerings.  No, this is not cheap, although I did think it was definitely worth it for the sale price... full price, it is rather extravagant.  On the other hand, I don’t think you would find some of these unusual snacks anywhere else… Not at most nearby asian grocery stores (I live near 5, including large supermarket types with many Japanese snacks).  A few of these can certainly be classed “artisan” and not that mass-produced.  For example, the white chocolate infused strawberry.  I still cannot figure out how they made that.  It’s like the strawberry was actually injected with chocolate as it was freeze-dried, perfectly melded together.  That big spicy cracker thing and the pear cream biscuit were amazing, too.  Many of the other savory snacks also had a lot of complexity and depth to their flavors.  They deftly combine subtle sweet, sour, spicy, salty, and umami notes together.  They put American snacks to shame because these seem to be very one-note in comparison—just sickly sweet or too salty.  I think it’s cool how Bokksu includes a booklet so you can learn more about the snacks and Japanese culture, too (every box has a theme).  To be sure, these are ‘high end’ fancy snacks not for bargain shoppers or those with unadventurous and unelevated palates.  Look, I have easy access to Asian supermarkets within 5 minutes from me and I’m Chinese American—I’m well familiar with shrimp crackers, dried seaweed rice crackers, Pocky, mochi, etc; in contrast, these boxes are not run-of-the mill and is not for everyone.  You have to be willing to try different flavors and clearly, some of the reviewers who didn’t like it weren’t.  Anyway, after I finished the box, I couldn’t stop thinking about it.  After trying to ignore the cravings for a week, I ended up going on the website and purchasing a 6 month subscription for $230.  I never would have thought I’d pay that much for monthly snack boxes before,  but it is officially an addiction now! I’m sure it’s a luxury that I’m not going to be able to afford eventually… however,  I’m going to just try it out for a few months.  I don’t know if I can say $40 a box is “worthwhile” to most people, but for me, I must feed the obsession!

title: Our 5th Grader Loves It...more than Scratch 2.0!
text: Our son just received his first installment of Bitsbox, and got started right away. He was thrilled that he could see immediately whether his coding was working or not. As well, the program gives feedback every time he tries to run a script-- if there's a mistake, it lets him know the approximate line that has the mistake. It will really help our son slow down to make sure details are exact-- a great skill for test taking in the classroom. Sharing his app with others is also very easy, and he got such joy out of seeing people react with excitement and fun when trying to play the game he coded. The Bitsbox program allows him to be successful enough to build his confidence to explore writing script on his own, which is something he seemed much more hesitant to do with Scratch 2.0. I think the biggest difference between the two is that Bitsbox makes it so easy to find mistakes every few lines. Plus, I think the layout is more attractive, as Bitsbox literally looks like an app on a smartphone or tablet. So, he gets that sense that he's doing what professional coders do. Way to go Bitsbox!

text:
First month I got London Calling, great album. No complaints. It's a good pressing, and sounds great.

Second month, Bitches Brew by Miles Davis. Again, great album, but I already have a good copy. Checked multiple times per day to see what album was next on the website, and when it finally showed what it was, it was too late to cancel. Like, couldn't have been more than a couple hours between checking and it was unable to cancel the shipment. I'm not sure if I'll be returning it, or gifting one of the copies, but a little heads up with time to cancel if not wanted would have been super awesome.

From what I've seen in the comments of what others are getting, it looks like largely good selections. A few duds (picture disks aren't for everyone), but a good variety of music to flesh out a collection. Having a few hundred albums already, I suspect this subscription is going to be a bit hit and miss. I hope they can work the bugs out and maybe find a way to link a Discogs account.

Update: Kind of swung the other way on timing. This time I got notification of what it was going to be at the end of September, it isn't going to ship until sometime in November. Exile on Main Street is a solid choice, and I don't already own it. But what's the point of a Vinyl of the Month Club if it is ordered one month and shows up two months later. Maybe a button to say yes I want this or skip this month with a couple of days before it auto ships would be better. Then, it should also be something in stock. I get the supply chain issues are a problem right now for vinyl, I've got half a dozen pre-orders pending for things, but I know the warehouse can't be completely devoid of things that are in stock.

title: 1st try of Allure & NOTHING like the picture as they say - "masking" a real "beauty box" somewhere?
text:
All masks?? Wha wha what??? Can't be. Was so excited to finally try Allure beauty box. They teased me with a $5 Black Friday discount to try them, so I said why not? Look at all the great stuff they like to put in THEIR boxes..how exciting!

My review is going to be one of disappointment.

Allure is proud to talk up and flash beautiful pictures in front of me of a wide and varied amount of miscellaneous products they want me to try including surprise bonuses. Here I am a brand new customer delighted to try these varied possible products I see in all the pictures.... Only to get home and open up my bright red box and go through one item after another only to discover they're all masks. From your lips to your feet. I have nothing against masks, I think they're great. However I can go out and buy a mask at any time. In fact one mask would have been fine. but my whole entire box is nothing but masks. Oh wait, there is a teeny tiny little box with three hair rings in it, cute but I think most people have hair ties of some sort? I guess that's for holding back your hair so you can do a face mask, a lip mask ,and put some eye gels on your eyes all at the same time , put the foot masks on too and boom you've used 5/7ths of your box all at once. I get that November is mask month apparently? (just read that somewhere before I wrote this review) If I had known that ahead of time I would not have started an Allure subscription even with a discount? November? Why didn't they send me December? It started soon enough.... just not quite sure this is the box to introduce to a new customer.... Oh wait there's a coupon inside that will also give you a $10 gift to enjoy at Anthropologie..... but only if you spend a minimum of $50. Yay.

Well thank you Allure - but I'm not at all impressed and will be canceling my subscription right now. I would not recommend this subscription. I would suggest that they give a welcome box to new customers. At least make them feel special at the beginning if nothing else.

title: Fun enough to see what you get, but certainly not worth the cost.
text: I was definitely not expecting to receive anything spectacular with this subscription box, but what I got was below expectations. I would say that 80% of it was just pure junk unless you have a very specific project to use it for. Both orders I received included video cards that were not actually all that bad, but most of the rest of it was unusable (for me anyway). My second box included an old Intel motherboard that I was able to sell on eBay for $20, which recouped some of what I paid for the box, but it arrived absolutely filthy-- it was caked with dust that I had to clean off just to get it to point where I felt comfortable selling it, not to mention the fact that I felt as if I needed to test it before selling, so that was a decent amount of work just to recoup some of the money I spent. Honestly, the Excelius branded tchotchkes they include with every box are probably the best part of the whole deal. You might get an optical drive for a laptop, but that doesn't do you a whole lot of good unless you have the same model laptop with a faulty optical drive, or if you care to take the time to sell it on eBay for $10 or less. To be clear, you are paying $30 for the fun of opening up a box to see what might be useful to you out of $20+ worth of discarded electronics. I am not unhappy that I did it for two months, but I can't help but feel like now I have to find some way to get rid of most of this crap. You'd be way better off analyzing what old components you actually need and spending that same $30 (or less) on those parts elsewhere.

title: Time will tell
text:
I signed up for the 5-7 year old plan since I have a 5 and 6 year old at home. I jumped at this once I saw it. I always had fun educational toys to tinker with growing up, mostly from Radio Shack back then.

Kind of bummed out over the first toy. It clearly says 8+ on the box. We were able to get some use out of it, but it was defiantly over their heads/attention span, (Snap Circuits Fundamentals); trying to explain electrical currents to a 5 year old is difficult. Nothing against the product, It is a pretty nice setup. What happened is I played with it for about an hour and let the boys do what they could and I answered any questions they had. They defiantly got some use out of it, I just had to guide them quite a bit. Not a total loss and it will be there for when they are older. Could have been avoided with an age appropriate toy though, especially the first toy out of the gate like that.

The value is there though. I feel I got my $20 worth.

Edit 9-25-17:
I bumped it from 3 stars to 4. Not much has changed, it is still hit and miss. Some shipments have been great, some have not (I'm looking at you magic school bus.) But, the value has been there throughout. We got some great building sets and some fun experiments out of this and I plan on keeping the subscription for a while. I think some of the best things about this subscription are the assortment of products I probobly wouldn't buy on my own, the monthly consistency, and the price; you tend to get very good deals on what is sent. Dislikes are sometimes you end up with a dud, and sometimes the shipment doesn't quite fit in the age range intended.

She caught the scent of the cat-nip laundry sack, and it was ON. She made a fool of herself when dad finally gave it to her... I’m talking chewing on it, rolling over like a dog, and all around turning into a feline frenzied fool.
Just yesterday, box 2 came. This time it was a safari theme... and my cat was SITTING on the box waiting for one of her slow brained parents to OPENTHEBOX! Got it, kiddo. Out came feathers on a stick - a classic favorite... a crinkly elephant which she immediately crunched to death... a catnip toy which is strangely MIA this morning... a toy hat with a bell that has impressive air-time when tossed like a frisbee and I think something else my husband stashed from her.
I love that this takes the annoying portion of finding toys that she wants/likes at the big name stores and paying the ridiculous prices out of the picture. I don’t have to spend an hour searching for them on amazon either. Someone who clearly knows cats is doing that for me. title: Total Bomb
text:
Got the Deadpool box. It was meh. Between the cool Pop and keychain I would have paid 30 but it wasn't a "deal". Skipped Venom. Not a big fan. Marvel 10 year!!! This could be cool. Maybe a bunch of small stuff spanning all the movies. Maybe a large exclusive avengers Pop! Nope.
Ironman 2 with Ironman fighting Whiplash as the big pop. A pez and a couple of dorbz. If this had been $10 I wouldn't have bought it.
10 years of Marvel and you picked the big Pop from the Movie that's consistently in most fans bottom 5. 10 years and that's your go to. And a hulk pez from Ragnorak. Meh. And two dorbz from Ragnorak. Meh and you already covered that with the pez.
Never again. It's a piddling amount of stuff for a loot box but also horribly curated.
The Funko Pop does look cool. It's well made and it was one of Ironman's cooler suits but come on. 10 years to pull from.

Subscription officially cancelled and no box will entice me back.

Edit** Three things.
One I should talk about the overall subscription. They say 4 to 7 items. Of the three boxes they’ve had two with 4 and one with 5.... Also t-shirt not guaranteed despite giving t-shirt size with subscription. Okay. Of three boxes only one has had a shirt and if I’m reading it right the X-Men box won’t have a shirt. So one of four. So while this review mostly hit the ten year box the overall value would also get a one.

Two. In case anyone from Amazon or Funko is reading here’s how you might fix this. Send everyone who got the ten year box a shirt with every character in the MCU to date in funko form. Fighting. Holding hands. Just standing there. Whatever. Don’t forget Stan Lee. Then for the X-Men box you need shirt with a team of X-Men. If you have a box like X-Men or 10 year you have to have a shirt. No way to encompass a team or timeline with individual items. For the pop figure probably do Phoenix. Dark or regular. Maybe Wolverine. Definitely have to have something Wolverine. Decal. Stress ball. Then an X-Men logo keychain. Then a side character something. Nightcrawler. Jubilee. A character maybe someone wouldn’t normally buy but are happy to see. And 7 items in this box. You’re buying back some credit.

Third. What the 10 year box should have been. The above mentioned shirt. That covers 10 years. The Pop. Iron man in the Mark 1 armor with no helmet. Or Mark 1 half off, the desert scene after the fight. Or Mark 1 with flames coming out of flamethrower. First superhero moment in MCU. There are other options. A Stan Lee pop. But the Mark 1 would have been good. Something Avengers. Keychain. Decal. Check. Something Guardians of the Galaxy. Then a few random whatevers. A Teseract stress ball or paperweitht. Infinity Gauntlet something. Black panther. Empty keychain labeled Ant-Man. Etc. So if anyone from Amazon or Funko! Is reading this here you go.

2nd edit.
Saw the Funko Marvel subscription was in danger of being below three stars. All of a sudden a sprinkling of 5 star reviews appear. Just enough to keep it at 3 stars... Wish I could give a negative 5 stars for that cheap play on Funko or Amazon's part.

3rd edit
Just Sam the X-Men box. Yeah. Glad I cancelled. I honestly don’t know how they even value the contents at $30. $15 pop, $5 socks, $1 pencil topper, $3 notebook, and candy for a few bucks. If they’re claiming these things cost more than that retail then wow. Consumers complained and they doubled down with less value and worse crap.

title: If you're looking for a deal, look elsewhere
text:
This is a tiny amount of coffee for $24; something like half a pound for four different flavors. It's not remotely a value, and if that's bothersome, move on to something else.

However, what you do get is the opportunity to try four possibly delicious varieties, but certainly high quality, different flavors of coffee every month. On more than one occasion I've spent $20 or more on a pound of coffee I didn't want to finish. This gives me the chance to spend $6 a flavor and explore coffees I would never have tried any other way.

One thing I want to emphasize is each of the four samples I got were incredibly fresh, and very high quality. I'm typically incredibly picky with my beans, and each of the four had something about them that I liked.

I'm going to keep my subscription going for as long as the variety adds $24 a month of value to my life. Maybe I'll find a new favorite bean, and that might be worth it on its own.

title: STEM subscription for homeschool kiddo
text:
I homeschool our 6yo grandson and wanted a STEM or STEAM subscription service to introduce into our curriculum. Researched several and opted for the Amazon service for multiple reasons (namely price and returns). Subscribed to the 8-13 level because it seemed he had already done a lot of the experiments listed in the description for 5-7yo category. Definitely challenging and will last quite awhile. First shipment was the Lasers, which I was looking at buying anyway - glad I did not because it was cheaper thru the subscription service.

Do wish Amazon would alert buyer to what's next in the service though - give an "opt out" to that months shipment. I anticipate some of the future shipments will include items we already have or have done and I will need to return as a result. I only get an email 1 day prior to delivery letting me know what's coming.

title: Great value, our pup loves her bark box!
text: I absolutely loved our Bark Box, and so did our pup! In our box, we received some Really good coupons for the next box and more treats, two full-sized toys, two full-sized bags of treats, and a large chew stick, which she devoured within minutes. I really like that Bark Box makes it possible to choose a box for your dog’s size. This isn’t one of those “one-size fits all” services, which is great! Our pup hid her toys in her spot almost immediately, as she normally does. She occasionally plays with them, however she is more of a hoarder than a player (she’s a beagle mix, beagles hide and hoard things they like). Anyways, she LOVES the treats! She gets excited anytime she hears the bag. I love that the treats are good for her, not filled with unnecessary fillers and chemicals. She loves eating them, and I love that she’s getting something good for her. All in all, Bark Box is a great value for everything you get! I’m very happy and very impressed with what we received!

title: Isn’t As Tailored As Advertised
text:
I’ve decided to quit after two. Here are the pros and cons that pushed me in that direction and a little about the box in general.
There is no theme to the things they put in. There’s a little leaflet where a few “editors” write a blurb about why they like some particular product.
I did receive things I might not have gone out and purchased. They all seem to have a penchant for pre-made masks. And trial sizes. So, on the plus side I was introduced to new things.
The only things I’ve received full size were mascara and eye liner. Everything else was trial or one out of a set.
Prior to starting I answered a bunch of questions meant to “tailor” the products. This last box had something for oily skin (mine is dry) and a brown lip liner (I’m very fair). According to the blurb from the leaflet it came in two colours. The other may have worked.
The final deal breaker was another product that wouldn’t have worked for me and wasn’t sealed. It leaked everywhere. It’s a lot of fun cleaning up tissue-lined paper box.
This months’ package was meant to include two masks according to the leaflet, but had only one.
I really hadn’t expected one this month due to the CV thing going on. If they did go ahead with it I’d have thought they’d have gone above and beyond to make one designed as a sort of pick me up. I don’t hold it against them that they didn’t, but did that they did such a poor job.
The missing, the leaking and wrong stuff does bother me. Also, I’m really not at all sure the value is there. Trial sizes don’t cost much, even at retail. Most any department store could put together a better selection.
And so, immediately after I’m done here I’ll be unsubscribing.
I hope this is helpful to someone.

title: Size Runs VERY Small and Short
text:
I'm 5'11 and am usually a 2XL. Since this was going to be my first order, I went up one size to 3XL. It fit like a brand name XL in terms of width. It was very short, barely reaching my waist. This shirt might fit someone 5'6" and on the heavy side. No way it wil fit anyone over 5'8". It's just not going to cover their front or rear, especially if bending, stretching or leaning. I measured the chest across and it was 2" shorter than the size chart said it was. Which means, it's 4" too narrow for it's size. As a 2XL I could probably have worn it but with any shrinkage in wash cycle, it would be too small and too short.

The other issue is that this is one of the thinnest and lightest weight tee shirts I have ever purchased. I would expect that after 20-30 wash and wear cycles it would become thin and essentially unusable.

title: Good value, boring selection, slightly deceptive display pics
text:
Here's my review of the July K-Glow Box. This is what's inside:

*Leaders - What Happened Last Night? Glowing Facial Mist
*Jeju:en Hyaluron Hydrogel Lip Patches
*Jeju:en Propolis Cream
*BetterSkin Premium Volcanic Ash & Botanical Fermentation Detoxing Sheet Mask
*Medius Ampoule Synergy - Moisture Plus
*Mediheal Cica: Ming Mask
*NoHj Healing Mask Pack Lustre

First off, I gotta say the display image for the K-Glow box is deceptive... It shows 3 full size items, a speciality item, and FIVE masks. Except the description itself says 3 full size items, 3 masks, and 1 specialty item... And I got 3 full size items and 4 masks (NO specialty item).

Here's my unpopular opinion on k beauty skincare.. Exoticism is a great marketing tool; in the past it was all about those exotic French women with their beauty secrets, and skincare brands with French names sold as luxury items. Now it's all about Korean beauty. In reality, a lot of these masks and creams are really just basic drugstore quality products in Korea, there's anything better about a Leaders face mist than something you could pick up at your local drugstore.

I'm Asian, I've lived in Asia. I've gone shopping in Myeongdong a couple times, and Facetory sells brands like Nature Republic masks at a 1000% markup (compared to what you'd pay for a pack of masks). Paying more for a foreign products doesn't mean it's inherently superior. I'd pay extra for stuff I can't find equivalents of here, but a basic cream and a face mist was a boring letdown considering I might as well just pick some up at the store five minutes from my house. If I'm paying for foreign products, I'd like stuff I can't easily find here, like k beauty serums or unique ingredients like slug.

To be clear: the K-Glow box is a good value, but the selection was a little boring--stuff you can easily find local equivalents of. I don't need a K beauty box for that, and

title: Haven’t Tried This Yet, But Might If I Can Get Some Answers?
text:
VMP offers yearly subscription for a cheaper price if you buy a year at a time. I also get a email notification from them and I can either skip the copy or get a previous copy to sell as they sell for a lot compared with most record clubs. It’s more expensive, but they make the covers which are very thick and all of the pressings are exclusive and 180g pressings. Some are even 45rpm remastered. I know many people are going to say they don’t like VMP or it’s too expensive. But I like knowing what I am getting and have plenty of time to exchange it, or if I don’t want a duplicate or something else, I will get a month’s credit.

The one thing that Amazon has FINALLY made an improvement with is their packaging for vinyl. The old method was absolutely terrible and I never purchased vinyl from Amazon because of this issue. I recently purchased two Phish LP on LP copies and discovered that they finally updated their packaging procedure!

Almost every album I would order, would arrive with either bent edges or corners, or worse, large seam splits or both! I can’t say it’s the post office every time either. I returned a copy of Bob Mould - Workbook 25 because it had about 2 inches of the spine missing from poor packaging. Another issue I have had with Amazon and vinyl pressings is that in the past, I ordered two Mobile Fidelity Sound Labs pressings and they kept saying it wasn’t in stock. I finally bought the two pressings from Music Direct, the owner of the MoFi label now, and canceled the Amazon copies. I don’t know why they didn’t have them in stock as they where not exactly low numbered repressings like some of the newer ones. However Amazon charged me for the crappy mp3 that they sent, instead of removing them. I don’t do mp3 format! Yes that sounds like a snobbish remark, but it’s a crude format! It’s why I have owned 4 Astell&Kern players over the years and I buy downloads that are in 24Bit/192 kHz or DSD. MQA is an amazing sounding format as well and I own several MQA CDs that I have ordered from Japan! You need a computer and special DAC to unfold the true sound of these releases! I have some great downloads that are 24Bit /96kHz as well. Amazon still charged me $9.99 each for the two albums they could have gotten and it was for a service I don’t even use! I don’t understand why they didn’t have the copies in stock in the first place because everyone else online had them in stock!

My last complaint about buying vinyl pressings from Amazon is that third party sellers are not listing their used vinyl pressings in the correct place. Yes, I know this Vinyl of the Month subscription is different, but their used Vinyl and CDs is a complete mess! I have sent back several that were listed as a certain pressings only to get a different pressing! Some of these albums have upwards of 200+ pressings. Yet they let third party sellers list them just anywhere! I purchased a copy of Queen - The Game that was supposed to be a MFSL copy and NM. It had a photo of the MFSL album . I even sent an email to the seller saying that if it wasn’t an MFSL issue, don’t send it! Well I got a terrible US pressing that was dirty and had severe ring wear. I tried to contact the seller and he was gone with my $75.00.

I haven’t purchased any Vinyl or CDs or SACDs from the third party sellers in a long time. I just got feed up with buying items that where listed incorrectly or the sellers idea of NM is much different than what the average person would consider NM, even to the people who have no clue about grading vinyl.

I’m going to post a question before I decide on weather or not this is a Record of the Month club I would want to be part of or is it not something I would like. So far the titles listed are copies I already have a few different pressings of. I’m also not a huge fan of picture disc, as they sound terrible for the most part. I have two copies of Pink Floyd - The Wall, one is a Japanese pressing and the other is a MFSL pressing. I have 5 copies of The Clash - London Calling. A earlier Japanese pressing, a red unofficial version, a couple of U.K. pressings and I bought a Clear Vinyl 50th Anniversary release that I have not played or opened as it is worth over $450.00+ on Discogs. I got it for about $70.00.

I’m also a little bit put off by customers saying that they got a different copy for the month than others got. That never happens with VMP! So I will have to see what response I get to my question about these albums that are being sent out before I join another vinyl club!

title: Perfect for the Right Couple
text:
Read the reviews and you'll know right away if this is for you. Do you take yourself seriously? Don't order. Do you like fancy restaurants and culture for your date nights? This isn't for you. Do you want each shipment to be an investment in products that you can use again and again? Um, that's not what a date night is, so no.

My husband and I have been married 19 years. We're both introverts but we enjoy laughing together. I'm a top-of-the-ladder professional and my husband is a "guys guy" type who wears steel toed boots to work. We firmly believe the science that doing something novel together builds our relationship and we're willing to try new things. But unless you have a lot of time and money and a reliable babysitter, it's hard to find novel activities. The point of the date night is each other.

The latest date was Hippie themed. We learned to tie dye bandanas, played a card game that had us answering questions to understand each other better, did face paint on each other that symbolized questions we wanted the other person to answer (and took photos and washed it off because we do have jobs to get to in the morning), etc.

One box lasts us multiple nights because we're tired and we only have the stamina for one activity per night. Also we use the activities as jumping off points to actually connect with each other, not just check the box that we did the activity. We have fun together. And that takes time.

At first $40 felt like a lot but a lot of thought and planning goes into each box. Yes, you could buy an expensive board game for $40 and play it many times. But that's not really the point. The activities are all designed by a therapist to help us connect with each other. After 19 years and 2 kids, that's something we desperately needed. Some of the activities keep on giving,
the card game this month has replay value. One box is worth about 4 sessions of marriage counseling for us... and that's a steal at $40! (And I do love the sturdy little boxes and use them for storage when we're done).

We currently have 5 adult cats and 7 kittens (only 1 over 6 months of age) under the roof at the moment.

Looks like this box's theme was "adult stuff." Wine treat, whiskey bottle toy, martini glass toy, cigar bunny kicker toy, romance "novel" toy, suitcase toy, and candy themed wand toy.

The cardboard box absorbed all of the catnip as it's the only item the adults showed interest in. Or it could just be that it's a perfect sized box for most of the adult cats and there wasn't really any strong catnip to begin with. 🤷🏼‍♀️

The replacement kitty wine leaked in the box during shipping. None of the catnip kitties liked the wine. The venison liver treats that were supposed to be included would have gone over well with the foster kittens and possibly some of the adults.

The wand toy is loved by the kittens and a couple of the adult cats. However, I can buy these types of wands for only $2 all year round.

We have 2 resident bunny kicker kitties and neither of them like the cigar toy.

The kittens are too young to be affected by catnip, but they are the only ones enjoying these overpriced toys. One of the foster kittens carries the luggage toy around in his mouth by the handle but I've never been able to get a picture of that adorableness! That uncaptured cuteness is what bumps this box to a solid 2 stars.

Maybe July just wasn't the best month for me to try out. 🤷🏼‍♀️ I probably should've waited until October.

title: Best beauty subscription for redheads
text:
How to Be a Redhead is a great beauty subscription box with a unique specialty— it’s for redheads. It’s available as a regular monthly subscription (for $25) or deluxe subscription (for $65 which arrives quarterly) both are well worth it and both are packed with goodies that are suitable for redheads!

For years I wanted to buy one of those monthly beauty subscription boxes, but I never did because I knew from experience that any time I’d buy an all inclusive selection of makeup (skin products, or eyeshadow palettes etc…) inevitably I end up getting annoyed and frustrated that almost everything in it is suited to “average” skin tones, which (compared to most redheads) that ends up being about 3-to-4 shades too dark— and therefore half of the pre-selected items would be useless— and that’s if I’m lucky! It usually ended up being more like 80% useless products that are all wrong for a redhead’s skin.

I understand the redhead population is relatively small (it’s estimated at only 1%–2% of the world’s population) but that said, it’s still a lot of people and as consumers, a redhead’s money is worth every bit as much as a blonde’s or a brunette’s, so it annoyed me how everything was catered to being either blonde or brunette and redheads (along with other groups) were all relegated to one “miscellaneous” category. Understanding this is one thing but I still wished I could easily find suitable products.

After years of feeling left out, I stumbled upon #H2BARbox. It’s been a godsend.

Each month your $25/ monthly subscription box is supposed to deliver a selection of redhead-friendly products to your door, said to be valued at many times more expensive than that $25/month subscription amount— and FTR, I do believe this to be true. I’m generally a skeptical person so I usually go online and check the individual prices myself just to make sure their claims hold up and to make sure I’m really getting my money’s worth.

Now, to be clear— it’s not always makeup, and it’s not always skincare. On average, the breakdown is APPROXIMATELY 70%-30%, the majority of them being hair and skincare products. Another complaint I read was the products are not always JUST for redheads.

NB: #H2BAR never claimed they curate products that are for “REDHEADS ONLY”, it’s just that some people apparently read into their description too much and then were disappointed the products were I guess “too versatile”? Since it’s estimated that Redheads only make up about 1%–2% of the earth’s population, it shouldn’t be surprising that makeup and beauty product manufacturers are not rushing to gear entire product lines towards such a small, niche market. Of course only SOME products will be for “redheads only”… but ALL will be “redhead friendly”, and that’s what was missing from other beauty box subscriptions.

The only real complaint that I have is that the perceived value of boxes is sometimes inconsistent. That is to say, some months the amount you get *feels* like you are really getting a great value and you can easily see how the sum of the products would retail for well over $250… but other months it doesn’t seem that way and it feels like you’re getting less. They would do well to even it out.

So to sum up, it sometimes feels lopsided. One month you might get a tube of sunblock, a fabulous full size Paul Mitchell shampoo and conditioner, a cute little makeup bag or brush, a nice moisturizer or a face serum, a pretty lipgloss in a redhead friendly shade, a mascara or eyebrow pencil (also in redhead friendly shades) and maybe a sample or two (usually of a higher-end, new &/or more expensive product, like toner or face serum) and on those months, you couldn’t be happier with your subscription. Those months you can easily see the value and you are thrilled with what you’re getting for $25…

but then other months— you’re less than thrilled. Some shipments feel too heavy on the samples. Samples are great too,and they’re appreciated in a beauty subscription box— especially when it’s a luxury brand—but add too many samples and it starts to feel (and look) cheap. Plus, it gets annoying.

I always put samples aside for “travel” but then they end up being forgotten (or passed over in favor of bringing something else I’ve already tried and I KNOW works for me and that I’m sure I like) samples often get lost or expire and then have to be discarded, after they’ve withered away at the bottom of my beauty stash.

Another issue I have with the excessive sample sizes is that the writing on the packages is always minuscule (or non-existent) and you have to save the little postcard that comes along with each shipment (which details the items they included that month, describes what it does, and/or its ingredients) and it inevitably gets lost or thrown away. In my experience, you pretty much have to use them right away— but, depending on what the samples are (e.g. sunblock or deep conditioning masque) you don’t necessarily need or WANT to use them right away, but I always find if I don’t use the samples right away, they just fall by the wayside. If I can’t identify the contents of the sample and it’s been sitting in my drawer for months. If I’m not sure of the contents, I usually just end up throwing them out.

Although I have checked H2BAR’s claims (I’ve googled each and every product) and I found that YES, technically the products WOULD retail for at least $250 and each box DOES work out to be roughly the same value from month-to-month (dollar-wise… the items always retail for CONSIDERABLY more than the $25/ month subscription price) but some months it doesn’t SEEM like you’re getting an equivalent amount compared to previous months. One month you’re delighted with your #H2BARbox haul… but then other times you feel little bit disappointed and the amount feels a little thin, by comparison.

For example:
Claim: to (usually) send full-sized products

Truth: Yes. Mostly this is the case— USUALLY, *but* occasionally (especially when they include something like a boutique brand, or higher-and serum, for example or some other prohibitively expensive item no one could possibly reasonably expect to receive a full-sized container of that item (along with several other products) inside their $25/monthly subscription box… they just give you a department store style sample. Sometimes there’s an online coupon code for10%-15% off that product (in addition, or sometimes INSTEAD of an actual sample) for said item. Those are annoying and truthfully (because you’d have to shell out additional money for that item to even get the discount) I don’t factor those into the overall value of the #H2BARbox or even appreciate getting those at all. It also doesn’t help that I usually don’t even know anything about the brand, or if I even like the product they’re giving me the coupon for, plus they ARE asking you to drive to a store (or order online and pay shipping) and you’d have to shell out more cash. These days, if you want me traipsing around a mall or shopping center, then you’re going to have to do better than that. Usually the discount they offering is ONLY about 10% or 15% off. That’s probably the manufacture’s doing, but still… #H2BAR IS including these coupons on occasion and they make it feel off-brand— very tacky.

That’s all well and good, but looking at the contents on those “thin months”, I can safely say that if that paltry LOOKING box (even though the cash value is probably equal to or greater than the others) can be a detriment. Last month’s box was a little heavy on the samples for my taste, and honestly I would have preferred it if they’d combined the value of those trial sizes and just thrown in one full size product instead (not even necessarily that same item or brand) just a full sized SOMETHING, rather than tons of trial size it’s preferable to the alternative, which is getting the same number of fluid ounces as the full size, only in sample/ trial-size form. If that month had been my very first foray into #H2BARbox, then I might have been one of those people griping online about it, and my first shipment would have been my last. My only complaint is about the lack of consistency there was in *perceived value* of boxes from one month, to the next. First impressions are everything and some months H2BAR makes a better impression than it does on others.

If I had received a sample-heavy box my first (or 2nd) month, I probably would have just canceled my subscription right then and there too. The majority of negative reviews I have read though are from people who are unhappy because of the of people who use hair color, well news flash: there are people who are natural redheads and who also use hair color, sometimes to touch up gray hair, sometimes just for fun.

When you love a product, you’re happy. When you’re not-so-in-love with what they sent, you want to know you at least got your money’s worth. Most people are not going to have the patience to google the price of each item like I did. People just eyeball it. They size it up, and rely on *perceived value*. If customers are happy because they *think* they’re getting a good deal, then they usually ARE getting a good deal.

Overall though, I still think the #H2BARbox is fantastic. It’s a great gift for a redhead (or for anyone with similar pale or rosy skin tone) there is nothing else like this— not that I’ve ever seen.

As a company though I do think they would do well to make each monthly shipment more consistent in its *perceived value* (vs. its actual/cash value, “costs a lot” doesn’t always = “looks expensive”)… because judging by the (relatively few) negative Amazon reviews, that seemed to be the most repetitive theme.

The other complaints were about the brands. There are no “cheap” brands. Some reviewer was upset because she’d never heard of a particular brand of skincare product, so she decided they must have thrown it in there because it must be “cheap”— meanwhile it was a luxe boutique brand and she wasn’t familiar with it because the entire line was brand new, she’s obviously a bargain shopper and it’s not sold in drugstores.

If you’re someone who’s brand loyal, who has a narrow scope of “faves” And you just want to use the same products over and over again, then H2BAR (and in all likelihood, also any other beauty subscription box) is probably just not for you.

It’s like handing a friend $25 and saying “You know I’m a redhead and you know what kinds of beauty products I usually buy, Here’s $25— surprise me!”

If that sounds like a fun idea or something interesting you’d be curious to try, then you’ll probably love #H2BARbox too.

If you are someone who’s open to trying new beauty and skincare products, if you’re someone who loves little surprises and who enjoys discovering and trying new brands— AND you also happen to be a redhead, then you’ll probably love it too.

title: Overpriced for Cheap Items
text:
$40 for THIS??? Seriously??? Who are they kidding? 3 of the items I can get at Target for around $15 and then get a $5 coupon back (a face mask, toner, face wipes- these items are so cheap!). A small candle- the $5 size, a “volcano” bracelet (which, I must admit, I was a bit excited about, at first, because I had looked into these in the past and had wanted one) that was so cheap it broke within a week, a lavender pillow spray/sheet mist, and some kind of roll on essential oil. Then there were 2 books both of which were a bit on the silly side. 1 was meant for a very specific audience- ones who travel around the world, frequently and like to journal their “adventures” and want to record all the clothes they pack for their trips (why?). The second one was a scratch off book. You’re supposed to scratch one bubble a day then you “have” to do what it says and it says ridiculous things- “light a candle”, “watch the sun rise”, “meditate”. Generic things that honestly you are either already doing or really have no interest in doing.
It’s a good idea “in theory” but it’s WAAAAAYYYYY overpriced!!! I may have kept the subscription going for $25/mo, but $40/mo is SUCH a ripoff. Plus, you end up with extra crap in your house that you absolutely don’t want or need.
I can say though, the packaging is lovely and it was fun to receive a “surprise” package in the mail. So...there’s that...

title: Wonderful!
text:
We ordered the family trio box. This was our first month, and I ordered in early December. Unfortunately, due to the joy of shipping during covid we didn't get it until after Christmas.

Our box came absolutely trashed and I was really concerned about what was inside. Originally, I was going to wait to open it until I had the kids with me so we could discover it together, but since it was ripped and crushed, I opened to make sure it was salvageable. Right off the bat I found a nutcracker head rolling around. I found his body, and reattached, then wrapped him back up in the tissue paper he came in. It came with some candy for each kid, a gingerbread man to decorate, a reindeer to decorate and the nutcracker, along with books wrapped up like gifts. I purposely did not open the books so that we at least got one surprise out of it.

My kids were super excited when I opened a box of books and candy (mostly for the candy, but hey. Books are cool too right?). My middle son claimed the nutcracker as his own before even opening the books. I realized one of my kids is younger and would have gotten the early reader book... so I PRAYED I had picked the right books for each kid, and handed them out.

They ripped them open to reveal an early reader Gingerbread Man, Nutcracked, and the Naughty List. Books none of my children had read before (even if they are older books, as they certainly look it from the covers, they were excited for new reading!) They're off chewing on suckers (yes. chewing. That is why they are off. They don't get to sit near me chomping on hard candies...) and reading their new books.
This was a shot in the dark for something to bring my kids books for their reading levels, and I'm really happy it worked out quite well! I'll see if I can get some pictures later, when my kids aren't munching on hard candies.

text:

For nearly $30 you get maybe $5 worth of items. The recipes are interesting, but I can buy a whole cookbook of child friendly and interesting recipes for that price, and have money to spare. My son is a huge fan of Gordon Ramsey and was thoroughly unimpressed by this kit, the conversation cards, and the dollar store quality tools.

I have already cancelled this subscription three times and somehow they keep adding me back to the list. I cancelled immediately after submitting for the promotion in December, because I wanted to try it out but didn't want to be roped into a subscription before deciding.

My son is 9 and an excellent little cook and foodie. My son thought this didn't offer anything more than we already have an do at home, and in fact had a lot of negative things to say about the kit overall. I was glad I had already cancelled.

Lo and behold, after Christmas while looking for things to spend a giftcard on, we were subscribed again and I cancelled again.

Today I logged into my account to order a birthday gift for a friend, and saw an order for January in my account! THIS is the third time now I've seen this in my account. I have gotten confirmation each time I've cancelled. I again got confirmation, but this order was placed on the 1st, after being cancelled twice previously, and is now "up to the seller" if they'll cancel. I am calling my bank and reporting thia as a fraudulent charge. I have received multiple cancellation confirmations.

My guess is they know this kit is garbage and has to resort to fraudulent practices to keep selling them.

title: Great Tea!
text:
I will say that I'm not much of a tea connoisseur - I've always kind of liked tea but never knew much about it. I've recently received my second box, but the first one has been amazing thus far. The variety has kind of kept me on my toes and they include information so you don't scorch and ruin tea leaves. It's been nice to learn as the first few cups I botched a little due to inexperience. I also live at a very high altitude and need to keep that in mind as it affects the temperatures at which water boils.

As I've figured out how long to heat up my water for each package of tea I've been able to taste and notice a lot more subtleties in each variety. They've all also been refreshing. Something else of note is that the packaging for each tea is pretty good too - I can usually smell sealed items easily but I can't really smell anything when these teas are still sealed.

text:
I've gotten two boxes so far and was really shocked when I looked up the items online. The first month (pictured), I got a full sized conditioner, two decent sized hair products, a hair mask, some other samples and an eyebrow product (a bit light for me so gave to my mom since she is strawberry blonde), plus the cute pink redhead zipper bag.

The second month was even better. There were full sized John Frieda redhead shampoo and conditioner bottles, plus a hair mask, a different type of eyebrow product (this time was perfect for me -- in fact it looks more natural on me than my own brows which are oddly brown), some other samples, and a full sized Aurora sunblock. The JF items were probably valued $25, and I looked up the sunblock and it was $53. I'd guess that the value of both boxes was $100 each so far, so I am really excited to find out what is coming in the next box. I have told a few of my friends who are either redheads or blondes with sensitive skin. I'm really glad I decided to get this box over a k beauty one I'd been checking out... That box seemed fun but I was worried most products may not suit my sensitive skin so I love that every time I know these products will be safe even if they aren't always a perfect color match.

title: Box full of junk
text:
I had high hopes for this crate, but what I received was: 1) a broken coffee mug (made in China); 2) a very cheap (and cheap-looking) brass necklace that maybe would be appropriate for a 10 year old; 3) a "toy" that appears to be made out of hard plastic (not rubber); 4) 3 scented products that I won't use because I don't like making my dog sit in cloying perfumed air; 5) two small bags of dog treat (which seem fine, but the retail price on the website is lower than the price listed as retail on the card provided in the crate); and a rope toy heart that was okay, but looked more like an oval after one tug game. I kept the treats, but everything else went into the garbage.

I was really disappointed. I subscribe to other crates, and while I wasn't expecting to be bowled over, I was also not expecting to have to throw away 90% of what I received. Also, I ordered a crate for a big dog, and the only thing I kept were the two bags of training-sized treats, so my dog gets nothing special and I get nothing special. Also, while I appreciate that the idea of the crate is that I am a female who owns a female dog, I thought there would be more creativity than just giving me junk that says "Dog Mom" on it.

For what I paid, I would have loved to have seen some larger treats (appropriate for a 60 pound dog), such as jerky strips or even a larger biscuit. Maybe a Valentine's themed collar and leash set or dog socks. I would have been thrilled with that.

The room spray was just a personal thing for me, so I am not going to fault that, but two cheap car fresheners (reminiscent of the cardboard trees) cheapened the crate. I would rather you not throw in "fillers" rather than think I will prefer quantity over quality.

title: I have cancelled after receiving my second box - updated review
text:
I have just received my first box and was prepared to be somewhat disappointed after reading quite a few reviews...
The delivery took a long time and I was super excited to finally receive my first bag of goodies.
The bag itself is super cute but not of fantastic quality, the zipper is pretty flimsy.
I received 4 full sized products (the product description on amazon said 4-5 products per month) but unlike advertised only 3 of them were lip products - the accompanying card said the company decided to switch things up with a “Monthly Mixup” - not sure I’m super thrilled about that.
The first thing I noticed is that there was no description given for the products I received or the manufacturers of those products.
I actually had to google the items to determine which one wasn’t the lip item! Since I subscribed to try out new products and companies I’m unfamiliar with I’d very much appreciate some pointers along with the products!
Now to the products themselves:
1. cougar lipgloss in cocoa - the website promises 24hrs of matte lips in “the perfect nude brown” - not a color I’d have picked but I think I’ll be able to use it on occasion
2. Cargo gel lipstick in Sicily - a bright, bold red. It’s a pretty color but certainly not fit for everyday use for me. Again not a color I’d have bought for myself.
3. Appeal gel liner in deep taupe - it’s a dark brown rather than what I’d expect from a taupe and as a lipliner it will be useless to me. The company’s website claims it can be used both as lip liner or eye liner so I’ll try it as an eyeliner and might actually get some use out of it. The color works with neither the lipstick nor lipgloss. It would have been really nice had they been coordinated!
4. Bellapierre shimmer roll in a deep bronze color - google let me know that this is the non lip product and that it is a roll on highlighter. I do not use highlighter and even if i did I don’t think this would be the color for me... I might try it a shimmer layer over eyeshadow or lipstick and see whether that works.

I’ll try another month or two to get a better idea of whether this just wasn’t the box for me or whether none of the boxes are for me before I’ll decide whether or not to continue this subscription.
I expected to not only get colors or products I’d have bought for myself - that’s part of the fun with a non personalized subscription like this.
But if the selection is so far out of the neutral, should fit most types and styles spectrum every month then I’ll not keep collecting a growing stack of useless products.

Update with November box:
Again 4, not 5 products:
1) peony lip scrub - it’s a very small tube but on the company’s website that’s the actual size offered
2) lipmonthly liquid lipstick - I think, the packaging only states it’s 02 of whatever it is, looks like a nude enough color to maybe work for me
3) lord&berry lip crayon in a statement color I couldn’t find on their website - what I could find there however is, that the crayon apparently requires a particular sharpener that can be bought on their website
4) a single eyeshadow in a very adventurous color.
I could have forgiven this, after all I don’t expect colors handpicked for me BUT it is a single eyeshadow that’s meant to be clicked into a palette and is going to be awkward to use on its own since it literally has no edges to nicely hold on to and the lid slides off since it’s not meant to stay on once it’s been put into the palette.

So essentially 2 out of the 4 products received would require additional expenditure to be used as intended by the manufacturers.

I’ve decided to not wait for a 3rd box and have cancelled my subscription.

text: I’d like to suggest that amazon stem club take in to account that a lot of girls do not enjoy toys that are geared towards boys. I have gotten five months of stem club. We have received the magic school bus engineering lab, which was great. Science experiments are for everyone. Then we received the learning resources code & go mouse. Also great, though we had trouble with the mouse going right when we told it to go straight. I have an email in to the company and I understand that it has been a common problem with this mouse. Next we received robotis play 600 pets kit, which is also fine as all kids like pets. Next was the gears gears gears set which was a disaster, but I was unable to return it because the very short 30 day window had passed by the time I opened it and let my girls try it out. It is very frustrating and does not work well. But, it is acceptable for either gender. At this time it seemed that amazon ran out of ideas that would work for both boys and girls so the next item I was set to receive was a Cars 3 Lightening McQueen model kit. Now that item is clearly intended for little boys. While I’m sure there is a little girl out there who’s parent will insist she loves this type of thing, the average little girl does not say hey, I want a model car for my birthday. My girls have less than zero interest in building a model car from the movie Cars, which they also have no interest in watching. And finally, we are set to receive the Zoob builderz 250 piece kit. This box has a very boyish boy on the picture and includes instructions for building both a tricked out boys bike and a dinosaur. Again, leans very much toward the male interest. Amazon needs to get on the ball and stop sending out so many toys that are clearly of more interest to little boys, or change the name to the amazon boys stem club.

title: Cancer, Cardiovascular Disease and Increased Mortality correlated with Processed Meat Consumption
text:
"A higher intake of red meat was associated with a significantly elevated risk of total, CVD, and cancer mortality, and this association was observed for unprocessed and processed red meat, with a relatively greater risk for processed red meat. Substitution of fish, poultry, nuts, legumes, low-fat dairy products, and whole grains for red meat was associated with a significantly lower risk of mortality."

"Red meat is a major food source of protein and fat, and its potential associations with risks of diabetes mellitus, CVD, cancer, and mortality have attracted much attention. Several studies have suggested that vegetarians have greater longevity compared with nonvegetarians, but this might not be ascribed to the absence of red meat only. Sinha et al showed in the National Institutes of Health–AARP (formerly known as the American Association of Retired Persons) study that higher intakes of red and processed meats were associated with an elevated risk of mortality."

Citation: Sinha R, Cross AJ, Graubard BI, et al: Meat intake and mortality: a prospective study of over half a million people. Arch Intern Med 2009;169:562-571.

text: I was disappointed with the junior box.  I may try again when he's old enough for the regular box.  Junior box didn't really seem to be well through through. The theme was 'on the farm' but there were no seeds, nothing about life cycles (should we tell kids where meat comes from--nothing here to guide that conversation).  There were 1) stickers to put on a picture of a barn; 2) a red gift box that they called a barn and suggested you save some stickers for it too; 3) noses to glue to Popsicle sticks; 4) pieces of felt to practice lacing together and 5) felt carrots with holes and tops with numbers to match the number of holes to the Arabic numeral.  There was also a bonus wooden frame that a kid could paint (the nicest part of the box).  Finally, there was an insidious sticker chart, with a 'badge' to encourage the parent to not cancel the box.  The included guide just suggested questions like why are farms important?  It didn't seem to me there was any science in it, ad the quality felt disappointing.  I think it is hard to do a box like this for pre-schoolers; it looks like the grade school box is of higher quality, so maybe we'll try that.

title: Rapidly declining quality
text:
January 2020's box was great. Then, like the rest of the year, Therabox dove downhill and shows no signs of getting better. The products are getting more and more dubious; the first warning sign was a cheap, ugly shower cap from Sugar Bear as well as Sugar Bear """vitamins.""" Uncomfortable socks. July's box, the one that made me quit, had a cheap, round blanket that could be charitably described as canvasy and fairly useless for humans. A card of tiny earrings felt more fitting for a very young kid. There was also a travel journal thrown in; the curator defends this tonedeaf choice in her letter, though doesn't give an excuse for why it feels like a dollar store journal. Nor why anyone thought a book with twee picture checklists would replace travel apps in this day and age.

In fairness, I did find some great skincare items in Therabox among the playing cards with cringey ice breakers and hair scrubs. There's also a nice, unconventional perfume that is now in my rotation. If you love masks, you'll probably find some new favorites in the box. The candles tended to be decent.

Finally, be aware if you have certain health issues, you won't be able to use some of the products. A foot peel from a previous box warned against using the product if you had a number of conditions, for example.

title: Best tea I’ve ever had! So fresh.
text:
Tea is for the most part the only thing I drink, so my cubbard is packed with brand named teas like Lipton, Twinings, Stash, Bigelow, Tiesta, and tons more and none of them I feel come close to the quality, taste and pureness of Simple Loose Leaf. This is by far the best tea I’ve had before, it’s so fresh and packs so much taste per cup it’s unreal.

The first sampler pack was absolutely delicious and opened my eyes to a few teas I haven’t heard of before, the Genmaicha, which was so unique and refreshing, and the Blue Lady. Their version of the blue lady is my favorite tea I have ever had, period. I bought another lavender earl grey tea at my grocery store since and it was so bitter and harsh comparatively, no comparison.

After my first month that was only $3, I was hooked! I searched up their website and found they offer green, herbal and black tea boxes as well for sale, same as here, $11.99 after shipping. They had a deal, 50% any box subscription so I got green and black for only $6 a piece.
After receiving I was thrilled to received 8 teas that I have never heard of before in my life. I’ve only tried 3 so far, but all have been winners, especially the cranberry orange herbal. I typically HATE herbal but this was incredible and was packed with dried cranberries.

For $11.99, you’re not getting a lot of tea I’m going to be honest, but what you are getting is a nice assortment of high quality tea that you most likely have not heard of before. This is perfect for people like me who is simply bored of the 3-4 choices grocery store shelves provide, and want teas from Africa, India, China, Indonesia and other countries around the world!

I attached a picture of all the teas I’ve received so far, left 4=sampler, middle 4=black box, right 4=green box.

title: 13 Month Subscription - Pros and Meh’s
text:
I subscribed to Gainzbox for 13 months, which was more than enough time to formulate an opinion of the subscription service. I ultimately decided to cancel the subscription.

Like any kind of a grab bag of stuff where you don’t know what you’re gonna get, there’s some good and meh stuff in there. For the clothing you do receive, it does actually fit and the Gainz team seem to adjust for sizing differences in items. I wear a medium. If the shirt fits tight like a small, they’ll send me a large, which I appreciate. This happens behind the scenes and you may not even notice it. The box contains some great stuff beyond just product samples, like full size bottles of recovery drinks and premium products like back packs, running bags, jump ropes and dope CBD lotion. There’s also a fair share of some meh stuff that tends to get repetitive, like lifting straps, tape and while I like getting tshirts, it’s like shirt tastic, like, I dunno, think of something else like sweat head bands or something.

The box often has a theme from a collaboration with a fitness or CrossFit person where boxes are tailored to that persons taste. These boxes are way more fun, with items I’ll actually use, and the picture books included, up the premium just a bit more. The box used to include coupon codes but sometimes the links didn’t work or the codes were invalid. Good luck getting a response from them aka don’t hold your breath.

So why did I cancel? I got tired of not hearing back from the company. This can be an area of improvement. They could outsource their customer questions to a call center which at least shows some kind of a presence or interest in talking to their subscribers and trying to help them. I’m spoiled with Amazon with their exceptional customer service and expect more of an effort from companies to which I subscribe. The box used to also gift a free special item every 3 boxes. This bonus seems to have been silently stopped as after the 6th box and getting 2 bonus items, I never got another bonus item again and never heard from Gainzbox either about my inquiry. While I didn’t subscribe for the bonus item, it stopping without any mention nor effort from the team to respond to my questions, and it is frustrating. Gainzbox needs to improve their customer service by well, offering it. Be honest and transparent when services and offerings change. It’s perceived as super shady when you don’t.

Each box typically includes some kind of a premium item. Premium items don’t have to just be items at all! Why not include a golden ticket in randomly selected boxes which offers a select 3 a meet and greet, training session and picture opportunity with some athlete? A workout with Jason Khalipa would be so cool! People will make arrangements on their own if they want it enough. Or, they can donate the experience.

If you’re still reading this, wow! lol So, why should you consider subscribing? If you like grab bag surprise items and goods, have a love for tshirts, product samples and appreciate collaborations with potentially some of your favorite athletes, it’s so worth it.

My box's value comes to $56.95.  They are kind enough to include a card listing each item and that items retail value.  I now have a cat head shaped bath mat ($17.99), cat light charging cord ($13.99), 3 pairs of cat paw socks ($14.99), and two catnip toys each valued at ($4.99).  The socks seem better suited for fall vs. summer, the rug is white and will probably end up a cat bed or in one, the charger has purple plastic cat faces all over it and looks more like those lights you hang up around your patio/porch in summer.  In truth, I have paid $25 for a differently themed subscription box and received items with a total value over $200.  So I guess I just expected better from a $35 box.  It would make a cute gift but I will not be looking to keep this as a month to month subscription.

title: Not worth the money, great customer service
text:
My first complaint is that when I ordered this, it was supposed to arrive BEFORE Christmas. It arrived a few days after making it kinda crappy because I wanted my dog to have his own box to open; something that both of us could be surprised by. That didn't happen.

My dog it a schnauzer, but he's only about 27 pounds. Per the listing, I bought him a box for medium dogs. I received 2 bags of dog treats and 2 toys. One toy, the Nutcracker, was very cute and is made to put treats into, however it's not durable at all. My dog ripped the stuffing out of the head before he was able to get a treat out! He's not a big chewer. He'll chew on something for a short time unless it's something like a dog bone or so. The second toy was the Walnut and while it was cute, it was far too big for him. It's a bit bigger than a grapefruit, slightly smaller than a honey dew melon. He won't even go after it if I throw it and when he does play with it, he get discouraged because of it's size.

There are coupons in the box for a free first box which I'm not sure applies since technically I have already gotten my first box so... I find that a bit odd to include. I contacted customer service and they were willing to resolve the issue, they asked what my dog preferred and I gave them some insight. I mentioned that softer toys were better but more durable ones worked best since he likes to rip the stuffing out of things. They sent two more toys and a dog jerky chew. The chew was a bit hard but he likes it. The first replacement toy was the cute apple slices (1 pair). I thought they were going to be durable since the fabric was similar to what they made backpacks out of but in less than a day, one of them was destroyed. The second toy was a soft toy too which I haven't bothered to give to him because I know it'll get destroyed instantly.

The treats he liked, I could have made a better Christmas box for him for less money and better quality. Even at half price, this wasn't worth getting. I'm only giving it two stars because of the good customer service and the treats.

text:

I was blown away on the first month with the value of the selection AND how much my daughter's loved them. I was expecting the value to drop in subsequent months, but so far it has not. This month's marbulous kit was just as much as a hit with my 6 year old as the others. She has not stopped playing with it for 2 days straight.

This subscription is a great way to get your kids interested in STEM as well as a great way to incentivize and reward them. Bank them for birthdays or holidays or keep a running sticker chore chart with the STEM toy being the monthly reward for hitting the mark.

I can't recommend this subscription enough.

title: Disappointing.
text:
A generous family member got a subscription to Young Chefs’ Club for my son for Christmas. Our first box arrived today and we were so excited to open it up. We have had a Kiwi Box subscription for several months now and the anticipation of opening the box and starting a new project together is great fun.
Sadly, the Young Chefs’ club box is just a pile of folded papers and one small kitchen tool (in this case, a gummy candy mold)). Because there aren’t any foods included in the box, there is very little immediate gratification. Instead, they include a hefty shopping list of ingredients (approximately 32 items!) that you might have on hand but probably don’t (gelatin? Anchovies?). The cost of the shopping list could easily be $50 which, added to the cost of the box itself, would be entirely too much to spend on some kitchen experiments in my opinion. That’s more than entire meal subscriptions that include recipes AND FOOD FOR SEVERAL PEOPLE. There’s no menu box for this pile of recipes we’ve been sent either. Just the cardboard box it was shipped in.

The actual recipes are not so bad. I just would have expected either a much lower price point or sent with actual products that could be used at the time of opening the box.

After receiving 10 boxes, I had to put the subscription on hold because of a lack of space and a long reading backlog.
However, I'm happy with it and I will subscribe again.

PROS
1 All the books are clearly new.
2 Most of them were real page-turners that I really enjoyed reading. That's why I will subscribe again.
3 As expected, are all hardcover editions.

CONS
1 Despite my choice being "surprise me", I've never received a horror novel. Maybe a gothic and in some way haunted one, but horror, no.
2 Some books have a pencil marker dot or line on the side. I hate seeing new books ruined like that.
3 At least three books were spy stories. I really do not like politics, wars, and so on, but this is just me, they cannot know it, and the genre end in the box's subject.

title: January 2019 beauty box CRUSHED IT!
text:
I love absolutely everything about this month's beauty box. I decided after hearing whispers on reddit to subscribe starting this month, and I was so excited that I signed up for two boxes. One through Amazon and one through Allure's beauty box website. The Amazon one has come already and I'm still waiting on the Allure one (hoping for the beauty blender minis variant!)

In this months box: (Pulled from the MySubscriptionAddiction.com spoiler post for $$$ value $$$)
Amika Soulfood Nourishing Mask – Full Size! Retail Value $12 OR Beautyblender Micro.Mini Value $9
Sunday Riley C.E.O. Glow Vitamin C + Turmeric Face Oil – 15 ml
Sunday Riley A+ High Dose Retinoid Serum – 8 ml
Ouai Hair and Body Scrub – 30 ml
Doucce Relentless Matte Lip Crayon in Winterberry – Full Size! Retail Value $22
Mally Eyeshadow Stick in Burnished Bronze – Full Size! Retail Value $25

The Mally Eyeshadow Stick and BONUS NCLA nail polish (in color CALL MY AGENT) were both pleasant surprises. I'd never heard of an eyeshadow stick, but now I need to buy some (Mally Beauty actually sells on Amazon, looking at Pink Champagne for my next buy!). It smudges really easily before setting about 50 seconds after putting it on. A little sparkly, blends well smudging with my finger, and a surprisingly flattering color. Usually I'm bad at eyeshadow but this was super easy for a natural, flattering look. Nail polish isn't firetruck red, more like a more pink? Or salmon hued red which is flattering on my fair complexion.

The clear standout of this beauty box aside from the pleasant surprises liking the eyeshadow stick and NCLA polish: a full size Sunday Riley CEO Glow Vitamin C serum. I've heard the praises heaped upon this product, and I am here for it. I need to get my skin in shape for my wedding in 8 months lol. Currently using Natrogix's vitamin C serum and liking it (softer, smoother skin so far), but interested to see how different luxury skincare compares to affordable skincare.

The few complaints I would have is that the bag came with a tear down the side (not bothered, gave it to my son to put his powder brush in). And the Ouai Hair and Body scrub looked kind of like it had either been tampered with (if there was supposed to be a seal--it was super broken) and it seemed like it was more half-full than full. However, I don't know how they come packaged as I've never used it before, so it could just be like some products come with some air in it in order to keep the product good & etc right? So, not entirely sure.

In short: This is an extremely affordable way to try out new makeup, skincare, hair products and nail polishes. $10/first month and $15/after is manageable for the sizes and brands of products received. Happy with my purchase and debating a third purchase. I looked ahead at the spoilers for next month and while they're not as exciting as SUNDAY RILEY! The mascara is supposed to be really good and worth the price of the subscription alone, so I'm happy to remain subscribed and gift what I don't think I'll use (but maybe switch to just one box :)).

text:
