It really is a good value for the price. The Natural Pumpkin Spice Soap is not too strongly scented and lathers well. It did not irritate the skin but left it soft. It fit perfectly into the sisal Soap Exfoliating Saver bag. It is firm enough to exfoliate nicely without scratching. I even used it on my face. The organic Bamboo Cotton Swabs are nicely cushioned, but I feel bad about throwing away these bamboo sticks so quickly. I will have to think about this before using more. The Multipurpose Tote Bag is all cotton and very roomy. The tight stitching held up to my veggies. It is machine washable and soft to carry. The Wooden Lint Remover is very useful since I have two cats and fur and lint and it never ends, but this helped a lot on my black sweater before I came to work this morning. My last item was a 20 oz. Silicone Lunch Bag. I love silicone bags, but this one fell short on the seal. I filled it partially with water and sealed it and shook and the seal opened. I would only use this item for dry items that don't need a tight seal.
Overall I love my monthly boxes. I get a treat for myself that is sustainable and I can try new things without a huge commitment. They pack a nice Thank You with a code to scan and get more info on the products. Thank you Kate and Nataly, I can't wait for the November Box!

title: Very Pleased
text:
The Vinyl-Of-The-Month Club (which should be called a RECORD-of-the-month, but I'm old so what do I know) has been working out very well so far.
I am an older guy with a largish record collection that enjoys filling holes in my collection. I have a steady lady who has been building her own collection from scratch for the past few years. Between us, there has not been a single mailing from the Club that we did not appreciate.
We joined last summer. Our first record was Pink Floyd's DSOTM (the stellar 2016 remaster). Since then we have received records by The Clash, The Who, The Supremes and others. Most of them have been double albums. All of them have been extremely good pressings. Many of them have been cheaper at the club price than if I had simply ordered them from Amazon individually. Every one has been an essential album for a well-rounded collection.
So far, the only hiccup has been that we never saw the January 2022 album. For us, that would have been Let It Be by The Beatles. On one hand, I understand why it probably isn't available - The Beatles are currently thin in North America due to recent manufacturing changes. On the other hand, I don't know why they wouldn't have skipped along to the next record or substituted something else. It hasn't been devastating; Amazon doesn't charge for them until they ship so we aren't out any money. But we have already gotten to looking forward to the monthly record.
In any case, barring that anomaly, this club has been a great experience so far. Anyone who has been collecting rock albums for a long time may already have most of what is on offer here. But if you are building, or rebuilding, a collection then this is a very good way to put together many of the essentials.
Update : Shortly after posting this review, that Beatles/Let It Be record held over from January showed up. It was properly packaged for shipping and on great shape. I have reviewed Let It Be on that product page. Still very happy with the service.

title: Uninspired crafts. Poor value.
text: For what you get, the Adults & Crafts subscription is not great. Basically, an 8-1/2 x 11 print-out of some things you can do with the contents included. If you remember Martha Stewart craft kits, this doesn't even come close in quality, ideas, or inspiration. For instance, one kit was "engraving" and came with a sheet of ugly clip art to trace onto items like a cheap stainless steel water bottle (the kind you can get for $1 almost anywhere, a metal chain and a glass coaster. Nothing you would be proud to display or give as a gift. MAYBE for kids, this kit would be okay, but I was expecting something more sophisticated as it is marketed to adults. You also do not get a reusable storage box or any way to keep the kit items together for future access. The card kit was similarly disappointing. The 8-1/2 x 11 project sheets aren't even nicely designed for saving in 3-ring binder. For the price, I truly expected higher quality in projects and materials. Also, with the subscription, you do not get an opportunity to know what is coming and skip months you don't want. I would recommend just buying a kit you're interested in vs. the subscription.

title: Overall a great experience, but some flaws.
text:
I got the Halloween box for 2020. Spoilers ahead if you have already received it!

The idea is, you get all these cards with a hotel room number on one side and you lay them down. Then you get some riddles that are supposed to direct you towards a certain room number to advance - most rooms are just empty, but the riddle will direct you to the five you need. The problem is, the riddles suck! One of them, the picture of the room had a grandfather clock next to it. The riddle mentioned a father and described him as having "A palatial paternal instinct". Palatial means "like a palace". Grand could be considered a synonym, but it's really just not the same thing. So you were supposed to put palatial paternal together to mean grandfather.... but no one would do that, because it's really not what the word means. Another riddle had you pull out a cocktail napkin that was included in the box (after the warning to not look at anything in the box until you're specifically referred to it) but then the cocktail napkin ends up not even being part of the solution anyways. Part of that same riddle involved counting the windows with lights out that are on the box. However, the box is mis-printed! One of the sides is a duplicate that will crash your solution to the puzzle.

All that being said, we had a blast. Every time you solve a riddle they give you a neat little game to play (Go find 3 pieces of clothing for your partner to wear, go make a hat using 4 ingredients from the kitchen and your partner has to wear it all night, etc.)

title: Mostly good albums, Poor Functionality
text:
I've had this membership for almost a year now, and I've gotten some really good albums for less than buying them individually, so that's great. It's fun to see what album they're sending... they've almost all been good so far.

Unfortunately, there's a big problem with the functionality of this membership. I signed up on the 18th of the month, so I have to look at my orders on the 18th of every month to see what's going to ship, in case I want to skip it. This month, nothing showed up. On the 19th, Dark Side of the Moon appeared in my order list... which is an awesome record, but I already own it, so I opted to skip it. Despite the fact that it hadn't shipped, Amazon said it was too late, and they shipped it to me the next day anyway. Now I have to keep the duplicate or deal with a return. Annoying. They really should have a period of several days, not several hours, for users to choose whether they want something shipped. This has happened to me a couple of times, now.

And in general, it would be really helpful if Amazon had a place to list preferences (bands, styles, albums, etc), or at the very least list the albums that we already own so that we don't get duplicates. I'd be really annoyed if I had to pay $25 for a Fleetwood Mac album that I could get for $3 on the used market.

title: It's A Mixed Bag, But Still Fun
text:
First of all, these shirts are all of good quality. They're soft, well-made and comfortable. After being washed a few times, the decals are still completely intact with no fading or peeling. No complaints there.

As far as the designs go, it's a really mixed bag. I've received seven of them so far. Some I love, and some I hate. Here's how I would rate them in the order in which they arrived:

Shirt #1: Painted Beholder - Rating: 5/5
This is my favorite of the bunch so far. The image is of very high quality, mostly red, green and white on a black shirt. The beholder looks fearsome and awesome, and it seems to be about to do battle with an elven adventurer. Absolutely love it.

Shirt #2: Dagger and Dice - Rating: 2/5
I wasn't very impressed with this one. The colors are bright to the point of being garish. The design itself is a bit shoddy and looks more like a rub-on tattoo from a gumball machine than something professional. I don't much care for white shirts, maybe it would have looked better on black?

Shirt #3: Drizzt Do'Urden - Rating: 4/5
This one's pretty cool. It features Drizzt in a stoic pose, with the outlines of Guenhwyvar, Icingdeath and Twinkle around him. The colors are fairly simplistic, mostly purple, black, orange and yellow. It's on a navy background, which compliments it well. Very nice overall.

Shirt #4: Choose Your Monster - Rating: 3/5
This one is a bit silly, but it's cute. It features classic Dungeons and Dragons monsters set up in a grid to resemble the start screen of a video game. The monsters featured are an Owlbear, a Lich, a Beholder, a Mind Flayer, a Red Dragon, a Displacer Beast, a Mimic, a Tarrasque and a Gelatinous Cube. The shirt itself is a nice asphalt gray. The only reason I didn't rate it higher was because it looks a little too busy, it might have been better if the size of the decal was a little smaller. I do like it though.

Shirt #5: Never Split The Party - Rating: 1/5
I HATE this one. It's sloppy, ugly and poorly designed. It features a faded map, the outline of some of RPG dice, and the slogan "never split the party". It feels like someone just slapped some ideas together with no concern about how they'd look when combined. The decal looks a bit fuzzy, as though it were enlarged from an image with poor resolution. It's also on a white shirt, which as I mentioned earlier, I don't really care for. This is the only one so far that I've returned for a refund. Amusingly enough, Amazon was kind enough to say that they'd give me the refund without my even having to send the shirt back. I guess they don't want it either.

Shirt #6: Acererak Card - Rating: 5/5
This shirt is so cool! Devoted Dungeons and Dragons players know exactly who Acererak is. Anyone who has faced the notorious demilich in his Tomb of Horrors would probably love to have this fun shirt to remember that classic adventure. It's a black, white and red design on a black shirt. Acererak is even rolling a pair of d20s as though he wants to join in the roleplaying fun. I love this one, it's among of the nicest of the bunch so far.

Shirt #7: Know Your Monster - Rating: 4/5
Another awesome shirt! The color of this one is a nice silver, which is far preferable to the white ones. It features five iconic monsters; Remorhaz, Beholder, Owlbear, Gnoll and Red Dragon. There's a snippet of detail about each monster and a black and white image of them that resembles a sketch an adventurer might jot down in their journal. There's a bit of color behind each monster to add some extra flair. It's a very nice design.

Overall, I am happy with the T-Shirt subscription. It's fun surprise to see what shirts are going to arrive each month. Amazon has been fair about returns/refund for the one I didn't like. It's not a bad deal that way - get a new shirt each month, keep the ones you like and return the ones you don't. :)

I look forward to my shirt every month, and I do recommend this subscription for Dungeons & Dragons fans.

I washed and wore my first shirt several time too and the shirt is holding true to the size I received, the design retained it’s quality, and the shirt retained it’s color.  I thought the shirts were always going to be a darkish neutral color and today’s design was PINK!!!  What joyous bliss!  I’m get tired of wearing always dark colors.  Though Hello Kitty is my main love in the Sanrio world by far , I also love Cinnamaroll who is also on the newest tee. Yheaaa!  Now with this club I will get to learn all her other friends. title: Good Mask Selection, Good Price
text:
I have the 4-pack monthly subscription. It's the perfect amount for me. I look forward to it arriving in the mail every month in its cute envelope. There's always something interesting and different to discover. My skin has never looked better!

They include a card in each pack that explains what each mask does, along with some tips. This is very helpful because sometimes the mask packaging is not in English. I usually get a couple of extra uses out of the leftover mask goo...err...serum.

It doesn't arrive in a box. It arrives in a cute printed plastic envelop and is delivered with your regular mail. I think you have to subscribe to one of the higher levels to get the box. I don't mind the delivery method and none of my masks have arrived damaged.

At $8.90, it comes out to around $2.22 per mask. Masks in my local area are typically around $2.50 and they can be up to $5 per mask depending on the brand and the store. These are equal in quality and sometimes better than what I can find. So this is a very good value for me.

But the real savings comes from the way it stops me from buying random (sometimes expensive!) masks from whatever store I happen to be in. This is much easier on my budget and I love looking forward to each month's mask surprises.

I've had this subscription for about 6 months and I'm very happy so far. I expect to remain subscribed for a while.

Photos:
This is just what I have leftover lying around. Each delivery comes with 4 masks. I'm saving the gold one for something special. You can see the Tea Tree one is the FaceStory brand. It's a 2 step mask with an extra serum packet at the top. I've included some photos of the bag. It's some kind of foil-lined plastic. It holds everything nicely. I store my masks in it to keep them organized.

title: Love this sub
text:
I love sub boxes... I've been doing boxycharm for a very long time, and cancelled recently due to makeup overload.

I was subbed to Allure along with BeautyFix, Sephora Play, etc. I now only sub if I like a box... if you want to know what is coming in a box, check out mysubscriptionaddiction [dot] com.

Considering I'm not a huge fan of masks (okay I use it like once a year!), I decided to wait until Dec-2018 to sub. I looooove Ofra highlighters, and have been dying to try Juvia's place. I've heard so many wonderful things about their palettes. The warrior palette is a lovely warm-nude palette that I otherwise would not have purchased since I have plenty of those shades in my collection. It's very travel friendly, so I highly recommend not depotting (I regret doing that to mine!).

I'm not sure if I'll stick with Allure or not at this point, as I'm pretty up their on frugality. I usually do cheap The Ordinary "dupes" to their skincare items from Sunday Riley. So we'll see.

I did love Sephora Play... I found more favorites from there as they tend to send out classic type of items that most makeup aficionados already own, like benefit lip tint, hoola bronzer, Porefessional primer, etc(and somehow tons of red lipsticks... which I can't decide is better than the brown liquid lipsticks that Boxycharm would send). I have been out of the sub game when Allure was killing it this fall. I was erroneously subbed to Boxycharm which was putting out boxes like the one with the Laura Lee Party Animal palette (super cringe). I think that Allure is the best "budget" sub box. I recommend checking what is in what sub box, and only subbing to the box you want in that month. I no longer sub to a box unless I love 80% of the items and need at least 1. Take it from someone sub box savvy, the companies do "spoilers" of what's coming up.

I also highly recommend subbing on Amazon. I've missed all my boxes from Feb 2018 to Nov 2018. Every time I call customer service they say my account is active, but I have no charge in my bank and no box. I called for a number of months before I gave up and said good riddance. Boxycharm offered the Holy Grail palette from Violet Voss for December, which I already own, so I had to find another box. I'm glad Allure was offered on Amazon, as I love the December box... OFRA!!!! Haha.

title: ABSOLUTELY WORTH EVERY PENNY!
text:
WHEN WE ADOPTED A 10 WEEK-OLD BLUE MERLE POMERANIAN (WHO WAS A LITTLE OVER 2 LBS AT THE TIME), I COULDN'T RESIST THE HYPE OF GETTING A MONTHLY PACKAGE IN THE MAIL WITH NEW TOYS (TOYS!!!) AND TREATS TO TRY (TREATS!!!). I PREPAID FOR THE 6 MONTH SUBSCRIPTION AND WAS PLEASANTLY SURPRISED BY THE QUALITY OF ITEMS, THE WELL CRAFTED HUMOR INFUSED TOYS AND TAGS WITH AN ASSORTMENT OF FEATURES SUCH AS SQUISHY, CRUNCHY, SQUEAKY, ETC).

I WAS NEVER DISAPPOINTED AND REMINGTON LOVED DELIVERY DAY. WHEN MY SITUATION IN LIFE CHANGED, HE WAS REHOMED TO A WONDERFUL NEW "POM MOM" AND JOINED AN OLDER BROTHER WHO SOON TAUGHT HIM WHERE TO PEE AND HOW TO BEG FOR TREATS. HE'S LIVING HIS BEST LIFE EVER!!

IT WAS EASY FOR ME TO SWITCH THE ADDRESS OF DELIVERY TO HIS NEW HOME AND THE PACKAGES WERE AS BIG A HIT THERE AS THEY WERE FOR ME.

I CONTACTED THE COMPANY TODAY WHEN I REALIZED THAT MY CREDIT CARD WAS ABOUT TO BE CHARGED FOR ANOTHER SUBSCRIPTION. I WASN'T SURE IF I WAS ALREADY TOO LATE BUT WAS REASSURED THAT THE CANCELLATION COULD BE COMPLETED AND THERE WOULD BE NO FURTHER CHARGES (OR BOXES).

CUSTOMER SERVICE WAS KIND AND UNDERSTANDING AND ASKED WHY I CANCELLED. I WAS HONEST AND TOLD THE REPRESENTATIVE THAT IT WAS ONLY DUE TO MY BEING TEMPORARILY UNEMPLOYED AND NOT DUE TO ANY DISSATISFACTION WITH ANY BARK BOXES. (I EVEN SENT A PIC OF MY SWEET PUP TO MELT THEIR HEART...). IF I WASN'T DOWN TO MY LAST BIT OF SAVINGS, I WOULD HAVE CONTINUED FOR ANOTHER 6 MONTHS JUST TO PAMPER THE HANDSOME GUY.

IF YOU HAVE THE MEANS TO SUBSCRIBE AND TREAT YOUR BEST FRIEND TO SOME MONTHLY SURPRISES, PLEASE DO SO! I FOUND THAT DURING REMINGTON'S POTTY AND CRATE TRAINING, SOME OF THE TOYS WOULD GET A "WEE" BIT DAMP OR STINKY. EVERYTHING THAT I PUT IN THE WASHER WITH TOWELS CAME OUT FRESH AND CLEAN WITHOUT ANY DAMAGE TO THE FEATURES OF CRINKLE, SQUEAK OR SQUISH. I WAS IMPRESSED.

IF YOU CAN'T HANDLE A 6 MONTH (OR LIFETIME) SUBSCRIPTION, GIVE A MONTH OR TWO A TRY. IT WILL STOCK UP YOUR SUPPLY OF EASY TO FIND TOYS AND YOU WILL BE VOTED MOM/DAD OF THE YEAR. WOOF WOOF!!

title: False advertising
text:
Was sent a box of "American" recipes. First of all, this was supposed to be an international thing, that was the entire point! Recipes were for things like spaghetti bolognese and crab cakes which aren't exactly trying something new. Did I mention this was sold as a vegetarian box and every single recipe was meat-based? The suggested "alternatives" would have changed the flavor of the whole dish and quite frankly sounded disgusting. Palm hearts and vegan mayo as a substitute for crab meat. Sorry, no. This box should have included recipes that were vegetarian by default if you're going to sell it as such.
Lastly, the included spices couldn't have cost more than $2 and were all things I already had in my kitchen (italian seasoning, mini packet of balsamic vinegar, panko bread crumbs). It felt like somebody went to the dollar store and made a box out of the cheapest spices they could find. Maybe some of the other boxes are closer to what was intended, but the one I received was a complete miss.

title: Great Game!  Don't Subscribe Through Amazon!!!!  Read below.
text:
This game is a lot of fun. Our kids love playing detective and really get into it. Each box has high quality materials and the online component is done very well.

DON"T SUBSCRIBE THROUGH AMAZON! Amazon's subscription service is horribly broken. Every time you ship an order to a different address or person through your account, the AMAZON subscription software automatically thinks that this is a new subscription and will start sending you box 1 again. Or a maybe a different previous box. As a result, we spent a lot of time and many emails with Hunt A Killer's customer service having them send us the correct boxes. And now we have three episode 1s, two episode 2s etc...

Do yourself and the poor customer service people a favor and just subscribe through the Hunt A Killer site directly. Amazon knows about their subscription issues but is not able to fix it.

title: PERFECT if you love skincare
text:
I've left my previous review so that you can see how much my perception of the quality has changed since the summer of 2021. The July box was an absolute delight for luxury beauty lovers. In August they stuck in a moisturizer made in China as their main product and then it went downhill from there. Instead of fucusing on luxury skincare, which is what their fan base really wants, September and October had cheapie makeup in it. November's, which I didn't get has an eyelash curler as one of the main products and then some non- waterproof mascara as the two main products. You can get this quality at half the price with other makeup boxes. I don't know if another subscription brand will focus on luxury skincare but that's what I really want. Please see my review below from summer of 2021.

------‐‐----------------

This beauty box, judging by the last two months is really more for people who like skincare. I LOVE it! For makeup, they added a lip stain last month and brushes this month. That's more than enough for me. I love that I can get really high quality products for such a low price and try brands that weren't even on my radar.

This is geared more for discerning beauty conscious people, including those who are more mature. I find myself gleefully surprised by the contents. Allure does a fantastic job of curating the products as well as promoting them. I'm already planning to purchase a couple of the items.

I previously tried Ipsy and hated it. They don't pay any attention to your preferences or what you say about your coloring. The last thing I want is another makeup box of things I don't use.

title: Hit and miss
text:
I'm usually a big fan of Japanese food but this box was a bit disappointing to me. The presentation was great and I appreciated having an assortment to choose from but the majority of the snacks were not for me. The Lemon Vinegar Arare (2 included) tasted stale (not sure if that was the intention but I did not like it all). The setouchi mochi puffs (2 packs included) have a bad aftertaste but the overall taste is passable. I got 2 packs of orange stick cakes which was okay tasting. I really liked the candied iyokan peels, they were like chewy, candied orange peels-I got one pack of those. The yuzu peanut brittle (2 included) was a chewy caramel snack and I did not expect that. It was good, though. My favorite item was the mikan orange mochi. Sadly, there were only two of those so I will have to search for a way to get more.

Overall, I'm glad I got this box when I did. I had been eyeing this for a long time so when Amazon had a sale I decided to go for it. I went ahead and canceled my subscription to this box because maybe my taste buds do not align with the tastes of whoever picks out the snacks. I would recommend anyone try it at least once to form your own opinion. I may try it again at another time, maybe Japanese citrus snacks just aren't my thing.

title: Great option for building a collection.
text:
I had a handful of records and a cheap Wal-Mart player but after purchasing a high end record player I wanted to grow my collection and quickly discovered how expensive new records are. I saw this option through Amazon for the vinyl of the month club and was intrigued by it so I signed up. I figured limiting myself to one record a month for a while wouldn’t be a bad idea.

Some folks are complaining with the random selection each month and would rather choose, I feel that defeats the purpose. If you want to choose then just look up what you want on Amazon and order it. I enjoy the surprise each month of seeing what comes next. So far they have all been amazing selections and encompass a large spectrum of music from the “Golden Era”.

For example I have received CCR, The Supremes, Simon & Garfunkel, Pink Floyd, Miles Davis, Charles Mingus, The Rolling Stones, etc. I think the value is truly there, I get these records for under $30 where in a record store many of these would cost $40-$50.

I haven’t received any notifications when the next album is ready to ship, it will just appear in my orders and the day varies each month. If I don’t catch it and cancel in time like any other order then it ships and I am charged.

My only complaint would be that process, I would like to relieve a notification before the album ships so I can approve or decline with ease, most I will approve anyway but I just feel that process could be a little smoother, as well as the albums becoming available on the same day each month.

Overall though, I feel this is a great way to grow a collection and so far I’ve been very satisfied with the price as well as the selections made by the “experts”.

title: Some hits and Some misses
text:
I have received two shipments of the Blue Sampler Box.

The Genmaicha will make people leave the house it smells so bad. One reviewer thought the white particles were Styrofoam - I don't. I think that some of the rice grains popped while being toasted. The Blood Orange is both funky and viscous - not a hit in my house, either.

The Formosa Oolong is quite enjoyable. I really like that tea...but for some reason you can't find it on their website.

Lastly, except for the cardboard box, all the packaging looks quite different from what is displayed on Amazon - the tea bags are said to be of linen, but they look like a polyester. The teas are all packaged in pretty and colorful little resealable plastic bags.

I don't know how often they duplicate something that has previously been sent with these samplers, and I really do not want to get more Genmaicha or Blood Orange tea. I looked for a way to make some pre-selections for the Blue Box sampler, but did not find one.

I will try a few more of the teas before I decide, but it is likely that I will cancel the Blue Sampler.

This product is overall a good idea, but unevenly implemented for me.

title: Why I eventually cancelled...
text:
Edit 2: My bag finally arrived — I may also be receiving a replacement for it. The November bag is terrible. It includes a bland Doucce Freematic shadow single, a sample sized lip scrub, a pinky Lord & Berry lip crayon... and the fourth product—I cannot stress this enough—is the worst lippie I have received from a beauty sub EVER.

The awful lippie is “Lip Monthly” brand. It’s made in China, which doesn’t automatically mean a product is terrible, but this one is. It’s bubblegum pink. You might like the shade; I tried. There’s no redeeming taste or scent... it’s vaguely unpleasant tasting, but not overwhelmingly so. After one coat, you notice the coverage is terrible. It’s matte, but looks like it needs another coat. So, you’ll kind of let it set and add another. Still not adequate. You wonder if you quickly press your lips together... it’s just so sticky. It kind of gums up into a weird rubbery, boogery paint. It takes a good rubbing with micellar water to remove it — you can skip the lip scrub. This is the first time I have ever just completely thrown a product in the trash and I am a junkie for sub bags/boxes.

Although I am glad that C.S. was willing to replace the stray package, I don’t know why it’s too much to ask for this subscription to ONLY send lip products. And I don’t want their own brand slapped on some 20 cent garbage from China.

Edit 1: so, my most recent bag seems to be a casualty of DHL and its generally rotten shipping. It’s been “out for delivery” for several days in a town that is a few hours away.

I realize that no one can control what happens once a package has shipped (aside from choosing something better than DHL!), but when I contacted the seller about the issue I didn’t receive any kind of resolution.

The fun of these things is lost when you have to go through a bunch of trouble to (maybe) get what you paid for.

~~~~

My first bag had a gloss, lipstick, lip oil, and a liner in it. If I was fond of nudes, I would probably have been more excited, and I can see the appeal of putting complementary shades together. If future bags aren’t more exciting, I don’t see myself paying $12.95/mo.

Would love to see at least one adventurous shade each month — black, green, etc.

title: It breaks my heart to leave this 1 star, but it is what they deserve. Cancelled subscription
text:
As an avid Marvel fan for 40 years, I love everything superhero-related. I jumped into the collector's boxes bandwagon when Amazon started them, and was super stoked when I saw that the first one was going to be Deadpool... but it was *meh*.

I saw that the next one was going to be Venom and I said: I will give it a shot. It was also *meh*. At this point my brain started whispering: "cancel this subscription", but then I saw the next one was going to be MARVEL 10 YEARS, and my heart blocked my brain. "This is going to be EPIC", I thought. Boy how wrong I was...

The person in charge of picking the contents of these boxes has NO IDEA of what the fans want. What a mediocre effort in assembling something so poorly crafted with such a grandiose theme. They could have done so much...

Today, my disappointment is as big as my hopes were for this box. I see that the next one is X-Men (which I also love), but nevertheless... you shall deceive me no more. In the wise words of Gandalf the Grey, I yell to my subscription: "YOU... SHALL NOT PASS".

It surprises me that Amazon (which must be in full damage control mode right now) actually tried to stop me from leaving this review for the past three days. So they know. The question is... will they do something about it?.

The main piece on this "Marvel 10 year celebration box" was the equivalent of a "Star Wars Lifetime Celebration Box" having an oversized Jar Jar Binx pop smiling while giving you the finger. MEESA DON"T LIKE DEES BOXES... ugh!

Until they fix this disaster, stay away from these boxes. All the one star reviews are not jokes. They are truly Charlie Romeo Alpha Papa.

title: small dog box = remnants of big dog box? just a bunch of ends of chews, definitely not giftable
text:
So I'll say first I bought this on promo before Christmas--like $10 for the first mo of a subscription--with the intention of buying it and canceling for a bunch of chews for my little dog (likely corgi/pom mix, 17 lbs) for the holidays.

And he was very happy! He loved the chews. There's about five types, and they're all delicious, apparently--although also quickly digestible: none lasts more than five minutes.

The problems (hoping to help out the seller/manufacturer here, honestly, because from a marketing angle you could do much, much better):

1. Packaging. This was literally a brown box with loose chews. No wrapping, no bow, no not even paper tissue or a guide to the different kinds of chews. This was just a box filled about 1/16 full of pieces of chew. Man, for the money you want, you should really a) make it look aesthetically more appealing; and b) attempt to do some branding. If I was a really uptight dog owner/one that had a dog with genuine allergies, I'd want some sort of info on what the chews are. Granted, this ends up going to a very happy dog, but the purchaser is a human, and would like to know they're paying for more than...

2. [P]ieces look like they are literally the cut-off ends of what I expect to be the grand chews put in the big-dog boxes. Like, everything from 1/2" long to some okay looking longer bits that were just fine. But hey, if you are going to charge $25 a month, you really, really should try harder? I was a little concerned that he might choke because some were so small, but I watched closely, and thank God he was just fine snarfing them down.

Nonetheless, my baby loved it, and for the $10 paid, okay. But for $25 a month? No way. And if it is $10 again and a small dog owner (above teacup Chihuahua sized, I'd say), I'd do the large-dog box, since that HAS to be better than this...

title: Okay Box
text:
I was excited at the prospect of this box, based on the fun bags and items shown in the photos. When my first one arrived, it was just stuffed into a Priority-type mailer envelope. I was half expecting something to be broken. Putting that aside, I opened it and was a bit disappointed; instead of a super cute little makeup bag, it was in a cheap looking little bag that had ‘sassiest’ on it. I loved the unicorn snot gloss’ feel but I wouldn’t realistically wear green glitter gloss. There was a lip contour, a matte liquid and another gloss. None in my color preferences, but I know that happens with a surprise box. I decided to give it another try, just in case this bag was a bad representation of their offering; don’t forget, I *had* seen the pictures showing other offerings.

Imagine my surprise when the second month, I get the same exact cheap looking bag. Nothing cutesy or adorable for Christmas nor one for New Year’s. Nothing remarkable inside, with more colors that I will have to struggle to make work for me.

When the third one arrived, and was basically a repeat of the first two, I decided to cancel. I don’t think I got a single color that works for me, by itself, in any of it.

Of course, I didn’t cancel until after the cutoff day, so I got my fourth one in today. STILL the same type of cheap looking bag, this time it contains a tube of chapstick type of product and an beautiful gold eyeshadow, in addition to a gloss and matte liquid. I like the eye shadow already, but a chapstick-esque product?!? I can get that at the dollar store, folks! I haven’t opened the other products to check their colors yet, but I’m not eager to any more.

If any of my bags had been adorable and any of the lipsticks really usable for me, it would have been worth it. 🙁 As it stands, even my daughter, whose skin coloring and tone work with almost ever color out there, doesn’t even think many would work for her!

I wanted to love this subscription box but I just can’t.

text:

The black eye liner doesn’t seem like anything special and doesn’t want to actually leave a line on my skin! What good is an eye liner that doesn’t line? I will try it again to see if it does better. Also, it requires a sharpener, which I have for other pencils. I haven’t tried the hair mask and will update this review after using it. The blemish stickers are the last thing I need at my age and the last thing I will pass on, risking embarrassing someone over their blemishes.

Bottom line: I wish I could customize the box at least a little. Age, skin tone and type, hair color or just preferred color pallets would be great. title: So worth it!
text:
I bought this for my 2 year old son. He is somewhat advanced for his age so I wasn't worried about the age group suggestions. I have the subscription sent to his grandparents house so when he visits them every month he has a new and cool surprise. The items that have come so far have been engaging, fun and child approved lol. All of the items we have received so far have also been of great quality and were definitely worth the price of the STEM club. Most of the items are very large, and have plenty of material to keep a preschooler busy for sometime. So far we have a wood math set, a bucket of construction gears, a car building set, a coding caterpillar, a science exploration kit, and a patterned drill set.

I will note that some of the items could potentially be difficult for a young person (2-3) to immediately grasp and may require more in depth adult assistance to navigate, but they're great all the same.

The shipping is also great, at the end of the month (for us) amazon notifies me of shipping and the package always arrives on time or early even.

Pros:
Price
Quality
Variety of toys
Ease of order
Packaging

Possible Cons:
Some toys may have a larger learning curve you really just have to know your child. The great thing with that is that they can learn to love certain toys as they age a little or even play with them with adult assistance.

I would definitely recommend purchasing this club subscription to anyone with little ones.

text:

I'm overall satisfied with the subscription and am going to change it to the 5-7 age range. below are short reviews on each kit we have received.
We got the gears kit and built some of the models. They showed a robot on the bucket however it wasn't in the instruction booklet so we had a blast trying to figure it out as a family. The platforms and gears are sometimes hard to take apart but other then that a good toy, plus it came in a nice hard plastic bucket for storage and additional play.
We received the Automobile Engineer kit and the 4 y/o and his friends love to build the different cars (the book has instructions for at least 4). They either don't want to take it apart or they like to crash it to bits (but that's what boys do). The kit had color coded pieces to indicate different lengths and sizes which is sometimes hard for the kids to differentiate and the instructions aren't written piece by piece. Overall it provides just enough learning with limited adult assistance.
We received the Cod-a-pillar recently and my kids don't play with it. We have limited hard flooring that the kids can play on so it doesn't have room to roam. they both already have remote controlled toys and cars so this is slow and boring waiting for it to turn. Although the most expensive kit so far it's the least enjoyable for our family.
We received the drill and screw peg board thing and it's so much fun for both kids. It comes with interchangeable bits for an electric and hand drill, different color screws and pattern maps. the little one learns dexterity and the use of tools and the older one follows the patterns. They actually play well together on this one and the older one teaches the little one the right pattern. Love this kit! (the drill goes clock wise and counter clock wise to remove screws).
We also received the Math Playbox. It's the most traditional kit since it teaches simple math. the pieces are hard pressed cardboard vice wood (they look like wood on the pic). It requires adult assistance to explain the math principles because it's built like a puzzle and my child just matches the pieces to the holes. It reinforces his numbers and allows him to visualize the math problems. It bores me as an adult but I don't get complaints when I suggest we play with it so I'll take it as a win.

title: Love it But One Big Issue
text: My family has been doing Eat2Explore for over a year now.  We started on Amazon and then switched over to the actual company site.  We have really enjoyed doing it and have liked all of the recipes.  It has been a great experience for our kids.  We love trying all of the new dishes and exploring other cultures through cuisine.  I've paired some of the meals up with our country of study in home school.  We do think it is a bit expensive for what you get.  I noticed a reviewer saying that you get one packet of spices which is not accurate.  You usually get three or four packets (sometimes bottles) of spices, seasonings, sauces, etc.  You also get a small kitchen tool, along with the recipes and shopping lists.  If you sign up through their site, they sometimes offer deals, and we have done the year subscription with a Black Friday discount two years in a row now (currently on our second year).  We have been disappointed this year as we have been receiving duplicate boxes of past meals.  Because of this, we have decided to not do a year subscription next year.  I looked at their site and as of now, they only add 2 new boxes every year.  For the price, we didn't want kits that we have already done.  These kits are in no way a cheap meal (they provide the recipes and harder to find seasonings and you provide pantry staple seasonings and all of the food).  They are for exploring other cultures (and other parts of the U.S. I might add).  We only did it for a few months through Amazon and then a full year and now into our second year, we have already received 3-4 duplicate boxes of past kits.  Each kit has recipes for several meals but we make them all at once and invite other family to join us.  Everyone has loved the meals.  I'm sad to not do it in the future, but there just aren't enough meal kits to sustain keeping the subscription.  Their customer service has been good when we've received broken spice packets, etc.  I recommend this for anyone who wants to make and try new foods.  It's not cheap though, so I would keep that in mind.  Every kit offers vegetarian alternatives with the recipes, which is nice.

Every month in homeschool, we study a different country, and we decided to just make that country the same country that this mystery is about.  It's a fun surprise of which country we will focus on. I recommend this for sure, but just be prepared if you give it to a kid that can read well and is older, then they can do it very quickly on their own.  It isn't really very challenging. However, the pictures in the story book don't look anything like what you can build and my son was so frustrated (and the story itself was not well written). And while the pieces were bright, the kit was hard to put together, the pictures in the instruction book were hard to follow, the colors didn't match the actual pieces and we all got a bit frustrated with pieces that were the same color but some had odd holes on them and others didn't. For a 3 - 4 year old this was way too hard to navigate, and an older child would find the story line juvenile. The next kit we got had a drill, colored screws and a white tray with holes on it. This was somewhat better, as pattern cards were included. Unfortunately, wasn't very interesting. The third kit was a cheaply executed maze game that you put together.

This club doesn't seem to be actually curated. I think it is more likely Amazon getting a premium from some lesser known "toy" vendors to include their products. Very disappointed, canceled after third box.

I have received an assortment of skincare, cosmetics, hair products, masks, false eyelashes, self tanner, etc.

The only negative issue I have is when I receive a product that I can buy at Wal-Mart or Walgreens. I feel like the whole point of this subscription is to find out about new products and brands. I don't want to see stuff that I have been using since I was 16. Maybe that is just me and other people don't mind, but with all the resources and brands at Allure's fingertips surely they can do better than Frizz-Ease as one of five products. title: Best Masks I've Used!
text:
I became a big fan of sheet masks while living in Japan. I usually bought cheap ones, though, and they weren't much more effective than just moisturizer. I also have very sensitive skin and sometimes I'd get a few zits after certain ones.

I have been busy and stressed lately, so I decided to treat myself to something small. I tried FaceTory. I have now used 8 masks and I have loved them all. None have irritated my skin, though a few did start to tingle. There are at least 2 that I felt made such a difference I would buy them again separately. I also like that there is a little explanation of what each one is supposed to do. It's fun to try different masks instead of being locked into basically different scents of the same mask, which is how I feel about sets I've bought on Amazon.

It does come in an envelope, not a box, but I don't see that as an issue. I also haven't had any problem with the size of the masks as some reviews mention. I have a wide, Mexican face and I'm fine with them. Like most sheet masks, I do sometimes cut extra slits around the eye holes so they lay flatter against my face instead of being stretched across.

My 3rd envelop should be arriving soon and I don't see myself unsubscribing any time soon.

I have been using these masks once a week. Combined with the rest of my skincare, my skin has never been better and I haven't felt dry at all this winter.

I like the subscription because you find unexpected hits. I didn't know she would love to make mazes and puzzles and her spacial reasoning was surprising. So far, all of the sets have been a great value too. I don't know if we will continue the subscription next year because she only needs so many toys and even 4 sets a year add up, but I can definitely see resubscribing when she is ready for the 5-7 year old club, and my husband and I anxiously await the big kid club (8-13) sets!

title: Updated post price hike: Great value, so far more skincare than makeup products
text:
I'm 2 months in on this subscription and super pleased. Receiving multiple full size products each month, all of which are products I actually use, is fantastic! Both May and June boxes contained products that were mostly skin care, which is just fine by me.

I am enjoying this box more than I did Birchbox, Ipsy, and the Sephora box. It is $15 instead of $10 but I find the price is acceptable because of the full size products and that each of the products is useful (instead of a throw-away perfume sample like we've all probably received in the other boxes).

-- update 4 months in --
Still absolutely loving this subscription. It is consistently more skin care than makeup and I'm completely good with that. The box always includes at least 1 full size item and I've been enjoying every sample that has come through. So pleased with the value and the breadth of brands - a nice mix of known, trusted mid-high tier brands, drug store brands, and a few new-to-me international brands. Love this subscription!

-- updated post price hike--
Decided to give it a try after the format change (more full sized products) and price hike; received that first box this week and just find that it's not worth it. The box is more make-up heavy, which in my case means a give-away product that I'll never use (matte red lipstick). I also think the vitamin C powder included in the box is such a piece of marketing rubbish, I would be amazed if the company that makes it ever hits sales beyond what the subscription boxes got from them. So heavier on make-up products, with disappointing skincare products. Canceled subscription as this is no longer worth it, no longer recommend.

“London Calling” by The Clash was received last month and I was pleased to see that it was a 180g pressing from the EU that sells on Amazon at about twice the cost of the monthly subscription.

This month it’s “Exile on Main Street” and I’m certainly “Happy!” Sooner or later they’re gonna pick a selection of which I already have a recent pressing but not so far. My copy of “Exile” dates from the 70s and it's time for a replacement.

UPDATE: Since providing this review, I have received and enjoyed several vinyl classics, not already in my collection such as "The Wall," "Are You Experienced?" and "The Who Sell Out." I see that this month's selection coming to me is "Quadrophenia," also by The Who and I see that it will be the soundtrack edition, not the original release of the album, so it's not what I would consider to be the "classic vinyl" edition. Good to have, but just not the same.

title: Great Package of High Quality Tea Leaves with Reusable Tea Bags
text:
I loved this, and they had the perfect first package sampler with Lady Grey, Formosa Oolong, Gen Mai Cha, and Blood Orange tisane.

Although I am an admirer of many teas, I am usually no longer a devotee of Earl Grey/Lady Grey blends. Years ago, I was a huge fan of Earl Grey, but over the years and after taste-testing some truly terrible bergamot-infused teas calling themselves "_____ Grey," I have found that I am no longer as excited about Earl Grey or Lady Grey teas. However, the Lady Grey was charming in this case, with a much more subtle bergamot and lavender that was not overly floral to create a very nice, smooth mouthfeel and flavor.

My favorite from this first box is the Formosa Oolong which I found to be very smooth, with the perfect amount of astringency to make a smooth overall Oolong with a slight muscatel crispness on the back of the tongue. Not my favorite in the world, but certainly an excellent Oolong.

The Gen Mai Cha was very nice, earthy, and warm with that traditional smoked popcorn-type flavor unique to that blend. And the Blood Orange tisane was a nice rounding-out of the four selections with a traditional hibiscus-based fruit tisane with a lovely blood orange flavor.

The only thing I would suggest for the company to improve is to consider that people who are not wholly new to tea are ordering this. Reading the backs of some of the packages felt like they were leaving out more important information such as altitude, estate, or specific tasting notes in favor of information that felt almost patronizing.

I appreciated the disposable tea bags, as I usually purchase those from OzarkMoons.net to brew my looseleaf teas. I'm sure other customers who do not have a lot of tea equipment will appreciate them as well.

Overall, I thought this was a lovely package, and I will be continuing my subscription for this tea sampler! Thank you!

title: Quality over quantity
text:
I would really emphasize that this packages provides delicious high quality teas, but not necessarily a large quantity. Personally, I think the variety plus the quality is worth the price. In the box I received four different teas (all quite delicious and flavorful) and the tea in each packet will provide three first seeps. So, if you seep your tea only once, you will get about twelve cups. But, all the teas I received were good enough to seep at least one more time. So, i got about 24 cups of tea out of the packets received. If you only seep your tea once, you may not feel like you are getting your money's worth and you won't get the full value out of the tea.
Also, to get the good flavor, you will need to follow the instructions and not over seep or use too hot of water. I found that when I set the timer and paid attention to the instructions, the tea was really good. One cup I let it seep too long and it killed the flavor.
I have only received one box so far and it had an Assam tea, floral tea, spicy tea, and chocolate tea. They covered four different flavors, which was a nice variety. My favorite was the Black Tea Melted Chocolate. I also really enjoyed the Organic Assama-zing tea. The Blackened Heart had nice hints of rose, it was very smooth, goes bitter if seeped too long. Mexican Hot chocolate is okay, but very strong. I am ending up with extra cups because I'm using a smaller amount of tea per cup. Also, I'm having to experiment with adding extra sugar or cream to really enjoy it.

Usually subscription boxes are worth the risk even if you get a dud, but this one was beyond disappointing.

text: I'm not at all happy about the first and last set I'll be getting from Surprise Ride. It was a paint your own birdhouse kit that came with a tiny 4" birdhouse. There was also a book that would be good for the younger child, surely not any child over 8. title: Best. Subscription. Ever.
text: My subscription was a gift from my wife, who is obviously the greatest wife ever.  I didn’t know what to expect, but I can’t say enough about these boxes.  Every month has been awesome.  It’s not that grab bag at your local store, the one that has 10 dollar books in it for $5.  The comics included are excellent.  They seriously pay attention to your selections.  Yes, there’s going to be some filler, but even those books are pretty sweet.  My first box was packed with nostalgia, with some nice issues from the 80’s and 90’s interspersed with current issues.  Some first appearances, too.  My second month was packed with #1 issues and all three issues of a three part miniseries.  This month, several key plot issues, and some of the second issues of the titles from last month.  I highly recommend this!

title: Disappointed

title: great quality and variety - perfect gift for tea lovers
text: I subscribe to this monthly tea service and I like a lot of things about it.  I like how the resealable pouches that the teas come in have a clear backing so you can see what the tea actually looks like.  I like the little cloth filters that are included that are easy to clean and reuse.  I was also pleased with the variety of teas included.  Lastly I like that the teas are re-steepable.  I tried dollar tea club and while the tea was tasty, if you tried to re-steep it, there was very little flavor.  I also love that they employ developmentally disabled people, and they buy their shipping boxes and tea filters from American-owned companies.  More reasons to love this tea company.  If you know someone who likes tea, send them this box.  They will not be disappointed.

title: loved this subscription - would absolutely resubscribe

Not sure how much longer we will keep this subscription if this type of quality issues and poor customer service continue.

title: Lacked enough instruction
text:
This would be great for those who are experienced in painting with acrylics. I'm a total newbie so I need a bit more direction. I need to know what brush they are using, I need to learn more about brush strokes, etc.

My paintings came out so bad because I simply do not know what I'm doing with the brush strokes. I'm getting way to many hard lines and I can't visually see exactly how he's doing the brush strokes and half way through the project I was using the wrong brush. Towards the end someone in chat (these are recorded live I suppose) asked what brush number and I had it all wrong. I'm not mad, I got a good laugh at my efforts.

Youtube beginner videos that I've followed in the past gave me such beautiful completed art that I started hanging them up all over my home. These will not make it to the walls, but will keep them hidden away for future giggles.

Once I get these basics mastered I WILL be back! Lol

title: Excellent Toys for Learning STEM Concepts
text:
I was worried about the quality of the toys that my kids would receive when I signed up for STEM club based on some of the reviews, but after two months I have been surprised with activities. The first toy was the [[ASIN:B00HSCQ4ZS Young Scientist Club The Magic School Bus Engineering Lab]]and the second toy was the [[ASIN:B01A5YMCH4 Code & Go Robot Mouse Activity Set, 83 piece]]. Both toys have a few basic directions, but the beauty of the toys is that those concepts have led my girls to think of new experiments and projects. My 7 year old absolutely loves completing the tasks and then showing us how she can incorporate other toys and objects into the task.

Engineering is more than following instructions on a sheet of paper, it is about taking concepts and applying them in new ways to build something new. The toys I have received so far for my girls are the type of toys that are fun for them to play with, but also provides that "spark" that will help them to think of intuitive new ways to build things. I definitely recommend.

I'm not completely satisfied. Product for most recent delivery is much better than last one. Last one wasn't much different than item that was sent prior, in my opinion. I would have preferred more material to do the activity several times (with group of kids/friends). But I don't feel that was Amazon's call, so no biggie. The item was from Spangler Science, which always has great, fun products! My one concern was that the description of the item was labeled on the exterior packaging of the item. title: 8-13 is bad. Others great.
text:
I have had a great experience in the quality of the lower age toys; however, this first month adding 8-13 is extremely disappointing. This "mechanics" set is filled with quizzes and lessons but none of the projects are actually mechanically sound. Beyond that, every project we have tried has had a minimum of 3 errors in the diagram to the point where the instructions actually contradict themselves.

Finally, (and this was the last straw for me) the "catapult" used as an example of a lever was supposed to be used by flipping it with a finger. Catapults use tension (and levers) but even though it would have been idiotically simple to add a rubber band, these "STEM experts" were apparently happier to ignore the concept of tension and just flick the toy across the room. And let's be real: a catapult is a poor example in the first place considering a trebuchet far better illustrates the concept.

Obviously this toy is meant to capitalize on parents who like the idea of STEM toys but have no actual experience in the field of physics or engineering while filling your child's head with incomplete theories and bad science.

Ugh.

But the 3-8 is great :) we'll be keeping those two.

title: The Best Science Subscription I've Had
text: I am a home school science teacher with a MS degree in Chemistry.  I LOVE science and have subscribed to a couple other science programs, such as Spangler Science and Magic School Bus.  I was curious as to what Amazon might include in the STEM subscription, so I took my chances.  Well, this is by far the BEST subscription I've ever had!  The other subscriptions got old after a year, and my kids rarely were interested in the boxes we received; I always cancelled the subscription after a year.  With the Amazon STEM program, we receive really interesting, fun, inspiring kits and toys, many way more valuable than the monthly subscription price!  I am enjoying this subscription so much that I have no intention of stopping it.  I have received items such as a wind generator kit (not one of those tiny ones, but a HUGE one that stands a few feet tall!), physics kits, construction kits, Smart Circuits, a National Geographic Fossil kit, a large dinosaur model kit, and several other really cool things. I'm like a kid at Christmas every month!  I have not received any kits that involve wet chemistry or biology, but many have involved experiments in the physical sciences. If you love all kinds of science and have students or children with whom you are willing to share your "toys" and love of science, this subscription is the one you've been looking for!

title: Fantastic Concept and I Love it!! (Updated 4/29/22)
text:
One of the FAQ's state,
How will I know what album I'll be receiving? "After you subscribe, visit the Returns & Orders page to see which album you'll receive this month. If you aren't interested in the album on its way, go to the Manage Your Subscriptions page and click 'skip this box' to skip the month's album".

With the first two albums I received, my first notification was when the Amazon truck dropped them off at my house. With my third album, my first notification was via an email when Amazon thanked me for my recent order. I logged in to see what I ordered, since I didn't remember ordering anything.

All three of the albums I received are albums I would never purchase,
1. The Clash - London Calling, not something I would enjoy and I returned it.
2. Van Valen - Van Halen, which was actually pretty good and I remember purchasing it went it was released. I may end up keeping this album.
3. Rolling Stones - Exile On Main Street, which is rated #1 or #2 most popular album of the Rolling Stones, depending on which website you use. Not a big fan of this album and I will be returning it.

I would much rather had received the Rolling Stones, Sticky Fingers, album versus Exile on Main Street, since I would listen to it repeatedly and never returned it.

Wild Horses, Brown Sugar, Can't You Hear Me Knocking are some of my favorite songs of all time. I can listen to these songs over and over.

Do not get me wrong, the three albums I received are outstanding albums of the 70's and 80's, but they are not the type of music I enjoy. I would play them once and never play them again, so I will return them.

As I said, the concept is an outstanding and a fantastic idea, especially, since was I was lead to believe I would be receiving albums by the following artists, according to the Amazon web page, https://www.amazon.com/Vinyl-Month-Club-Golden-Subscription.
1. Mile Davis - I already have most of Miles Davis albums.
2. Led Zeppelin - I love Led Zeppelin
3. Fleetwood Mac - I love the early Fleetwood Mac
4. Aretha Franklin - Songs I grew up listening to and I already have most of her albums.
5. Pink Floyd - The Dark Side of the Moon, Meddle, Animals, Wish You Were Here, The Wall, all fantastic albums !!

I read where some people received Pink Floyd albums, The Dark Side of the Moon or The Wall. I would really enjoy receiving them versus what I already received.

Update - I received The Wall, in March, and I already have The Dark Side of the Moon on a SACD, plus the Immersion Box Set. Every time I play the "multi channel" SACD version of The Dark Side of the Moon, it sounds like Pink Floyd is playing my living room. Each instrument is playing on a separate speaker. Lower the lights, turn up the volume, close your eyes, and enjoy the music!!

I am a big music lover, so the Vinyl of the Month Club is a perfect fit for me. Iron out the kinks and it will be a big success .

Since I have to give STARS but haven't purchased any yet but am considering it on the basis of reviews I've read, my gut thought is 4. W/grandkids <2 to 9.5 yrs, this is how I've used these reviews to decide if this would be a WISE decision for various kids.
1. Purchase some of the toys to determine which TYPES of toys the kids like.
2. Is AGE LEVEL indicated appropriate for YOUR child.
3.Do you want to provide SUPERVISION, be INVOLVED w/your child to the degree needed.
4. Do you want the same type product monthly or change.
5. Is price a better value this way or if purchased as child is ready or if child EARNS it as in when ready for next stage.
These are my recommendations for how to view the reviews of those who HAVE purchased the STEM program. When/if I DO sign any of my Gkids up for it, I'll evaluate it in detail. I hope this won't be rejected because I haven't purchased the program. Knowing HOW to make the decision based on the reviews of others is important. I make this statement as a physician who had spent MANY YEARS reading copious medical journals deciding how patients will best benefit from products w/o being influenced by the hype of advertising but on the basis of what is best for the INDIVIDUAL patient sitting in front of me. I use the same criteria when choosing products for my Gkids.

title: The BEST Tea I've Ever Had
text:
I am NOT exaggerating when I say this is some of the best tea I've ever had. I love tea. One might say I have an obsession. I have about 47 million tea bags stashed around my house. (is THAT an exaggeration? The world may never know...)
Anyway the shipping on this box was FAST - even to Guam! Usually boxes from Amazon arrive via a singular man in a rowboat, 8 weeks after ordering. This box came less than a week later though so they must have flagged down an airplane. And the TEA! oh man. I got the following flavors, and loved all of them:
1) Blood Orange Herbal - a rooibos base with delicious notes of orange and vanilla. Truly a flavor explosion as promised. So delightful and amazing for fall!
2) Genmaicha Green Tea - how delighted I was to find itty bitty pieces of popcorn in my loose tea along with toasted hulled rice kernals! Sounds weird, tastes AMAZING. a nice earthy toasty flavor.
3) Blue Lady Grey - Earl Grey is my favorite type of tea, but this may have changed my mind. It has added lavender and is perfect for a pick me up that is also calming. Which I need in my desk job.
4) Qi Lan Oolong - I literally took one sip of this and audibly exclaimed OH MY GOD THIS IS AMAZING. I wish I could describe it to you here, but there just aren't words. i'll try. It's like angels kissed some oolong tea leaves and then blessed them with kittens and flowers. Seriously. It's earthy but floral, soothing and DELISH.

I highly, highly recommend this box of tea. It's cheap and the tea quality is so good, I don't even know how they're making a profit. Perhaps they aren't. Perhaps they're just doing the greatest act of service the world has ever known.

text: I have been getting the Allure beauty box for years now, and am usually always impressed with what I receive. There always seems to be at least one full size item per box (and often times even more than one) and a bunch of sample and deluxe sized beauty items as well. This box has a good mix of skincare and makeup usually, and compared to the cost of some other subscription boxes out there I’m usually pretty impressed with Allure boxes and they don’t break the bank either. Pictured is my June 2020 box which I loved, the Purlisse cleanser alone was more than worth the cost of the box and I will use all of the items in it. Some months are better than others, and I didn’t give a full five stars because in my years of being a subscriber there have been a few repeat items (though still good products) which can be disappointing from a beauty box. I’ve also found its much better to subscribe through Amazon than through their website, because shipping is much faster via Amazon and you can see which products you’re getting for the month on the homepage for the box. When subscribing through Allure boxes can take anywhere from a couple weeks to over a month to make it to me, and I’ve had boxes get lost with them before so Amazon is definitely the way to go. If you love trying and testing out new beauty products, this is definitely worth trying and you won’t be disappointed.

title: Awesome indie brand makeup box, known for bright colors!

If you don’t like bright colors and trying new products that are often a bit daring, then this box is NOT for you. However I am 30 years old and I absolutely love the glitters and bright colors often featured in this box, they apply beautifully and can be worn subtly if you know to apply them. I will say their monthly boxes can be hit or miss, so I usually like to see what’s going to be featured in their boxes for the month before I commit to buy through Amazon (which is so easy to do on here compared to through their site). For example their December box was a huge hit for me (pictured), but I just wasn’t feeling their January so I’ll likely pick up again in February. Love that they’re a cruelty free brand and they do have wonderful, innovative products. Definitely would recommend for other makeup obsessed people who aren’t afraid to use bright shades!

title: Interesting Idea But Odd Implementation - Not The Best Value for Me
text:
Overall, the box was decent but not exceed my expectations. I like the idea that if you see a box on their website that you like, you can go ahead and get it at a great discount compared to full retail price for the items when purchased individually. I see no advantage to buying this on Amazon rather than the GQ site. It might be easier to cancel through Amazon? If I had purchased through GQ site directly, I would actually have received a free bonus item, a pair of socks.

I ordered a box in May 2019 which was delivered on June 1. I expected that the first box delivered would be the summer edition that had not yet been released. I was a bit disappointed when the box arrived with with the spring items that had already been revealed on GQ site, Instagram, and other subscription blogs. This completely eliminated the surprise factor of the subscription box for new items. My initial reaction was negative since I had already seen the items inside online! If I had known that this box would be the spring box, I would not have purchased it. If you like the items pictured on the GQ site, go ahead and order! If not, hold off for the next quarter.

Part of what lead to my expectation that I would receive the summer box was that it wasn't going to be delivered immediately like normal prime items. Seeing the expected delivery of June made it seem like these would be summer items. It appears that these ship out in batches each month with the same boxes for a three month window.

Specific to the Spring box (MSA blog valued this box at ~$177):

I liked getting to try new toiletry items such as shaving cream and moisturizer, however I felt that this box was too focused on this type of item. The website and product description (estimated box value) made it seem like the box would include full size items. However, the box shipped with mostly trial size items - the bar of soap was full size. Great if you are interested in trying new toiletries but don't expect full size packages.

I have used the mophie battery pack a few times. Always nice to have another spare charger. I would not have specifically purchased this brand or paid full price for it.

The Hims gummy bear supplement was an interesting idea - However this had a significant amount of sugar and was basically gummy bears + emergen-C/Airborne. I expected that this would be a gummy vitamin. I opened the bottle and these smelled awful - I gave these away at work.

The bluetooth speaker was not what I expected. The color in all the GQ website images was black, however the one I received was blue. Additionally, the blue color did not match the color on the packaging and was very shiny which made it look cheap. I already have a bluetooth speaker. I didn't need an additional one so I gave this away as well.

title: High Quality and Delicious
text:
I wanted to give my kids something interesting since we are all stuck at home during lockdown, so I decided to spring for a snack box subscription. I chose Japanese snacks because I can't eat gluten and on occasion, they have rice-based snacks so even I can join in the fun sometimes. Through a series of bizarre circumstances I accidentally ordered a "Tokyo Treat" brand box AND this Bokksu in the same month, and it was too late to cancel when I found out. I can say that this box is absolutely better. I has full descriptions, interesting information, allergen info, and a really nice selection. It says they are premium quality and they really are -- this isn't gas station crap, it's delicious. The kids love it, and I like it, too. As far as value for money, it's a little pricey but it's coming from Japan, and in my box everything arrived whole and in good condition. I like that it comes with tea, too.

The short version is that this is definitely better than Tokyo Treat, and it's cheaper, and it's a really nice and interesting thing that kids enjoy and so do I. Not really the best budgeting choice, but I justify it to myself because I'm only buying gas for the car once a month now.

text:

title: As advertised, but not for me
text:
This is a pretty nice period kit, but it doesn't include everything I need, and it has things I will never use. I wish there were options for the tampons that come in the box. For example, I need mostly light tampons, some regulars, and a few supers, as well as some overnight pads (it is a really bad idea to sleep with a tampon in). This box came with only regular tampons. The other items that came were a handful of liners, scented feminine wipes, one pain killer (acetaminophen), a serum face mask, an eye mask, 4 bags of raspberry leaf tea, 2 Ferrero Rochers, and a wafer chocolate called a "knopper".

Over all, it's a well curated box, but it doesn't replace me having to go to the store to get tampons and pads. There are also things that I would never use, such as the scented feminine wipes (a bad idea for any person with a vagina), tea in a tea bag, and the pain killer that could interfere with my medications. Some people may be able to use this box, but I think it is not for me. I would rather make my own kit that has things I will actually use.

Note, this box does take over 2 weeks to arrive.

title: Disappointed. A Pick-Nick Kit does not equal Tactical Gear.
text:
For over $100, I was expecting a lot more, and I was expecting tactical gear, like a first aid kit, or tactical pack. Instead, I basically got a pick-nick kit.

In the box was an insulated pick-nick backpack (there are $30 ones that actually come with dishes and silverware, while this one did not), a small pick-nick blanket (I've seen much better for less than $30), a cloth hammock (they literally call it a "hippy hammock", and would be about $20), a small ax ($20), a knife (I've seen these for $11), and a pack of freeze-dried biscuits and gravy (about $7). So, overall, worth about $118, which is just a handful of dollars more than I payed for it.

They could have at least had a camping hammock, or a tactical backpack. The fact that this box is themed around tactical gear, but I got a pick-nick kit instead, was really disappointing. I was expecting survival gear, not lounging gear.

title: Nice to get one or two, but not a long term subscription.
text:
I am only giving this box 5 stars because it deserves way more than 1.6 stars, and I want to counter balance the negative reviews.

If I had continued getting similar to what I got in my first box, I would have continued this subscription. The first box seemed like a perfect emergency period kit. It had a few regular pads and tampons (not enough for a full period, but enough to get by until you can get to the store), a couple of overnight pads and super tampons, a handful of pantyliners, a couple of patches for period cramps, and wipes for bloodstains (love those). The next box had different cramp patches and no bloodstain wipes. Instead, there were snacks in this box (banana chips, granola bites, and chocolate)
Overall, I like the other various items I got in the box, especially the CBD massage oil that was in every box (It's amazing!). It seems like everything together is worth about $45 to $55, so it's not getting a deal, and is actually rather pricey considering I got the pampered ($80).
I'm not sure if I like or dislike that there is the same fabric zip pouch in every box. On one hand, it is a really useful bag, on the other hand, if I was to keep this subscription box for a year, I would have 12 bags. I have uses for all three I have gotten, but I'm going to run out of uses eventually. It would be helpful if the bags were different in every box. The bags being the same makes it hard to tell them apart and harder to find things.

I liked getting a few of these boxes, but I just can't justify keeping this subscription. If there were enough products for a full period, a comprehensive period emergency kit, a different bag every month, and the extra items in every box, I could see keeping it. As is, it just isn't worth it every month. That said, it is a nice treat once in a while.

title: What a fun box!
text:
Ok, so I don't believe in crystals having magical properties, but this is a really fun box! I love finding the little treasures in the products and adding them to my collection. I also love all of the products (which is saying something for a box of random items)! The scrub is fluffy, the shower steamers smell divine, the bath tea is rich, the bath oil is beautiful, the bath bomb is huge, and the wax melts are moisturizing (not waxy). I also have VERY sensitive skin, but none of the products have made me break out (in spite of the pleasant aromas). Overall, I am very impressed with this box and will continue my subscription.
- For those interested in crystal quality, the crystals range from about the size of a pea to a bit bigger than a quarter. They are partially tumbled. They would make for good beginner collectors samples but are not great for quality collections. Or, if you're like me and have a "treasure" chest of low-quality samples, These crystals make for a perfect addition

title: A box to make you feel ashamed.
text:
Update 2:
Order if you want to feel ashamed and think that vaginas are filthy disgusting monsters that need to be covered in perfume. The only "pampering" products I got in this last order were vagina wipes, vagina wash, and a vagina perfume spray.

Edit: (My third box was delayed because they did not put the full address on the box)
It says on amazon that the box is supposed to come with 3 products in addition to the pads, but I only got 2 in my first box. I also did not feel pampered by the products that I got in my first box. I got a feminine wash and hand sanitizing wipes. (What is with the sanitizing wipes in every box? I get its Covid times but come on, I want to feel pampered. Where are the face masks and heating patches? They would make much better regular items than sanitizing wipes.) I was thinking I would get comfort items, like their heating pads or face masks. I want things that make me feel better, not ashamed about normal feminine hygiene. I was also disappointed that the microthin liners (the only worthwhile liners) that were in my first box, were not in the second or third box. This makes 3 out of 3 boxes that had missing items. I must add that the second box was at least better. It had their snowballs, heat pads, and a sample of serum, along with some feminine wipes, of course.
I do like feeling prepared for my next period and feel there are enough pads/tampons (I have gotten both) to get me through my period. That said, there are too many liners. There are more than enough liners to wear one every day of the month.
The pads, unfortunately, do not stick to underwear of any material. Because of this, they are difficult to place. That said, once on, they surprisingly stay put. They just fall of every time you pull your underwear down. Yet, they are among the better pads I have tried. I honestly can't decide if I like this box or not. On one hand, getting the Pads Value Pack would get me similar things + more things I can actually use. On the other hand, this box is cheaper and there is the fun of the surprises. However, that an item is continuously missing from my boxes is a problem. It makes me not trust the company and makes me feel ripped off.

title: Not what I expected..
text:
I've had two shipments from Amazon at their discounted price now, hoping maybe the first one I had gotten was maybe a dud. There's no way I'd ever want to pay a full subscription price for what you get?

The first one was painting coasters. It was an okay craft, and glad I only paid $6.
The second one just came, and it's a painted "barn quilt" on a frame. It's basically the same craft on different materials. Luckily, I also only paid $6.

Do you get different crafts if you sign up when it's not $6? The pictures they show of the sample crafts look awesome, and I'd probably pay for that! But if this promotion is supposed to be an example of future crafts, there's no way the price is justifiable.

title: Great if you like what they send
text:
This was fun for a few months, but they should consider customizing your subscriptions a little more. I don’t need more products for frizzy hair, nor do I need any more bright red lipsticks or black eye makeup. And why is it that when they send cologne, its always the heavy, cloying scents—never the lighter, fresh scents that wouldnt’ gag you after trying it on your wrist? I really like getting new make-up to try, but there are way too many dark reds or nude lipsticks, and every eye makeup is always black. And for some reason, whenever they send hair products its for frizzy hair.
However every now and then they will send something really innovative—a dry shampoo, or a self-tanner, something you would always prefer to try before buying!! I will stick with them for a few more months and see if they make adjustments, but it seems like lately there are just a ton of mediocre face creams and mini hair products.
