title: A thoughtful gift!
text: I received a year-long subscription of this product from my husband for Christmas and have been delighted with the two that I've received so far! The first box was a surprise and contained a travel-sized cinnamon and cardamom hand sanitizer spritzer (which lives in my pocketbook and I use all the time), a bar of lightly scented botanical (avocado and cucumber) soap with a natural fiber (sisal) draw string bag (I'm not looking forward to the soap being gone - I've already found it on amazon and put it in my save for later bin), a small tube of leave on mask gel that smells of berries (Australian wildberry harvest and hyaluronic acid, aloe vera and cucumber extract), an avocado face mask, a self-care notebook, and lastly, an unusual piece of jewelry - a necklace made of wood (mango tree) and resin. I would have never purchased on my own, as it is not quite my style; however, I thought I would wear it because my husband gave it to me and received more kind comments on it than any other piece of jewelry I've ever owned :-) I'm happy to say it has grown on me and now I wear it all the time. It will always have special significance to me now. If you enjoy a little mystery pampering, this product is a great little gift containing a variety of high-quality beauty products. I'm really looking forward to receiving my next box!

title: Some folks are missing the point
text:
The way I see this box is that it’s for curated things that I wouldn’t usually buy. For example, in the Spring box, I received a Reily throw that is sold for $70-80 on the seller website. It’s very high quality and felt great and immediately became my favorite throw - and I wouldn’t normally pay that much for a blanket! The other items in the box were nice to have. As for the Summer box, the sunglasses are very high quality and they’re sold for $115 on the brand website. I haven’t heard about that brand before but was really impressed by the quality and looked up their other models. The same box contained a $60 retinol eye cream, and I normally wouldn’t pay that much for an eye cream! So it’s a good chance to try to see if it’s worth it. The waterproof packs are very useful to keep credit card, ID, and cash when, for example, going to the beach and I don’t want to carry my wallet.

Opinions are divided on the usefulness of the items and I totally agree, and didn’t expect, that not everything in the box is useful or needed at all! But if the goal is to receive items that I would usually buy on my own, then I wouldn’t subscribe and just go buy what I need!

title: It was worth trying.
text: I subscribed because of the Amazon deal where my first box would only cost $3. I was pleasantly surprised by the sturdy packaging and amount of tea I received. Since I already have strainers for brewing loose leaf tea, I have not tried the bags which came in the box. As for the teas, I received Blood Orange Herbal, Blue Lady Grey, QiLan Oolong, and Genmaicha. I really enjoyed the herbal tea (rooibos, orange peel, hibiscus, rosehips, apple pieces, safflowers, rose petals, and orange/vanilla/lemon flavor) and would buy it again on its own. The black tea (whole leaf black tea, blue mellow blossoms, lavender flowers, and bergamot flavor) was pretty good, although I already have other Earl and Lady Grey teas that I enjoy. I found the oolong to be okay and drinkable, but will probably pass it on to a friend. The Genmaicha (bancha green tea, popped corn and toasted hulled rice kernels) was horrible on all counts. Upon opening it smelled odd as though something was old or rancid, but I decided to give it a go anyway.  After forcing three sips I had to pour it out. I don't know if I got a bad bag or I just don't have a taste for that blend, but I'm throwing the rest of the bag in the trash. While I enjoyed this box experience (for the most part), I'll be cancelling my subscription since it's a better deal for me to buy tea that I can see, smell and ideally sample first.

title: My girls aren't impressed
text:
This month was my first month getting the boxcat box. I decided to try the Luxury box; normally $35.99 a month, my first box discount priced it at $29.99. Included was:
* Chicken treats.
* A little bunny thing with 2 puffballs.
* A carrot.
* A mat.
* A string-powered jitterpig.
* A little jangleball.

1. My cats LOVE their food, normally, but kept spitting the treats back out of their mouths as soon as they picked them up :( Additionally there was no nutritional value provided such as estimated caloric or protein content, so I feel hesitant to pass the unused treats to one of my other cat-owning friends.
2. The little jitter toy only moved long enough to make them look at it, then I would have to touch it again and the girls would get distracted.
3. I think the carrot was intended as a kicker toy, but they were only interested in tearing up the tissue paper. And unless the carrot is their "skincare, wellness item or cat gear item", that item is missing from the box.
The quality of the mat isn't what I expected from a "luxury" addition, to be honest- it feels very handmade and flimsy, and my cats immediately disregarded it- and overall what we got doesn't feel like the kind of thing I would expect from a box that costs $36/month.

title: One of the best beauty sub boxes out there!
text:
Pictured above is my first box, sometime last year when it was only $15. Price is now $23, with free shipping still. I’ve loved everything they’ve sent so far, including amazing brands like Sunday Riley, Akar, AHC, and many more that I never would have splurged on or known about otherwise. Before Allure, my skincare routine was practically nonexistent, and quite frankly boring. Using the same drugstore face wash, makeup, moisturizer, and beauty products wasn’t exactly exciting. Now my skincare routine is SO much better, and I definitely look forward to using fun, new items every month. So far, I’ve gotten face wash (including an AMAZING face bar by Erno Laslo, sp?) moisturizer, oils, pimple patches, nail appliqués, face masks, eye masks, hair cream, hair protective spray, highlighter, eyeshadow, eyeliner, mascara,, sunscreen, lipstick, toner, and just... so many things. They NEVER send you the same product twice, and I absolutely love the full size products and small size products are perfect for traveling. I love that you can preview the next month’s box and skip if you don’t think you’ll like it too. I check the value on every product, and there’s been MANY times where one product alone is worth well over the cost of the box.

New member gift when signing up, and a huge box if you sign up for a year at a time. Great Facebook community (Allure Beauty Box subscribers) where members discuss items in their box and sell or swap their stashes. Every box comes with a booklet that gives hints and tips on how to use the products, as well as coupon codes if you wish to purchase more.

I’ve since subscribed to BoxyCharm as well, and they’re both a great value for the money. BoxyCharm is more tailored to your quiz results, while Allure is pretty much one size fits all, with slight variations, like brown or black eyeliner for instance. Both send notifications upon shipment, and I’ve never had anything arrive broken or unable to use.

Overall, great box! Really happy I went with it!

title: Very mixed feelings
text:
I have very mixed feelings about this whole subscription:
Pros: the colors of product/kitchen tool is vibrant and bright. Everything my daughter has received so far has been good quality and I've actually used hers instead.
The "recipe" is lamented which is nice for beginner cooks.
It always ships on time and in tacked.

That's about it though bc my cons list is higher...in fact, and I was typing the pros, I kept wanting to say, "ya BUT". So here are my Ya BUT:
There has yet to be a month where I thought, "Wow, that was total worth the subscription price" and actually I only kept it coming bc I thought maybe they were starting out slow and simplistic to make sure kids and their parents were enjoying and kept the monthly subscription going, but NOPE, most months are really pretty pathetic on which kitchen tool comes.
The products ARE quality, like I mentioned above, I even enjoy using them at times. BUT the choice of tools AND the recipes are way out there for the most part and NOT something beginner little chefs would even WANT to eat, let alone spending their time learning to try to make.
Which brings my next con...I've noticed the grocery product list get pretty pricey and are not always sold in every day grocery stores or in smaller quantities. Instead, you end up either going from store to store, buying it on Amazon/somewhere online and wait days for arrival, or your young chef gives up and the recipe is never made, which brings you back to comments about price and kids really wanting to learn to cook.
I gave this a try for a solid year before canceling. What was even more sad is my now 14 yr old loved getting a fun surprise each month but didn't bat an eye, yell/fight about deciding to cancel etc, instead was actually happy about it bc she said she felt guilty about receiving something she never used. I could have purchased her ... anything else with the money wasted on this subscription. Heck, I could have and should have (maybe I still will) actual cooking lessons from one of the local grocers. I could have taken them with her and made fun memories instead of all this. Boo, wish I could get my money back, would even give everything received back as well.

title: This "Service" is a Ripoff and Customer Service is a Joke!
text:
I subscribed to Pusheen Box back in Summer of 2020 because I wanted something to cheer us up while we were all stuck in our homes and unable to go or do anything due to my husband's job. The first box (Summer), was fine, but it had some issues in shipping making its way to us. That's fine, most of the items in the box were cute and seemed to be mostly well made.

Both Fall and Winter boxes (2020) had shipping issues and it took over two weeks to get to us, despite being shipped FedEx. Items in the box were mixed; the clothing items were of quality, but almost everything else in the boxes outside of the figurines was dollar store or knock-off quality that you'd see for sale in a a dollar store or from a "third-party" vendor from China here on Amazon. Numerous people complained that their electronic lantern in the fall box was broken and didn't work... Pusheen Box did not offer refunds to anyone... and instead told them to go find EXTREMELY specific battery brands to use in the lantern (which didn't fix the problem). The Winter Box had dollar store salt and pepper shakers and "wine" glasses. The glasses I received were imperfect and had bubbles trapped in the glass. The decals were placed over glasses with nub defects (small bits of glass sticking out of an otherwise smooth surface). No refunds or replacements were offered to anyone with these issues or if they were, people never GOT the replacements they were promised.

Fast forward to Spring 2021. The box was charged to my account on March 17. The box's release was delayed with NO REASON given by the company.. so it didn't even "ship" until April 28th. I didn't get any tracking information until May 4th... and it's been stuck in limbo with no updates and several "delivery" dates that have been passed on.

Add to that that you can't get a hold of ANYONE at their customer support. You send an email into the void and you MIGHT get a response 5 days later that is cursory and mostly doesn't answer your complaints or questions. It's May 19th now... and I still have no Spring Box, STILL have not heard back from customer service despite THREE SEPARATE tickets being launched. I have only received ONE response about tracking not updating.. and that was on May 14th. NOTHING since then, my package is still lost... and you can't even call up FedEx to look into it because Culture Fly (the company that runs these boxes) has a "sticky" on all the boxes, stating that the receiver (me) has to contact them (the sender) to launch an investigation... but how am I supposed to that when you NEVER REPLY TO YOUR EMAILS?!?!

So subpar service, SLOW delivery times, lost packages and declining quality of items in just 9 months... I do NOT recommend anyone purchase a sub from this company. Do yourself a favor and look up other reviews about this company on other review aggregate sites. It's not pretty. I wish I had.

title: Old Cats Like It
text:
They all come running - seems they all know the box has arrived. On our 3rd box now for my five 13 and 14 year old kitties. This month was the safari themed box. They like everything in it. The mama-cat went wild with the 'vest', throwing it up in the air, tossing it about. It's great to see her playing again.

Most of my toy choices simply weren't working for my kitties. Their one favorite mouse product was discontinued by the manufacturer a few years ago and the extras I bought are slowly dying. They had no interest in the toys I was getting them except the glitter ball. So, I tried a Kitnip box to see if they could improve on what I was buying and it has been pretty successful. I get the box without the treats, so they get an extra toy. So far, out of 3 boxes, only 2 toys were not played with - those went to my sister who has much younger cats.

Here's the thing - it's not going to work for all cats. If your cat tears toys apart, your cat will tear these apart as well. They are well made toys, but they are not indestructible. Some of my cats like big toys, some prefer teeny tiny toys. I was actually surprised Mama was playing with the safari vest as she is normally exclusively a tiny toy cat. Pricewise, not bad - the average toy at Petsmart is $5-7. So 5 toys for $20 is pretty reasonable especially since they are playing with most of them! Each box includes a wand-like toy for you to encourage them to movement, although the one that hung on the door was of no interest to my older cats.

title: I cannot stress this enough
text:
I bought a single one time box on amazon at Christmas for the fuzzbucket. I was honestly far more impressed than I thought I would be. I then started a subscription with Barkbox directly.
The customer service this company has cannot be surpassed. Seriously. I have a 90 monster who is “dainty” when it comes to his toys. He wants the little boy toys and the big boy treats. He believes that toys that are made for his size are far too big for his delicate little mouth, so he wants the tinier toys. But don’t you dare skimp on his treat size, he’s not that dainty! Dogs are weird.
Anyway, they helped to customize his boxes so they come to his liking. The toys are very well made and quite clever honestly. He gets the normal ones, so I cannot attest to the durability of the super chewer box. And let’s face it, if your dog wants the stuffing, the squeaker, or the crinkle out; the stuffing, squeaker, and crinkle ARE coming out.
The dog loves his bark boxes. I know the day they get delivered, when I come through the back door after work the dog will frantically herd me to the front door to get the mail. Once I get the box in, the dog noses at it until I get it open, while the cat lies in wait behind the sofa to pounce out and claim the box the moment it empties.
The thought and work they put into designing these themes is amazing. It’s not just a couple of themed toys and treats, they’ve also got cleverly designed box liners (last month was gym themed, the liner had an elaborate and cute step by step exercise sheet for your dog to do) and a little booklet for the humans to be amused by (last months shaped like a vcr tape box with a dog dressed like Richard Simmons and a tape shaped insert that slid out). On the inside of every box there is also an amusing little cartoon dog saying something punny. He’s kind of hidden, it took a few months before I saw him.
Honestly, for the price, you will get good quality toys, a couple of bags of treats, and a chew that your dog will love. If your dog doesn’t love something, they will replace it. If your dog immediately destroys a toy, they will replace it with a more durable one.
If your unsure about the quality of the toys or treats, you can order an individual one from their website. The same goes for the treats.
I honestly spend a lot less on my dog since I’ve started this subscription. I’d go to Petco every month for his treats and come out with a bagful of cheap crappy toys and about $100 lighter. Now he gets a few long lasting durable toys he loves and some treats to boot and I don’t have to go to petco!

title: Value doesn't make sense for the gamble
text:
Okay, the box I received was a pretty good match. I got the single cat box because I wasn't sure how I'd feel about the contents for a house of two kitties, and honestly, that was totally fine. It's not like we go through a bag of treats in a month or toys are like, color-coded per cat. The "College" themed box included a bag of treats, a catnip "textbook" toy, a kicker stick that looks like a brick library building, two hard bouncy "atom" balls, and a pom-pom ended toy that has a bungee cord so if the cat pulls hard enough at the pom-pom treats you've loaded inside will drop. The last had a velcro loop on top so you could hang it, and it says it's adjustable as to how hard they have to pull if your cats dig it.
For my cats, the catnip book has been a hit, the building toy was meh, the atom balls are amusing but they're hard rubber so they won't pick them up and we'll see if they play soccer with them. The pom-pom toy was amusing as a dancer toy, but they haven't pulled hard enough to release treats from it yet. It's a short tube with a short line to the pom-pom so it's not a great dancer toy. Only one of my cats will eat the treats.
That's 2.5 - 3 out of 5 successes for my house. There's no customization, so I figured it wouldn't be all wins, and there was a variety of types of toy which is great. However, according to their math on the insert, the value of the items adds up to $25. If the subscriber price for the box is $20 and not everything tickles your fancy, you might as well just go to PetCo. Having a curated theme and a box that is a nice nap spot doesn't feel like it adds a whole lot of value.

title: It’s a classic alternative to going to a Comic Shop
text:
I bought the Super Box as originally I was seeking to expand my new growing comic book collection. I was impressed with the variety and they really do cater to which categories you pick in your order.

I spent time doing research on each packed comic and almost all of the issues are just like regular “issues” you can buy at a shop. I cannot say the box is worth double, but you do receive comics (total) worth more than the purchase. It also must be noted most of the comics dates back 3-4-5-6 and more years ago. Of course this box is still reasonable priced and is a deal.

Now I did receive several variants which are very pleasant but as mentioned above, they still fall in the same category of “regular comics you could buy anywhere.”

Now of course I might be contracting myself, but I did receive a special 1-25 variant which is considered very valuable as of now. That being said, all of the other included comics were just all right.

Maybe I am a little biased because I’m also into comics as a investment aspect, but this is still an excellent subscription box service. This is considered the perfect gift for anyone for any occasion.

Just don’t go into this service for the appreciation or investment reasons, this is more of a collection box kind of deal with exposure to new comic worlds we never would of thought of.

This box subscription service still has an excellent price, just be sure to appreciate what you get. I do plan to buy more boxes because I admire the exposure to new comic worlds.

title: Gift for our adventurous teen
text:
We have one of those kids that really likes weird, odd things... literally his favorite snacks are seaweed strips. So, while these are all things I could easily go out and get myself for a much cheaper price, this is the kind of thing that he could appreciate and enjoy getting as a monthly box. We received the box yesterday and he's already consumed more than half of it (teenager). There were some odd things that he really liked and some things that were just "weird" and likely won't be consumed completely. He really enjoyed that there was a rating card included with the box. There were snacks that had I bought him or just presented to him he likely would have turned his nose up in response to, but the idea of the box being his gave it excitement.
The parents in our house get a monthly cocktail subscription box (Shaker & Spoon) and a more adult snacks subscription box (Mantry) - so I didn't have a problem with paying for the Premium box for him.

title: Gourmet Cookies & Organic Coffee Oh my!
text:
In my never ending search for more and more, and more organic coffee I stumbled into this subscription box. I've tried other subscription coffees on Amazon, those that will not be named here, but they did not offer organic coffee. With one service you may get organic coffee from time to time and with the other service there was just no option.
The idea of getting 2 cookies paired with a great roast of organic coffee seems like a perfect combo with the only negative thing being that it leaves me wanting more and more, and more...
The cookies are always bakery fresh and individually sealed. They are a decent size and always taste amazing. Every cookie that I have had to date from this service is always fresh, delicious, and leaves me wanting more.
The coffee is where it's at and was my main focus. While I do not like any flavored coffee, I always love trying different roasts of coffee from different places. It amazes me how coffee can taste so different even though from the outside it's "just coffee". It's fun getting a box with bright green shredded paper for packaging every month filled with 2 small packages, which is now 1 bigger package of coffee and 2 cookies.
The coffee comes freshly ground and sealed in the multi-layer pouch. I don't notice any valves on these pouches to release the gas that ground coffee can emit, but given that it is so freshly ground and you will probably drink it up fast I guess this isn't a big deal. I believe the coffee would last a year as they do seem to be vacuum sealed with no room for anything to get in there or out until you break open the seal and inhale the fragrant & freshly roasted coffee. I don't think there is any better smell than ground coffee. Maybe fresh baked cookies? No, on second thought, coffee smells better and is so much better for you, usually (depending on how you enjoy your coffee).

title: Excellent quality but not age appropriate-- maybe 8-11
text:
I've gotten this box for several months. The contents are great, the materials well thought out and educational, and I love the consistency in how information is presented. I.E, there's always magazine that has a consistent format, and a lot of the materials are made at the same level of quality with instructions, etc. My problem with this is my 5 (almost 6 year old now) is not able to understand the level that the information is presented at, nor is she able to build the demonstrations with a 5 year old's limited dexterity. I had to build every single demonstration myself while she watched with minimal ability to assist. Considering that it can take an hour or more to build something, she'd get bored and want to "help". It hasn't been much fun.

Also, I'd read the materials to her and most of it would go over her head. Note this from the current box: "Newton's 2nd Law: The force exerted on an object is equal to the object's mass times its acceleration. The acceleration of a gymnast spinning on a beam is based on their mass and the force of the energy they exert." This is completely ungraspable by a 5 year old. I'm ditching this box subscription and will come back in 3-5 years.

title: Worst Candy I Have EVER Tasted!
text: This was gifted to me. When it showed up at my house I was excited because I love candy and it looked cool. Once I opened the box, I noticed that a bunch of the candy had melted together. Disappointing, but not a game changer. However, once I opened the containers to try the gummies, I couldn't even get them out of the container because they had hardened into one massive gummie lump. Once I finally cut a piece out, it was terrible, then I tried a little of each one, and for the first time in my sweets-loving life, I wasn't willing to try a second bite of any of it. I eat a lot of candy and I'm not very picky, but this candy tasted like chemicals and had a mouth feel like plastic. I even called my sister to tell her to never gift this to anyone ever again because it was so bad! She was very sad and disappointed because she said it looked so good and she knew how much I liked candy. If I could give it 0 stars, I would. I don't care how cute the package is, if your product tastes like crap, awesome packaging can't make up for it and those who gave it 1 or 2 stars for cute packaging were being waaaaaay too nice.

title: Not Appropriate For Age Group Specified.
text: I was looking for a monthly book subscription for my granddaughter. I had read mixed reviews about this service so I had the first set sent to my home so I could tell for myself. I have to side with the people who said the books were not well-chosen for the specified audience. I picked 0-12 months. One book was a board book and it was about the nose. It was cute. The other two were not for a 6-month old. One was a "First Reader" with small peel off stickers to place in the book. The other was nursery rhymes, but more of the Grimm's variety. No rhyme, no meter, and one was about pulling off a guys legs. Definitely not age appropriate. I ended up just buying a bunch of books from Amazon with 10,000+ reviews, 4.8+ stars, and rated by customers on age group appropriateness. I ended up with a great list of well-known and loved books. Now I'll just send her some each month. It took a little longer and some research, but in the end I think it will be well worth it. Reading is too important to start them out with "just whatever". I want all the book spines to be worn and cracked and the pages falling out from how often it was read. Not used under a short leg on a bedside table to keep it from wobbling. :)

title: Nice idea, but expensive for what you actually get
text:
Sure, it's convenient, but I just expected something a bit more than what was in the box.

Ingredients - I thought the box would have unusual or non- staple items. Nope. The most unusual for November was cranberries. Everything else was just pretty normal stuff. Now, if you want to re-create the box, i can see where you might just want staple items. I just thought for the price, there'd be something unique about the ingredients.

Packaging -- The packaging was inviting with well marked items and a tissue wrapper that made it into an experience to unwrap and explore. My one recommendation: it'd be nice to know the amount of each ingredient, in case you want to make more.

November bake -- it really was just a sweet sticky mess. I split the dough into 2; preserving the second batch to see how the first turned out. The needed much more flour to release from the pan, which was really a pain if you wait the 10 minutes to cool on the cooking sheet. The second batch I put in well sprayed muffin tins and they hung together better and was much easier clean (I didn't let the Rugelach cool -- I immediately removed from the pan. Much easier cleaning.

Bottom line: it's restaurant prices, but you do all the clean up yourself! I understand there's proprietary recipe and decorative packaging to give you the experience itself. It's just a bit too expensive.

I can't even remember the specific roaster or whatever because I threw the bag away after dumping the beans into my container but what a difference. Like the first time you try a craft IPA after drinking bud light your whole life. Night and day.

So now instead of cheap grocery store coffee I'm spending ~$26/month on bean box AND I'm buying whole bean coffee from the local roaster on my block at work. I do normal (i.e. cheaper but still kinda expensive) coffee at work everyday and save the (premium) bean box stuff for weekends when I can relax with my wife and try to pick out the "tasting notes". The 12 ounce bag per month is perfect for this. So it is REALLY good and it's a great weekend tradition/treat but be careful because you will find yourself venturing ever-further into coffee snobbery. I even tested the temperature of the water I poured into my chemex the other day. Seriously - I'm insufferable. And it can happen to you. So don't say you weren't warned.

title: Deceptive and Horrid Customer Experience
text:
I've probably tried about 4-5 boxes from GQ over the past 3 years. Here's what I learned: often you're receive the same free samples they hand out in a mall, except now you're paying for them. Once in a while, you'll get a full size product, and rarely it'll be something you'll enjoy.

The other items that you'd expect in the box are actually index cards with coupon codes where you're supposed to redeem them for "free" items. Well, let me explain what in reality happens: half the sizes/colors aren't available when you go to redeem your coupon, and often, these aren't items that the retailer normally sells -- they're thinner, cheaper, less desirable versions specially made for GQ. You want to redeem your free shirt in Large, and prefer blue? Too bad: you'll get size small in white.

Another deception: last quarter they gave a code for a "free pair of Bombas sock". Guess what? The socks are free, but Bombas bangs you for $5 to ship them, so that's in addition to the $50 you wasted on the GQ Box.

And here's also where the wheels fall off: they regularly forget to pack items in the box. You can call them and they'll try to help, but sometimes they have nothing left.

My last box also provided my a coupon code for a free pair of underwear, but they provided a broken link to redeem them. I called and the rep couldn't help so now I'm waiting for a manager to resolve. It's a Mickey Mouse operation from top to bottom.

I love the concept, but the execution is just piss poor. Save your money.

Makeup shades were always way off for dark brown skin and the hair products were absolute no-no’s for those of us with kinky hair! I even called customer service to inquire about a more diversity-friendly box, but the nice lady just apologized that they didn’t have that, so I ended my subscription and threw the useless products away. Some of the products work for everyone, but everyone should be able to use all of the products in the box. I suspect thousands of us who are currently left out, would become faithful customers and would probably flood YouTube with reviews, if we were to be included. title: Watch for Shipping Charges
text:
I've been very happy with the type of toys and quality of toys I've been sent the last five months (3 to 4 year old option) though they lean a bit heavy toward engineering and not enough technology, science or math IMHO, BUT my last shipment was charged a hefty shipment fee, regardless of the fact that the subscription terms promise free shipping. When I called to correct the problem, I was put on hold repeatedly and read FAQ files that had nothing to do with my problem. After 30 minutes of repeatedly explaining that I wanted the shipping charges removed because the subscription promises free shipping, the representative finally cancelled my shipment completely. I am not sure what would have happened if I hadn't called before the toy had actually shipped. Would I have had to return the toy? Pay for return shipping? Just eat the shipping charges that month? I'm sure the result would have been something annoyin since it was apparently completely impossible to simply remove the shipping charge.

Anyway, keep an eye out for stealth shipping charges and be prepared for a 30 minute call that culminates in losing your shipment for the month to "fix it."

title: Wanted to love this...
text: First off, I want to say that this program could be an amazing, old school record club with a few improvements. Right now though, it's not quite right. I was a member for several months receiving similar classic albums to the rest of the group, each of which was at or a little below their normal cost. The albums were packaged well, arrived on time and were of high quality. Last month I was excited to receive an updated copy of Pink Floyd's "Darkside of the Moon", noting it on my orders page prior to shipping. A few days later Amazon cancelled the shipment due to a carrier issue and rather than reship it or send something new, they refunded the monthly fee. That's fine, but it's a record club so just send a new one or something different rather than cancelling out the entire month's shipment. This month my next album showed up on my order screen, CCR's Greatest Hits which isn't an album I currently have, so I was happy to get it. I clicked on the album link to see what songs were included and noticed that the album's current selling price through Amazon is actually less than the monthly club price which is problematic. As this is a club format, getting whatever album Amazon chooses is part of fun and excitement, however paying more than what I would if I'd just picked the album and ordered myself, not so much. I've cancelled the club for now, but will rejoin if Amazon figures out how to work through some of the challenges this program currently has.

title: The Who records delivered to you every month!
text:
I have over 5k records spread out over several musical genres so I figured this would be a longshot but opted to try it out. Maybe I could get a few I missed, maybe some reasonably priced upgrades, perhaps something I haven't considered but enjoy. Surprisingly in the several months I've been using this, they haven't sent me any duplicates yet. How is that you ask? Well it's because it's been The Who, over and over, every month. I don't really like The Who all that much. I mean sure, they're OK. But outside of Who's Next (which somehow hasn't even been one of the records) I'd be fine with a greatest hits comp.
Interesting side note, there was one Blondie record mixed in, but it was the Heart Of Glass EP. Which retails for about $16. Keep in mind the service costs $25 at the time of this writing.

I guess I was really hoping for a Columbia House type experience and I'm just not getting it here. Hopefully they can turn it around and make this into something great, which it definitely has the potential to be. Right now however I'd save my money if I was on the fence.

title: On Third Box and Still Enjoying It!
text:
October 2020 Box: Since I can only update my existing review, just thought I'd mention I'm still enjoying this subscription box. There are always several items I can use and so far, it has exceeded its value. That includes both merits in cost and time because I don't have to put in the research or effort to try to find these items. I get to sample a variety of products at a fraction of the cost, too. Saves me from a big letdown if an item isn't to my liking.

October is my favorite month so far, likely because it was a change of pace. Instead of the bevy of natural hair care products normally contained in the box, this month's focus was primarily on skin and self-care. I even received a black tote bag instead of the standard beige one. It'll be easier to keep this one looking clean!

The following full-sized items were included in my October box: Reshma Rose Water Toner, Reshma Tumeric Face Wash, Revealu Face & Body Gold (skin moisturizing gel), Eden Bodyworks Almond Marshmallow Leave-in Conditioner, and a Hawaiian Silky Gel Activator. I am looking forward to using ALL of these products!

The sample-sized items received for October were: Allsan gel hand sanitizer (the description "travel size" probably fits better than "sample size"), travel-size Solar Bloom/Rain "Reserve Blend" duo (Sephora exclusive perfumes), Kiss Colors & Care Shampoo sample pouches x 3 (interestingly, this is black herbal hair dye in the form of a shampoo), Hero Cosmetic acne blemish patches x 2 + rescue balm x 1, and Pink Walnut Tooth Powder.

With the exception of the Color Change shampoo/dye, I'll definitely sample all of these to determine if I like them or not, including the scents, even though they are not my style (I lean towards lighter citrus/warm/floral notes). EDIT: Love the scents and am keeping. They do have floral and fruit notes in them. The Solar Bloom is definitely my fave of the two.

Again, still loving my COCOTIQUE subscription box and although I'm only three boxes in, October is by far my favorite month. Looking forward to the next one!

OLD REVIEW (Summarized):

Overall, I enjoyed my first Cocotique subscription box and am looking forward to the next one. For me, I was most excited to receive the five full-sized Lotta Body Milk & Honey curly hair care products. Those items alone totaled more than the price of the subscription box. While excited over the hair care products, I actually loved the Herbacin hand creams the most. This is something I will use every day and will likely purchase a full-sized product once I run out of the samples. The face mask (the beauty kind, not the COVID-19 kind :D) and Teleties hair ties were simply viewed as complimentary items and I'll eventually get around to using/testing them out. :p Although it says this is for women of color, interestingly enough, anyone could have used most of the products in it and if you have naturally curly or coily hair, you'd receive the full benefit of the items in the box.

text: I stumbled across Therabox in a facebook ad and was intrigued and bought a 3-month subscription.  I'm really awful at making time for myself and I thought this might be a good way to try and integrate some self-care into my life.  I got my first box and it contained several items such as face masks, a journal, a pen, a necklace, tea, and a few other items.  Since then, I have received four boxes and I LOVE them.  They contain about 8ish items per box and the box contains a description of each item and where you can buy them if you like them.  I like the variety of items in the box and it has exposed to me to a lot of different items I never would have tried otherwise.  Every box contains one item specifically for self-care such as a self-esteem book, self-care idea cards, positivity journal, etc.  Best of all, if you don't like certain items they have a facebook page where you can trade for other items.  This box is a really fun way to try new items while taking care of yourself.  I would highly recommend it.

title: Like a box of chocolates, you never know what you're gonna git!
text:
We're 3 months into STEM Club so far, and so far its "pretty good". My daughter is 6 years old, and I'm doing my darndest to make her a geek like me. Here's the breakdown...

Month 1, we received a kit to create your own bounce balls, a gyroscope kit, and a make your own dinosaur fossil kit. All in all, the 3 items combined were worth about $20, so you got your value, but the items weren't the most exciting for my daughter. We played with the bounce balls and gyroscope for about 10 minutes and then forgot about them.
- Kit cost: approximately $20.
- Entertainment: approximately 10 minutes.
- Ranking: 2/5

Month 2, we received a science kit which was a lot of fun. It contained items to make water bubble, ways to test for acids and bases, some fun stuff. All in all the kit was fun, it was once and done however, but we'd definately buy the kit again in the future.
- Kit cost: approximately $20.
- Entertainment: 2 hours.
- Ranking: 4/5

Month 3, we received a STEM Programmable Mouse, this thing is VERY cool. You essentially program a mouse to find the cheese by pressing forward, backward and turn buttons on the mouse. The kit comes with cards that help you teach the child how many button presses you need, etc. We've unpacked this thing at least 5 times since we received it, and my daughter really enjoyed it every time.We'd buy this as a gift for other kids in the future as well.
- Kit Cost $40
- Entertainment: 10+ Hours
- Ranking 5/5

text: On one of the text inserts that came with the box, they said that they aren't actually a tea company, they are a gift company. And that is exactly right. It's a cute gift, nicely packaged, but the tea is very subpar. We drink a lot of tea and my husband recently gave up caffeine, so I got him this box to sample lots of herbal teas to see what he might like. I think there are suposed to be 5 tsp per tea for 20 cups of tea total, but they are consistently underfilled (4 tsp per bag) and when brewed, they are consistently really weak teas. Usually loose leaf tea is nicer than bagged tea with full leaves and fresh ingredients. However, the teas are more like the bottom of the barrel and more dust than leaves. We have a micromesh strainer for rooibos so that you don't end up drinking the "splinters", but this tea is so dusty and tiny that it escaped the cotton bag and metal filters. It really should be reserved for low quality bags. Normally brewing rooibos, it gets nice and dark in 3-5 minutes rich with flavor, but this never gets really dark and tastes so watered down even when brewed exactly like similar teas from other companies. We had this subscription for 4 months now and while it's cute and the tea flavors sound good with a good variety, they are all just so WEAK compared to very similar flavors and types of teas from other companies. Even the hibiscus tea didn't get dark red or have flavor. It just makes me think that the tea is really old and broken down, or whatever leftovers there were that couldn't be sold to higher quality companies. I wanted to love this box, but am just disapointed. They say you should have 20 cups of tea with 1 tsp each. We have a 1 tsp tea scoop from vhadam (a really good quality tea company that also has an amazon subscription) and the bags are consistenyly only filled with 4 tsp. With how weak it is, you really have to use double that and you can't really rebrew since it's so weak already, so ou really only get 2-4 cups per type of tea (8-16 total instead of 20).

title: VALUE!!!
text:
My usual medium is oil paint so I was a bit skeptical.

I needn’t have been. This kit is BRILLIANT! Not only does it provide art lessons I will take into my oil paintings, it’s beginner friendly enough that my 16 year old (who has never even shown any interest in art at ALL) is excited to try it. There are full color illustrated instructions- as well as access to a video tutorial for the piece.

The paints are brilliantly colored, and I LOVE that part of this is (perhaps unintentionally) teaching color theory to beginners. My first kit has 2 BEAUTIFUL, vibrant, colorful projects, and it teaches how to mix the base colors-red blue yellow- and black and white to create every color needed in the pieces.

Everything needed to complete the projects was included. Canvases. Brushes. Paints. Someone who has NEVER painted but has seen or been inspired by Bob Ross could pick this kit up and knock out a beautiful piece of art on their first try.

I’m very VERY impressed with this kit for the price. Very worth it. I will be maintaining my subscription for the foreseeable future!!!

title: Three boxes in, and things aren't looking too good.
text:
The Deadpool Box was fairly uninspiring. The Pop! was great, but the rest, not so much.

I loved the Venom box. Great pose for Venom, nice shirt, neat pint-size, decal. Your mileage may vary, but it was a step up, I thought.

The First Ten Years box? This one makes me wonder if Funko is even involved in curating the items. Funko boxes used to look like boxes for fans, by fans. But this latest looks like it was planned by someone with little investment in the community.

For starters, how about that centerpiece? Iron Man vs. Whiplash. If you like Iron Man 2, great. None of the Marvel films have been absolute stinkers, not even Dark World. But Iron Man 2 isn't at the top of people's lists. And, perhaps more to the point, it is not worth commemorating in a celebration of Marvel Studios first ten years. Why not surprise and delight customers and do a Movie Moments diorama with Thor coming down on Cap's shield? Or if that already exists, surely there's something else out there. Even an exclusive Thanos Pop! marking some significant moment from Infinity War would have been a more fitting thing.

As for the rest of the items, I don't think Pint-Size are bad, or even the Pez, but the characters are not immediately recognizable in gold, and I had to look at the back of the package (with characters in color) to recognize Thor. And between the Pez and one of the Pint-Size, you've got two items from Ragnarok!

No Cap, no Guardians, and a lot of wasted space for Whiplash. People will always disagree about the class of item included, but the themes should always make sense. And for a box advertised as a celebration of the first ten years of Marvel Studios, this is an utter failure.

title: You lost a lifer... don’t waste your $$, people!!!
text:
UPDATED AFTER MARVEL STUDIOS BOX
(Skip to 2nd to last paragraph for November ‘18 review)

*Venom Box*

So disappointing. I have purchased every MCC box since Funko started doing these. The last one (Deadpool) was nice. Good items, Good box, etc. This Venom box was pretty horrible all-around. From the lackluster items (including one just thrown into a ziploc baggie, never seen that before) to the fact that Amazon stuck packing and shipping stickers ALL OVER the box in lieu of packing into a shipping box, just not good.

I am not going to cancel my subscription... yet, as I am cautiously optimistic about the 10 year box in November. I will say though, as a "lifer" with MCC, if the November box is a disappointment, I will be cancelling, and I know a lot of other people that will be as well.

Here's hoping for a better future *fingers crossed*

*Marvel Studios First Ten Years Box*

Well... that’s it for me, never purchasing another box. To say that the Marvel Studios First Ten Years box is disappointing would be the understatement of 2018. Lazy, cheap, unappealing, and just downright sad. I don’t necessarily want to spoil what’s in the box because I know we’re not “supposed” to do that. That being said though, I will say that this box only contains 4 items, two of which are the same thing. One you can get for $3. The last item is probably the least satisfying Pop! Vinyl since the MCC started.

With all that, I’m officially out. I can’t justify wasting any more money on this program. Cheers to the MCC of ole, and I hope people read this prior to the new box purchase.

title: Best subscription out there!
text:
We just hit one year of our subscription and plan to keep it going for quite a while! We started it when our son was 7.5 years old (the 8-13 year old STEM club). These are the items we have received so far:
Smartivity Mechanical Xylofun Music Machine
Constructechs Educational Engineering DIY Remote Control 2 in 1 Space Racer
Thames & Kosmos Optical Science
SmartLab Toys Ultimate Secret Formula Lab
Thames & Kosmos Wind Power 2.0
OWI Kingii Dragon Robot Science Kit
Thames & Kosmos Physics Workshop
National Geographic Mega Fossil Mine
SmartLab Toys Smart Circuits Games & Gadgets Electronics Lab
Engino Discovering Stem: Levers, Linkages & Structures Building Kit

There have also been two months with ThinkFun games (Gravity Maze and Laser Maze). We absolutely love ThinkFun games in our home, and have many of them, so we cancelled the orders before they shipped since we already had those two particular ones.

The variety of items has been incredible. The prices can't be beat! I check out each item we get on Amazon and the cheapest one has been $25, all the way up to $40+, for the subscription fee of only $20. The quality of items has been wonderful as well. The Engino set was such a huge hit that my son requested more for birthday and Christmas. He plays with the Engino sets more than Legos now! I think he is up to 5 of the sets, and they all work together.

You CAN see what is coming before it ships. The items are ordered on the same day each month. If you check your order page you can see what is going to be coming and cancel it if you want before it ships. It is a very small time window, but it is very possible if you choose. The value and quality we receive far outweighs any perceived inconvenience for checking the order page once a month.

I have recommended the Amazon STEM Club to many people as I feel it's one of the best subscription services of any kind based on the value and quality. We have not had experience with the younger subscriptions, but I can vouch for the 8-13 year old one. I definitely think that age range is appropriate. Our 7.5 year old was able to do most of the first several sets that came, but he has needed parental assistance for a good number of them. We've just turned it into a fun weekly activity - "Maker Monday". We make some tea together and have fun with the sets. These aren't "once-and-done" type sets. There is a lot of longevity in most of them, different builds, different experiments, etc. It's been a great experience to share together. :)

My 7 year old kept getting super babyish items suited for Pre-schoolers, and my 9 year old was overwhelmed by the teen level kits in his age bracket. The final bit for me was a non-stem baby RC car and the complicated formula lab that is just too messy for my hyperactive boys.
Had there been some sort of approval for the kits or preview of the shipment that might have helped, but unless I had some way of saying No Thanks to the kits I felt were not appropriate I would not do Amazon STEM again.
To be fair- about half of the kits were ok, but rarely in the same month for my two kids. I had to skip months to stock up on the acceptable kits so that one of my kids was not left out due to an effectively unusable STEM kit. With the disappointing kits and the stream of returns I had to manage, it was a monthly hassle I started to really dread.
Paying full price for actual age appropriate STEM activities is where I will have to be. Too wide of age brackets and no order approval has made it unworkable for us.

text:
When my first box came in, I immediately brewed all four teas, with each one yielding approximately 8 cups.

The teas included were an Oolong, a lavender Earl Gray, a Green Tea with rice in it, and an orange herbal Rooibos tea.

The Earl Gray was very mild and not bad. It doesn't even rank in the top ten Earl Grays that I have had, though. It's probably the best of the four teas that came in the box.

The Oolong Tea was pretty strong, musky, and smelled terrible. I turned it into iced tea to control some of the pungent aroma. When chilled, it's not bad as a sipping tea, but I certainly wouldn't want to try it again.

The Green Tea was pretty unremarkable. It was filled with grains of rice, which didn't add much of anything to the brew. I added some lemon and honey to make it more appealing.

The Blood Orange Roobios tea wasn't bad, but not nearly as tasty as most other herbal teas I've had. I think I'll pass on this one.

I went to their website to check out their Earl Gray tea, and noticed that it is more than TWICE the price of top-grade Earl Gray that I order directly from Assam, India. That is hilarious. It's clear they make their money on marking up unremarkable tea and selling it to their subscribers on the back end.

I cancelled my subscription immediately.

title: Stay Away, It Is Expensive And Awful
text:
I was so excited for this. I am currently toward the end of writing something I have been working on for three years so I opened this up like it was going to spring forth some golden light and writing fairies were going to come out handing me pens and stickers and little trinkets that I had never thought of.

But I got some hot chocolate. I can’t eat chocolate or sugar. So that was a waste.

I got some really ugly fabric thumbtacks from the couture collection. I like the idea. But these bright orange and black, crayola blue with halloween orange triangles all on a tiny pin for me to post on a wall of my work is never going to happen. They belong in a remainder pile somewhere. Oh wait, maybe that’s where they found them!

And then I got a coaster that looks like a record player but says, when you read it around in a circle “Replaying my thoughts and plots- Scribbler”. Not a bad idea but the coaster is made from a weird material. It feels awkward. I wouldn’t trust my hot drinks on this thing,

Then there was a small booklet that gave some help on writing. I quite liked that. It had some very good ideas.

There is an a button that says, “Ask Me About My Novel.” I have not yet become that pretentious. Nor do I ever plan too. And if I did, it wouldn’t be with a teal and bright yellow pin.

And lastly a book and a nametag with the writers name. It isn’t even written in the book. Quite odd.

If I was shown this beforehand and asked how much I would pay for it, my answer would be nothing. No thank you. I am not sure whether to try again or if this is truly what this has to offer. If so, I am horribly disappointed and would tell you to save your money.

That was my review for November and then lo and behold, I get another box for December even though I was sure I cancelled it. When I contacted the seller, they said they couldn’t accept returns because there is food in the box. So that is why you are getting that random child sized raise box this month!

And a fairly unattractive duo tone tote bag saying “Between the pages is a lovely place to be” with an open book and some black trees on it. Behind that there is a golden mountain in the background with lines flashing out like when kids draw a sun on pictures. Looks more like a warning than a welcoming picture. Again you can make these at zazzle or many places online. (worth $3.95 or less)

Then there is a twenty one page notebook about cliffhangers including an interview with the book writer and nine pages of dos and donts. For example, DO have compelling characters. DON’T drone on and on with description and a paragraph describing why. Felt a little pedantic to me but was probably just the format of the do’s and dont’s in capital letters and the simplicity of the message. But maybe it will be right on for some people. Who knows? The interview is fairly decent but can that information be found easily online by searching writing and cliffhangers basically.

The one pamphlet I did like was the “Inside Look” into the publishing process where they shared Charlie N. Holmberg’s story pitch for “Spellbreaker.”. That was interesting and helpful to read. All two and a half pages of it.

So, all in all I paid $41.50 ($39 plus tax) for what I could have gotten for $10.95 minus the three pages about on story pitch. But if you don’t have Kindle Unlimited like me and have to pay full price for the book, it would cost you $20.94. It’s reasonable to assume you could get the paperback for cheaper than $10.99 though.

Anyway, beyond just the cost of this was the excitement and wonder as had for this that was lost. I bought the November box as a birthday present for myself for my 47th birthday. It was beyond disappointing and I am always very unhappy when the sellers won’t even try to work with you especially when they send articles I am allergic too.

I have taken a picture so you can see for yourself. I want you to know what you are getting yourself into before you buy. Maybe you will love this! And then that will be great. Good on you.

But if it isn’t what you expected like me and if spending almost fifty dollars is a lot of money for you and something you try to spend cautiously then this box is not what you want to spend it on. Many blessings everyone!

title: Love the concept!
text:
People can complain that you might as well just print out these sort of things and organize them themselves are missing the point: you are paying for the convenience of all that being curated for you. I homeschool and have 5 kids, I've got enough to organize and coordinate every day, so I decided this would be one of the things I outsource. It prompts geography, history, and civics lessons for our laidback homeschool, the conversation cards are alot of fun to collect and pull out once in a while, and the recipes all have lots of great information about history of ingredients and other fun factoids.
COULD you pull this together yourself each month?
Absolutely.
Is the money worth the time, paper, ink, and cost of the little tool?
Also Absolutely in my opinion.
I will say as a Muslim family I was super disappointed with the very religious (witchcraft) theme for the most recent kit. I want comfortable just opening it up to go through without an advanced lesson on pagan spirituality, and I didn't subscribe for religious input. To balance this out I'm expecting to see a Ramadan kit come with lots of good recipes using dates!

For the price of $20 a month for 7 masks they would need to up the quality of their masks to masks that can be purchased for a total of $40-50 if I were to pick them out and buy individually. I feel that losing the ability to pick the masks myself and the fact that it's a subscription service so they can count on an income stream should offer a better value than what has been presented thus far in the masks. title: Important things to know if you subscribe through Amazon.
text:
If you subscribe through amazon.

1. it's easier to sign up and cancel.
2. Everything in the box must adhere to Amazons code of conduct, and thus some item will be different (inferior) to the ones in a regular batlbox.
3. Because of Amazons policy, Battle box must ship on the exact first day of the shipping window. To implement this you don't' get "this months" battlbox.You get whatever battle box they have handy, this months, last months 4 months ago (that's what i got) and there is no guarantee you will not get the same box twice. (took me about a week of repeatedly asking to get this answer)

for me #3 was the killer so i canceled through amazon and signed up straight through battlbox.

title: Very cool selection, but not good for folks with celiac
text:
Our bokksu was a neat collection of snacks that were a fun experiment. Some tasted good, even though they also tasted strange and unfamiliar. Others were just plain delicious. The Bokksu came from Japan fresh and in perfect condition and the child unit we did this for was thrilled. We lucked out and got a box (July 2019) where only four items had wheat, which we promptly handed to Dad. The rest was safe to eat. Unfortunately, looking forward one month and back one month, those boxes had almost all products with wheat and only a couple that didn’t have wheat. Since we have celiac, that makes this interesting cultural exploration not as useful. Guess we’ll make the rounds of the local Asian markets and see if we can make our own collections. Too bad, this is a fantastic idea. It’s also cool that they have a vegetarian option. I’d recommend this for those without an allergy to wheat. That said, another very useful feature is the booklet, which lists the common allergens in each snack.

title: Culinary Paint-by-Numbers
text:
I received a 4-month subscription to Blissful Bakes as a birthday gift. To say I was disappointed when the first box arrived is an understatement. Thankfully, my friends were able to cancel the remaining subscription through Amazon. So, what’s my problem with the product?

First: Pricing. The first month’s subscription is $25.00; subsequent months are $30.00. Yet the box I received contained less than $2.00 worth of ingredients. The box pictured online is artfully arranged with craft crinkle paper. The box I received showed no such care. The individual ingredients were stored in baggies, dumped into a box, and shipped.

Second: Quality of the recipes. This month’s offering is Lemon Oatmeal Crumb Bars. We all recognize that a good recipe has value. However, the recipe provided isn’t a Blissful Bakes proprietary recipe, but one that can be found all over the internet. It failed to meet my expectations given the price-point.

Third: Food safety. Flour, oats, and sugar each stored in generic kitchen baggies? Seriously? Under what conditions are these ingredients measured and dispensed? Do they use a certified kitchen? Has their staff taken food safety classes? The manner in which these ingredients are offered up is worrisome. I’m not comfortable using anything provided other than the can of sweetened condensed milk.

Fourth: The premise. You’re provided with the dry/shelf stable ingredients, and a basic and widely available internet recipe. You still have to provide your own butter, eggs, etc. You make the dessert and clean up afterwards. Save your money. Give Blissful Bakes a pass.

title: Great value, wonderful products,
text:
So, confession time: I ordered this box without realizing it was made with WOC in mind. I'm pretty white, so I considered cancelling, but I kept my order for a few reasons. For one, WOC have had to deal with boxes not made for them since the inception of subscription boxes, so who was I to whine about it not being made just for me. Second, I really believe in supporting concepts like this, obviously the world needs more. And third, of course, I was curious - what's in the box??

I have weird hair, it's thick and wavy/slightly curly, but has a second texture, a very kinky/wirey curl mixed in. These two types have a very hard time finding a pattern together. No one in my family has hair like mine, so as a kid I was on my own to figure out how to style it. I got teased a lot in school because it was so frizzy. Back in the day, before there were luxury hair and skin and cosmetic products in every major box store, products for hair like mine were hard to find. In middle school I started shopping in the "black hair" section (seriously, why is there a separate section?) and found products like Let's Jam (lol!) )worked for my texture. So that's what I used for years. Because of that I figured I would be able to use at least some of the items included.

As you can tell by the 5 stars above, the products were delightful.
First, I love that they came in a reusable tote instead of a box. I can always use a tote, I cannot use another box.
So to get to it, THE PRODUCTS:
I received. 4 Palmer's Cocoa & Biotin hair products. Shampoo, conditioner, leave in conditioner, and glaxe serum (totaling about $25 value) No mineral oil, no silicones, they make my hair feel soft and strong and shiny and help hold it's curl pattern with no stiffness or crunch. And they smell unbelievably good.
Next there was a travel atomizer of Michel Germain Paris Sexúal perfume, which I looooove (value $30).
Next was a container of Specific Beauty Dark Spot Lightening skin pads that I already am obsessing over. (90 count, very generous, $60 value, seriously). Kojic acid and bearberry, the ingredients are great.
Next was a really neat glass exfoliating disk. I've never seen one of these before, and I'm willing to bet they will be the next big thing. Very cool and modern concept and it left my skin baby bottom smooth. ($15 value, I believe) (edit: this evidently triggered my perioral dermatitis so I had to pass it on)
Then there was the Fleur and Bee Rose and Shine Rosewater toner spritz. Delightful and all natural. ($15?)
Also included was a Vitabath travel size set of shower gel and lotion. (maybe $10?)
Lastly, a few lovely samples rounded the bag out.
As you can see, this bag/box is easily worth $140 or more. Everything was made in the US or EU. High quality natural ingredients. Such an amazing value and I'm sure I will use every single product until they're done. Wonderful experience, thanks to the people who put this together. It really felt like it was made with love.

When I decided to try out a plant subscription, I chose Costa Farms because it seemed like the best “deal” and would be something I enjoyed, even after the price jump after the first box.

When the first box arrived, both of my “O2” plants were the same plant, not a deal breaker, but disappointing none the less. That shipment came with a total of 3 plants (2 Arrowhead and 1 torch cactus). It was missing the “free watering can” that was promised. An email to the company was replied to very quickly stating that they had run out of them and one would be shipped in my next subscription. Cool, I can wait a month, no big deal. A few weeks later, I received an email letting me know they had the watering cans back in stock and I should expect one in my next order. Cool, I like the communication!

However, today my second subscription box arrived and guess what WASN’T in the box?! You guessed it, no watering can. Now, they did send 4 plants this time (2 very small cacti; ball and bieblii, a coffee plant and a corn plant)….all very pretty and I do love them, but having now paid almost $40 and not received what is probably a 30¢ plastic water cup is very disappointing and I will likely be canceling this subscription to find a more trust worthy company to exchange money with. title: OK depending on what you’re looking for
text:
TL;DR: the comics you get are NOT worth double the price as claimed by the seller but the subscription is fairly priced after considering costs involved in shipping and curating comics. Cheaper alternatives include TPBs and subscriptions from the publisher.

What I asked for: Daredevil, Batman, Superman

What I got: 2 outstanding Daredevil comics, #3 of 5 from a random Batman miniseries, a dollar bin Superman comic (Action Comics #999), the rest were B- and C- list comics including a comic that literally said “free” because it was a free comic book day issue.

Shipping: comics are not individually bagged and boarded but rather stacked together and shrink wrapped. As a result there is a minimum amount of creasing around the corners and spine, not enough to affect aesthetic appeal but collectors know even the smallest imperfections can have a significant impact on a comic’s value.

Value: based on previous sales on eBay, the comics I received were worth ~$14. I consider the subscription to be a fair price after considering the costs involved in shipping and having someone curate the comics for you, but by no measure (cover price or market value) were the comics worth “double the subscription cost” as claimed by comic garage.

Alternatives: if you want to read good comic stories, TPBs are among the cheapest way to do so. If you want comics with your favorite characters mailed to you monthly in an ongoing series, you can subscribe to ~12-18 different comic series direct from Marvel or DC for the price of a Comic’s Garage subscription over the course of the year. If you want to be surprised by a collection of random comics each month, Comics Garage might be for you.

title: Loyal customer for over a year
text:
I have been getting beauty boxes for over a year and a half. Every single box has things I love and things that I never knew I needed in my life. Anything I didn't like I gave away to my makeup fanatical friends which were received with absolute joy. I haven't had an issue up until now.
April 2020 box was a disaster! The LUE by Jen Seo Hydrating & Calming serum had leaked all over the box. There was almost no serum left. This wouldn't initially make me mad or upset. Things happens and accidents happen. My issue is that I have over the last few weeks have reached out to the seller to resolve the issue. I haven't heard anything back from the seller This is very annoying and makes me wonder if they actually care to retain customers. I would give them less than a two star review if this wasn't a singular incident in a year plus worth of non-issue. I will happily update the stars once my issue is resolved or even acknowledged

***UPDATE***
They finally replied to my email and have said they are sending me a new box as a replacement. I will continue to update you as things happen. Also I will update the stars once I get my replacement. For now one will do since I haven't gotten a replacement yet.

***UPDATE 2***
I have now received the May 2020 box but nothing as fa as a replacement box as promised. I will be patient and expect in the next week or so my replacement as promised. I will not be adding any stars. If I don't get my box as promised I will have no other option than to take away more stars. If in the event a replacement is received I will happily update the stars and update my review.

***UPDATE FINAL***
All stars returned! They followed through with their promise to replace my box! I am super stoked that the box was in my mail today. It came a lot quicker than I had imagined. I am glad to give a five star review. I have been above and beyond happy about the end results. I have had over a year of goodness from this company and was distressed by radio silence for a long time. title: Nope. Was not impressed x4
text:
Dec-2020: So read the reviews from last month which weren't the greatest---unflattering shirt color with a kind of not-so-cool comic graphic. But I'm a big Marvel fan so I figured why not. Well, I received my first order-- a black t-shirt (not my fav color, but fine), ordered a size up because Marvel stuff tends to run small/shrink (..and the collar was still too tight), decal featured Deadpool (cool/fun artwork), ...but it was a Christmas themed shirt. Now it's my own personal preference, but I would never waste $20 on a Christmas themed t-shirt--- essentially you're purchasing something you'll only wear for less than two month's out of year. As for quality, the shirt size was adequate, but the collar is a bit on the smaller side--was thankful that I ordered a size up, but still ended up disappointed. As for the graphic itself-- feels a bit rubbery-- not sure the print/decal would last more than a year's worth of washings. So ended up returning my first shirt for a refund --mostly because of the Christmas theme. I'll give the club a couple more opportunities to impress, but I must say it's not looking very promising.

Jan-2021 Update: Another black shirt [which I'm not a fan of] with an obscure graphic [I'm a huge Marvel fan, but just kinda passive when it comes to the Guardians' series. So a picture of Knowhere just doesn't do it for me.] Again, shirt one-size-up and quality were adequate. Rubbery iron-on/decal still feels weird. Definitely won't last more than a year of regular wear. Regardless, I'm still not impressed-- mostly just not into the color or graphic--sooo-- another return. 2-for-2 on returns. And yes, shipping was a bit late, but I don't fault Amazon for that. I think it's just the world we live in right now.

Feb-2021 Update: Another black shirt [which did I mention, I'm not a fan of?!]. Is a white or light gray/heather not an option? The Black Panther graphic is just ok-- I would have liked something a bit cooler--bigger claws and teeth, some shreds, a roar?--a more viscous looking character/panther. Sooo-- another return. 3-for-3 on returns.

Mar-2021 Update: OMG!! I think this is the ugliest color I have ever seen!! And the graphic?--What was Marvel thinking?!! I mean the graphic itself is ok at best, but it is barely visible on the ugliest colored shirt. Might have been viable on a light colored or white shirt-- Not a dark, puke green color. Oh wait.. sorry... it's called "Grass"... smh. So maybe Marvel thought green for St Patty's day would be cool? Umm ok fine. So most normal folks would think..green? Well then, why not Hulk? Nope! Not even close. I think this shows extreme laziness on Marvel's part--I bet you couldn't get $5 for this ugly shirt in a department store. So now we're 4-for-4 on returned shirts. I'm out. Done. Sorry Marvel, you failed miserably on this one... and lost a customer.

title: Our favorite dog subscription
text:
I don’t agree with the one star reviews upset about the value. My dog is a big boy and a tough chewer and started shredding plush toys in minutes, which made his “other” box a REAL waste of money. (I also hate how much throw away plastic goes into dog toys.) So I switched him over to natural/ingestible chews and we are much happier. Sure this stuff is not cheap, but he is satisfied and doesn’t chew shoes or furniture or any other costly items! I have sourced quality dried trachea, tendons, bully sticks, etc, from a local vendor and they just aren’t that cheap. From what I’ve been able to find (check tendons on Chewy), I think the price of this box isn’t bad. I do wish there was more in the bag, but that’s because we run out before the month is up. Roscoe likes the variety of items.

For those hesitant about the hooves, I use them like a Kong and stick a little soft treat or something in the tippy toe. You can freeze stuff in there, too. Roscoe doesn’t love the hoof alone but he chews on it for a good long time if I get him started with a little something in it.

title: Changing my rating to one star
text:
Edited to add on July 7, 2019:
Subscription cancelled and I am reducing my 4 star rating to one star because I went to their website and looked at the cost of each of the chews sold separately and the total cost would be $15.72 plus flat rate shipping $7, so total cost would be $22.72. The first box was a good price and being able to try a variety of their chews was nice, but seeing how they could be bought separately for less than the $29.99 it would cost each month, the subscription box is not at all a good value.

Original review:
They advertise 7 different types of chews per box, and 7-15 total chews per box. I am now assuming looking at the card insert and photo in the product description that boxes for large dogs cost more because some of the chews are larger and it is assumed they’ll consume more chews each month so they get more per box.

I ordered the small size box for dogs under 20 lbs, and did receive 7 different types of treats (all 7 of the varieties shown for small dogs on the card the sent, see pic), and a total of 9 treats (see pics... they came in 3 bags... two of the bags had 3 different types of chews and the third bag contained the 2 large pig skins).

They appear to be high quality chews and my 2 dogs went nuts at the smell of the box, they knew it was something for them as I opened the box and tried to take the first pic! Because we received 2 pig skins I gave them each one and because they were so large I planned on taking them away after a few minutes so they could enjoy them over several days (I usually do with that large chews)... and about 3 minutes later they had each already devoured half of their chew! Apparently they love those chews so much they are whining about having them taken away (sorry, pups... but those are too large for you to gobble up in a matter of minutes)! I should mention my dogs are both about 2 years old and 12-15 lbs... one’s a Scottie/Yorkie, the other a chi/dox... both with long narrow mouths, and neither have been aggressive chewers... but they went nuts for those pig skins like I’ve never seen before!

That said... I am cancelling our subscription because 5 of the kinds of chews we only received one chew (pig skins and beef esophagus strap 2 each)... but with 2 dogs I need to give them each the same thing or they’ll want whatever the other has. Also, the chews are rather large for our dogs’ small mouths, the puff braid is supposed to be small size but it’s so large they’d have a hard time chewing it (they’d probably try... but possibly it’d harm a small mouth... I may give that chew away to a friend’s larger dog). Yes, larger chews can last several days, but I don’t want them eating a large chew all at once and then when I take their chews away I always feel guilty.

I possibly would not be cancelling our subscription if there were double the number of chews that were half the sizes for smaller dogs. 5 stars for the flavor of the pig skins (only thing they’ve tried so far, will lower the rating if they really dislike a different chew), but I’d rate 3 1/2 stars overall for my dogs as I don’t feel the larger sizes of the most of the chews are appropriate for a dog under 20 lbs.

title: Funko seems to not care, Amazon is clueless. But the items are still exclusive and Pops!
text:
Funko is not listening to their fans, and they’ve basically washed their hands and say it’s all Amazon now. With regards to the huge debacle that was the Dagobah box, Amazon has no clue how the subscription works as evidenced by numerous posts regarding this. I reached out to Funko, and received the below response.

Funko Support (Funko)
Mar 4, 2:47 PM PST

Hi Richard,

I understand your frustration with the Amazon subscriptions. Unfortunately, we cannot assist with orders through Amazon, since they are an independent distributor. We know that Amazon's customer support encompasses the countless number of products they offer, so individual agents may not have in-depth knowledge of how their company processes these subscriptions.

If supplies are limited, that is a concern that Amazon must handle with their distributor contact or supply chain management, so it is disappointing to hear that they are pointing you to us, when we handle issues related to purchases made through the Funko Shop.

And while we do not have any insight into Amazon's system, our best guess is that next month's box is shown on Amazon's website, leading their customers to believe that they will not receive the current month's box, or that there is a delay in shipment. For example, a February box expected to ship in April or May.

For further support with your subscription account, we encourage you to reach back out to Amazon and see if they can put you in contact with a representative that has more insight into their Smugglers Bounty boxes.

Best regards,
Maca with Funko Support

Now...with regards to content, well...it has gone down. I’ve been a subscriber to Smugglers Bounty since it’s introduction when it was done directly by Funko. So I have tons of pins and patches, t-shirts or hats, even socks and wrist bands etc. The box quality has declined, we used to get art specific to the theme on the box, now it’s just not the same.

Specific to the “Dagobah” theme now: SPOILERS!

A movie moment...okay, these aren’t always popular, they’re large and hard to display. Especially if you have to look down to see them. I’m not usually disappointed in them, but I was this time mostly because we literally just got a movie moment from “Empire” when we got the Cloud City box. So to receive another movie moment was disappointing. The mystery mini HAD to be who it was or else we wouldn’t have gotten him at all. So many things they could’ve done with Yoda!

Overall the box isn’t the same as when Funko distributes the box themselves. We haven’t had a wearable since Amazon took over. I really wish Funko would listen/read the reviews and see what fans are missing and wanting. I personally love Star Wars, and I do enjoy having exclusive items you can’t find in stores. So I keep buying, but the dollar doesn’t always stretch as much as it used to.
