title: Very Impressed
text: I was very tempted by this subscription box based on the description that Amazon provided. For reference, I do not have any other box subscriptions, so it is not a temptation I give into easily. I was absolutely tickled by every item I got in my first box. Everything is well made and of the quality that's appropriate for the price. I noticed a couple of reviewers complaining about low quality, but folks, I have bought hair accessories from Anthropologie and Evita Peroni - just because you are paying above average price and there is extra attention to detail does not mean that the items will not break, pieces will not fall off, and the construction is convenient, easy to use and won't damage hair. Hair accessories work hard - they get in the sun, they get a ton of oils and products on them, they move with every step and beat around in boxes full of other metal, plastic, and stone items. If you're lucky, they last a long time and look good doing it. That part remains to be seen, as I have only just gotten my subscription and have only worn everything once or twice. But so far, the quality is actually impressive for most items I received (good construction, noticeable extra steps taken to ensure longevity and appeal of product), and average (cheap feeling, but acceptable) for one of them. I am so excited about my next box. This is not a subscription that I plan to keep long term, instead I think of it as a way of enriching my collection of hair accessories until I have enough.

I know it doesn’t sound like it over all I am happy with the subscription. I have no plans to cancel it. I continue to look forward to the next box, though at this point who knows what it will be or when it will arrive.

People if the box is going to be late send the email. In a month if its going to continue to be late send an email. If it continues to be late send another email just so we are aware that you haven’t forgotten about us.

title: Decent box as long as you aren't expecting too much...
text:
Pros:
1. Really cute themes every month
2. Good variety of toys (nylon, rubber, etc) and you can customize how much of each kind you get by
contacting customer service. You can also customize to have a "toys only" box if you aren't interested in
treats
3. Great customer service in general
4. Good price for the number and quality of toys

Cons:
1. Hard nylon toys should ONLY be given to puppies - that way if they crack a tooth it isn't a permanent one.
As a general rule of thumb, if you can't make at least a small indent with your fingernail, it is too hard for
adult teeth. They really shouldn't be encouraging people to give rock-hard nylon toys to adult dogs.
2. If you have a dog that is over 75 lbs then this is not the box for you. The toys in the "large" size box were
on the small side for my GSD and are a full-on choking hazard for my mastiff. They should have an option
for giant breeds or they should explicitly state that when they ask you for your dog's breed, that they
aren't actually using that to choose the toy size - every dog in the large size box gets the same toys
regardless of whether they are a 60 lb collie or a 200 pound mastiff. It's extremely misleading for them to
ask what breed you have and then send everyone the same size toys anyway.
3. Their rubber toys are not nearly as heavy duty as kong or bullymake rubber toys. For true super chewers I
would choose bullymake. I have both subscriptions and I find that while barkbox is okay for my GSD, the
toys they provide are entirely unsafe, and not nearly durable enough, for my mastiff.

Conclusion:
I will keep getting this box for a couple of months because it has a nice selection of toys for my GSD and my smaller mixed-breed. However, they really should be offering a size up from the large box - I would say the toys in the large box would be more accurately described as being for medium-sized dogs like collies, smaller labs, and spaniels. The attached picture is of the rubber toy they sent after approximately 10 minutes with my mastiff (who isn't even full grown yet). The tail was ripped off by my GSD about 20 minutes after I took this picture. The whole things was in the garbage after about 45 minutes when I caught my mastiff eating pieces of the rubber. However, I will say that my experience with customer service was great and they sent out a replacement toy immediately, so no complaints there.

I can't even cancel my "automatic payments" until my 6 month subscription has ended.
I know my brother had his best intentions in giving me this, but I can guarantee I will never get this for anyone as I'd be embarrassed for them to have to give their credit card information for a gift.
The only reason I could see a company using a system like this is that they don't believe in their own product and wouldn't expect people to continue their subscription without hoping they are too lazy to cancel their payment.

title: Great way to passively introduce coding and math
text:
If you have an advanced 1st grader this is about the perfect amount of challenge for them to tackle. The box requires young learners to learn the keyboard and lessor used keys which is a skill learned much later. It gets students used to x/y axis, functions, if/then, critical thinking (if you do the challenge), creativity, and a good preview of how code is written. These skills are all way early so the box doesn’t need to explain what a function is or go into detail about how x represents the horizontal movement. It shows them and now they have a concrete example in their heads for when they are shown the maths behind it.
My learner quickly caught on, adjusting the first value would move the stamp left or right.
The best part is that after we did a section he wanted to make his own without the guides.
This is an almost perfect box. The only downside here is that the introduction just ends. It doesn’t say begin card # 1 or anything. It just ends. Also 2 apps on the first kit don’t have a card. They are hidden on the tricks and tips card. So they need to redo the directions and intro but certainly keep the part where you throw the kids right into coding. It’s something they will pick up by doing.
Would love to see more challenge cards too.

title: SUPER hit or miss. Every time.
text:
Some of the stuff is really cool and practical! So far in my boxes, I've got a SandBar, a waterproof bluetooth speaker, some nice (women's) tank tops. Resistance bands! Books on squat technique! A handy fanny-pack type thing!

Some of it, I can't figure out. Why did I get a box of ginger tea & a container of tequila-lime seasoning this month?? What does that have to do with fitness?

Some of it is just random stuff with a brand name. LVFT fleece headbands -- yes, I can get the exact same thing at the literal dollar store, with no brand. So far, I have received two. Yet I only have one head.

But the problem for me is the stuff I get that I would never, ever ask for. Examples:

I am a vegetarian, but I keep getting boxes with beef jerky sticks. No option in my profile to mention dietary preferences; which is one thing for me, but what about people with food intolerances (they send peanut butter!) or religious restrictions??

Another example: I don't appreciate the pandering to me, as a female, with fancy smelly sprays and scented wipes and "face refreshing spray" -- seriously? I want what the guys got (you often get different items if your box is for male or female). And maybe the guys wanted the fancy smelly wipes. But Gainz doesn't ask, they just assume. Why did I get whey powder this month and the guys got pre-workout?? Huh???

I think the last straw was getting a unisex tshirt (from Hybrid Performance). In the account profile, you specify not just size but, as I mentioned, also gender, so that you can get the fit you want. Are you a girl who likes longer, looser tshirts? Go with a guys size. Are you a guy who wants flowy tank tops? You can choose a girls size. So WHY are we getting unisex anything? We pay a premium to get premium cuts, not the run-of-the-mill cuts. And, I did a little digging -- Hybrid Performance DOES make women's cut shirts...just not the one Gainz Box sent. Hmm.

My subscription is halted until I can see spoilers in time to decide each month if I actually want what they're sending anymore. Going in blind is only worth it if you can use a BOGO code -- look for those on social media -- that way, if only half the stuff in each box is good, at least you got a full box worth of good stuff. :)

The good: The decal gave me a chuckle. The beanie isn’t too horrendously ugly, so there’s that.

The bad: the shirt and socks look poorly sewn and I’m pretty sure sneezing while wearing either will cause them to rip. The plush looks cheap, like a toy you’d get outta a $0.50 claw machine.

The ugly: the mug came chipped. The box was not in an external box nor did it have any kind of protection.

If I’d paid $30 for this, I’d feel I got ripped off. But having paid $60 it makes me wish Culture Fly would’ve at least bought me dinner first and told me I was pretty before screwing me like this.

Very disappointed. I guess that Marvel collectors corps and Star Wars Bounty Hunter box I was given for Christmas and my birthday last year had me expecting something WORTH sixty bucks. Next time I’ll just burn the money to light a pipe and give myself cancer instead. That’d been a better waste of money.

title: Cosmetic Formulation Chemist: half thrown away every month.
text:
Their products are a mixed bag of poor formulas and dried out products. I’ve subscribed since their first box (2014?) and the quality has gone from 50% potential for allure beauty award and 50% start-up/ new launch, to 90% products that were likely given to them for free and 10% new launches.

The last box, when the price hike started, included a vitamin C (LAA) powder that the ‘editor’ claimed could ‘be added into your daily moisturizer’ (so does the company). Of course it isn’t done BG anything to your skin, because it’s NOT DOING ANYTHING FOR YOUR SKIN. first I’m a cosmetic formulation chemist, and that’s not how to make an efficacious L-Ascorbic Acid formula:

LAA is EXTREMELY pH dependent, even if your DRY formula contained a manically powder pH buffer, you cannot accurately dose out 2-3 ‘shakes’ to make an effective serum, not to mention adding it to moisturizer (FOR THE LOVE OF SCIENCE DO NOT DO THIS). This is beyond stupid, it’s potentially dangerous and Allure is backing this; If Amazon rejects this review because of this, they are too.

Anyone who has a problem with properly formulated LAA serums, please try Vitamin C’s other forms: magnesium ascorbyl phosphate, Ascorbyl Tetraisopalmitate, sodium ascorbyl palmitate, ascorbyl glucoside, 3-0-Ethyl Ascorbate and a few others that can be stable and effective in a properly formulated moisturizer.

I keep expecting Allure to return to quality, but every month it’s another amateur selection touting the virtues of the flaws like they are shining a turd. I’m tired of all the waste, I throw half my box away every month. Unfortunately, I paid for a yearly subscription before the price increase, so another 11 boxes to go.

title: Extra Fresh Teas From a Company Who Cares
text:
Simple Loose Leaf Tea subscription at Amazon features impeccably fresh teas from a company who truly cares. All teas are ethically and sustainably sourced. All materials used in the production of their products are USA small and local company based; with the exception of some of the teas themselves. They feature everything from mellow and fresh herbal teas to genuine and high quality green teas imported from ancient tea farms in Japan. Additionally, much of the labor provided in the creation and assemblage of their monthly subscription packages are conducted by the differently abled.
This is a positive and healthy, pro-active way of supplying your quality tea beverage needs, while supporting employment in American supply companies with an eye toward fair labor practices and equal access for the developmentally disabled. I can't think personally of a better way to feel good about my tea indulgences. Very highly recommended.

I have signed up for the 5-7 age group. The toy being shipped says it's for 8+ The set looks simple enough but the colored instructions seem pretty complicated for a 6 YO. The product is: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01KZQZHE2/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

So I just looked up the product online. The product is selling for $28 right now on Amazon so at first you think you're getting a good deal at $20 a month, but I see this product was being sold on Nov 7, 2016 for $17 on Amazon. I'm having serious doubts about this program right now as it looks like I'm getting a product that is not in my son's age group and I'm not getting a particularly good deal on it. I'm thinking now it's better to pick and choose your own STEM toys to make sure you're getting the right age group and a good price.

title: Great first box but...
text:
I've tried almost all of the tea subscriptions out there currently and although this was actually a pretty decent first box (would make a great gift), ultimately this sub is far too expensive for what you receive (in terms of the tea).
This box came with 5 teas in bags, 1 tea in a tin, plus an extra (1 tea bag) "sample" tea. As well as a card describing the teas (the ones that arrived bagged), a recipe for a Mock Mint Green Tea Julep, a bookmark, a small(ish) notepad, and a sachet dish. I believe (although I could be wrong), the sachet dish that came in this box is an extra item that comes only in the first box.
The 5 teas in bags, contained only 2 tea bags each for a total, including the sample, of 11 tea bags and a small tin of tea. The first cup with a tea bag took quite awhile (longer than the recommended 3-5 minutes) to get a even a fair amount of color and flavor of tea, into the water. I tried re-using the tea bags, as stated in the description (2-3 cups per bag) with very little success. The second (I wouldn't even dare try a third) cup of tea, I let each bag steep overnight, and never did get even close to the first cups' amount of tea into the water. In other words....I was only able to get one satisfactory cup of tea out of each tea bag. Now as I previously stated, I have tried just about every tea subscription out there and I ALWAYS reuse my teas to make two, three and sometimes even four cups each time but I was not able to get even close to that, out of these teas. Granted, I have only tried three of the teas in one monthly box but, in terms of the tea alone, I certainly didn't feel like I had gotten my moneys worth.
This sub seems to be about more than just the tea itself though and if you are in it for the extra(s) as much as the tea itself, you may find it to be worth your money. Though it just wasn't for me.
Thank you for your time. Hope you are well.

I thought that given his advanced skill sets and curiosity, it would be an engaging, exciting present.  But my sister told me he was so frustrated with the materials after the second box, to just go ahead and cancel it.  She said it requires a skill set and level of concentration 3-year-olds just don't possess and that if he were a couple of years older it would have been perfect.  My own former 3-year-olds are much older now, but from the way my sister described the box's contents (vs. the description), I'd agree.  My overall consensus is, it's probably a fun box for older kids, but maybe wait another year (or two) before buying this for your 3-year-old.

title: Everyone has an opinion-Don't let others make up your mind for you.
text: I have heard and read many reviews upset over the first run of the collector's corps through Amazon.  I was a member of collector's core for about year with Funko before it switched to Amazon.  Is it different now? Yes. Are there items found in the Funko version missing from the Amazon version? Yes. Should you subscribe anyway? Depends on you.  For me I am happy with the FIRST box.  These boxes are a suprise each time and filled with items that I cannot or usally would not find in my normal day to day shopping experience.  I am a collector like many others who subscribe. I focus mainly on Marvel legends figures and have Pop! as a side collection. I enjoy the idea that each box will have a custom one of a kind Pop! in each box. I like knowing that I have something in my collection( as small as it is approx. 50 or less Pop figures) that others cannot have without a subscription.  So to me I enjoy the suprise and the value of this subscription. I don't see this as a way to beat the system and circumvent capitalism. These boxes cannot be sold at  a loss and continue. There must be some sort of profit. Otherwise the toys and collectables we all love will cease to exist. So I do feel that this is a good value and something to look forward to every other month. I encourage you to try it and see for yourself. Some months are far better than others (my bruce banner/Hulk two in one Pop! being one of my all time favorites) but overall they are fun to collect.  Besides if you get something in the box you don't like or enjoy give to a child in your life.  They tend to be much less picky about toys than the adults posting here.

title: Initial impression wasn't good, but the seller is making things right
text:
After seeing a video online for this service, I decided to give it a try. I just received my first box, but it was underwhelming. This is what I received:

Standard PC AC cable
Molex to SATA power adapter cable
80GB SATA 1 hard drive
PCI based modem card
Excelius retractable cleaning brush

The parts were packaged well and included a handwritten manifest of the parts that were given.

I realize it is a mystery box and what you get will be different every month and different than what someone else gets, but the claim that every box contains $55 or more of parts is not accurate based on my first box. At best I’d say $15 tops. The only item of any value is the hard drive, but at only 80GB and SATA 1 it is only good for use with older systems and laptops...fine for Windows XP or 7. That’s really about a $10 used part based on prices on the bay. The rest of the parts I got were “meh”. The cleaning brush is nice but I’m sure it costed them maybe $1 each to have a bulk order of them purchased with their company name put on them. I’ll see what comes in the next box a month from now as I want to see if it is going to be crap again or if it will have some better parts worth more than what I paid. So far, not even close. I like the thrill of a mystery box, but it better live up to claim that there’s $55 or more in value. I’ll update my review either way to help those of you wondering if this is a good deal or not.

UPDATE 2020-01-27: I reported the problem to the seller, and I was contacted almost immediately after that. The seller gave me a partial refund. He explained that I should have received much better items than I did and that for my next box he would personally ensure I receive items that meet what is promised in the product description. I bumped up one star for great customer service. I will review again after I received my next box.

UPDATE 2020-02-27: The box I received was better in February. There was a functional 500GB SATA hard drive, a Chromebook (parts only), an Excelius wallet tool (very cool), and HP rechargeable laptop battery, and an HP motherboard. The motherboard has some bent cpu socket pins, but I might be able to repair it. I'm not sure what I can do with the battery and Chromebook, but at least the LCD of the Chromebook looks like it may be working. I will report-out again in March on the quality of that box.

UPDATE 2022-03-29: Boxes got really good for the most part over a year. Then the box I received Feb 2022 had nothing but junk...literally maybe $10 worth of parts. There was no list of parts as there normally is, and the box did not have the Excelius label on it. Then a week ago my subscription was canceled. I did not initiate canceling it either. The service was great IMO this past year...not sure what the heck is going on now, but I'm not happy now.

title: Bit of a letdown
text:
I hunted for a subscription box service for my honeschooled 9 year old that would give him some screen free entertainment and learning outside of our usual routine. I watched several youtube videos of several STEM boxes before deciding to purchase this one, primarily sold on it based on the fact that it was discounted, and I felt it was a low-risk way to see how we felt about it before committing to a full year.

The box arrived ahead of schedule, which was exciting, but was already smaller than anticipated, because all of the unboxing videos and advertisements showed this kit coming in a durable tin lunchbox style case, and advertised that the first box would include a canvas bag... not a huge let down, but misleading and also detracts from the overall calue of the contents.

Upon opening the box, my kid and I were both underwhelmed. Included was a booklet describing the contents, the "Who Was" series book about Frank Lloyd Wright, a black and white postcard, which was ripped on one edge, 3 Wonder Crate Heroes cards, and a sample of a construction toy kit that was simple cardboard shapes and plastic clips. I paid $22 (at a discount) , and recieved a $6 book, $1 worth of trading cards, a 50c postcard and what amounts to at most, a $3 craft kit.

I will not be continuing my subscription.

title: good and bad
text: I've only received one of these, and I currently don't think it's worth it as a subscription to me, but it certainly wasn't all bad. I got some kind of citrus-themed box. Now, citrus is not one of my favorite flavor types, though I don't hate it, either. So, this boxed was a mixed bag for me. There were some absolutely amazing lemon cookies, which I was not able to find online when I went to see if I could buy just them anywhere. There was a filled bun thing that was pretty good, too. There were other things that I tasted and tossed without finishing. There was definitely a lot of variety in products, which was nice, and the pamphlet explaining things was helpful. But for me, there were maybe two items that were really good, at least three or four which I didn't care for at all, and some others that were interesting and not too bad but nothing amazing. Now, if it had been a chocolate-themed box, it might have been entirely different. For $40/month, it's just not worth the gamble to me. I'd probably buy it if I could buy individual boxes that interested me, rather than the random sub thing, but for $40/month, that's too much money for me to want to bet on the curated randomness (random to me) of this sub box. But if you're a lot more open to different foods and really enjoy lots of different things, maybe it'll be more worth it to you. It definitely looked well put together.

title: Don't buy this.
text:
Was gifted this for Christmas. You get 4 kinds of cheap tea that make a weak 2-3 cups each (if you requested loose). They're selling what should be free samples for $16. Don't fall for this guys. It's a borderline scam.

What I got:
A Hallows Eve flavored tea that only made 2 cups because most of the sample bag was a big hunk of apricot.
A roasted yerba mate. I like yerba mate as well as anyone but I can literally buy 2kg of better for $16. And the amount was so stingy.
A masala chai tea made with CTC black. CTC black is possibly the cheapest black tea on the market.
A green tea blend that seems to be mostly apple pieces. I also like flavored teas as much as anyone but apple pieces are cheaper by weight than tea leaves so getting a stingy sample full of apple pieces is a let down.

There's many, many tea websites that will sell you a nice, hefty sample of high quality tea for $4. There's nothing Or, for equivalent quality, you can head to a grocery store for equivalent quality, pick up 4 boxes, and have tea for the month.

title: Clever way to learn programming
text:
Bitsbox is a clever, well-designed program to teach an actual programming language. We stopped our subscription after the 4th installment and have no regrets for trying it out.

What We Like About Bitsbox:
* Kids are learning a programming language with real-world applicability
* Beautifully designed materials delivered in a box that lights up our kids' eyes when it shows up
* Step-by-step instructions about how to develop each app
* A unique QR code technique to transfer an app from a web browser to a mobile device
* Includes extra material for parents, encouraging engagement together

Concerns:
* Having to use a text-based editor instead of a visual programming interface is, in our opinion, a limitation. If a child has good typing skills, this is less of a deal--and it might not be a problem for you. I've just seen how they engage longer in visual programming environments. And if they're preparing for something like Mindstorms, learning in a visual environment with blocks is a helpful thing to get used to.
* There are other ways to learn programming that are free. Personally, I think Bitsbox is a little overpriced for the value in comparison to other options. However, there are a couple different pricing options on the website that we didn't catch onto when we started.

Our bottom-line:
Our 9 year old prefers MIT's Scratch. It has a visual programming interface, it's fun, and you can take someone else's program and "see inside it", which is to say "you can learn from their code". You can re-mix someone else's program, which is an interesting learning technique. And she enjoys the community aspect of Scratch.

Our 7 year old prefers Bitsbox! Despite his just typing in what he's seeing in the code provided, he enjoys the games and when we work together on Bitsbox projects, I think he's picking up on some little things.

Where Bitsbox shines is the step-by-step learning process, which is not nearly as strong with Scratch. If you don't mind the Bitsbox subscription fee, do both! The key is that the kids ultimately find that programming is fun and engaging.

UPDATE: My 7 year old wanted to jump back into Bitsbox this week. We started tweaking a game and came across a coding issue we couldn't solve. I sent a support email to Bitsbox and literally less than 5 minutes, someone got back to us with a clarifying question. We answered the question, she reviewed the code, and replied promptly explaining the issue in a way we could understand, with an offer for further help. So impressive! I'll suggest that's why Bitsbox may be worth paying for. Good job, Bitsbox! I wish I could share the name of the person who provided the great support but I'm pretty sure it's against Review policy guidelines. But thank you!

title: Treat yourself!
text:
After having flowers for nearly two months (birthday and anniversary are a few weeks apart), I missed the splash of life in my dreary windowless office when the last of them died. As with anything else, I headed to Amazon to look for a solution. Bloomsybox looked like the perfect match and was offering a discount. I purchased a three month subscription and received my first bouquet a couple of weeks later.

Despite being in the middle of a winter storm with sub zero temperatures, the flowers arrived in excellent condition, with just some bruised guard petals on the roses. I was impressed with the mix of varieties and colors. While the roses started to die a few days later, the rest of the bouquet held up well. Every few days I trimmed the stems, changed the water and removed any dying material. It was nearly four weeks later before I finally threw away the last of the greenery.

My second bouquet arrived on time and in even better condition than the first. The roses in this arrangement lasted a solid two weeks before they started to droop and three weeks before enough had died that I threw it away. The photo is this second bouquet at two weeks old.

My third bouquet was scheduled to be delivered over our Christmas holiday but Bloomsybox let me delay the delivery so I’ll be receiving it after I return to work.

While it may be a bit of an indulgence, I’ve loved having fresh flowers in my house office and plan to continue to treat myself periodically. I would unequivocally recommend it as a gift to any flower lover in your life.

I only have one minor complaint. The description and their website say you’ll get care information with the flowers and I didn’t. While it was easy enough to look up the flower varieties and care online, it was a little annoying to expect to have it included and then not get it.

title: I'm a fan of the idea but not the execution
text:
I purchased the discounted first month of one of these boxes (the February 2020 Cupid's box) to try out. I agree with others that $24 a month is a lot for what you get, but I would be willing to look past this, factoring in not just the items you receive, but the amount of time you'd have to invest in putting something similar together.

However...

In two of the three recipes, we had to make significant adjustments. Not just for taste preference (way too much salt called for in one), but for practical purposes. As an example... the muffin recipe that came with this was the consistency of wallpaper paste 'as is'. Had to add liquid to thin it down enough to be able to add the chocolate chips and raspberries (which would have been a total mess to try to mix in otherwise). So for me, if the recipes can't be used as written, what's the point?

I did agree to give this one more shot, so time will tell.

Also on the negative side... not only do you not receive the apron by going to Amazon route, you don't have a way to create an account on the Raddish Kids site. It just seems like this could have been better thought out.

Update March 2021: Well after having been a subscriber for a few months, I must say I have mixed reviews. The shirts are good quality and sized to fit pretty accurately. The designs are mostly great , ( I have only had one design I did not like.) however the printing quality is kinda sloppy. The Deadpool shirt came in with printing blotch on the bottom of the design, and the Knowhere shirt design was awesome but mine was printed crooked. However the X men shirt and the latest Black Panther shirt have been perfect. However they have been great about returns as well , either for quality or for just not liking the design. All in all I really like the subscription but, think they could make it better simply by giving the ability to get a replacement for shirt that has a problem, now you can send it back , but you cant just get a replacement. Making a batch of extra shirts would solve this problem and not make Amazon have to refund so many mistakes, just replace it. title: Survived my terrible terrors - good quality for the cost
text:
[[VIDEOID:fe0c4c07f36943a946ffd89ec196329b]] (In short, good toys, I’m happy with them, though I can imagine a few cats not being as interested as mine are.)

As someone who fosters a lot of cats (and has a couple long-term residents), I figured getting toys every month would be nice if only to send them home with the fosters when they go to their new furever families. $20 for 4-5 toys isn’t too bad considering good quality toys at a pet store usually cost around that much. So I went on over to the KitNipBox site and subscribed, asking them to replace any treats with another toy (since cats can be pretty picky about food sometimes, and one of my residents has a sensitive stomach).

The toys are purrfect - the theme this month was the beach and (although I had my hopes set pretty low just in case) I was impressed and quite happy with everything. Each of the four adult cats currently in my home seemed to take a liking to a different toy. One of my resident cat loves crinkle toys and started happily beating up the yellow beach towel as soon as I gave it to her, and the other wouldn’t leave the jingling sandal alone (she has always had a love for bell toys). And my current fosters (two terrors who have torn apart countless mice and other toys within minutes of receiving them since I started looking after them) instantly took a liking to the toys that were stuffed with catnip. I was worried they would start ripping them up and eating them like the other toys I’ve gotten for them in the past; they were chewing on these ones before I even took the tags off! But I was worried for nothing - they have been chewing on and beating them around for the past couple of hours and aside from being soaked in saliva, they’re still in pretty good condition (which is more than I can say for the dollar store and Walmart ones I’ve gotten them in the past). The ‘dietary box’ replacement toy (that one foster is carrying around in the video) even matches the theme of the box, which is a nice surprise.

Will definitely stay subscribed to the box myself! Though if you’re thinking of getting this for your own cats or as a gift for cats of a friend, please take their personalities into consideration. My cats love new things and cycling through playing with their old toys. They also love all kinds of treats - hard, soft, freeze-dried, any flavor (though they don’t have to clean their boxes when the one’s stomach reacts poorly to it). Not all cats like to run around and play with new toys, and some are picky about treats - if mine were less enthusiastic about playing, I probably would have cancelled the box (or wouldn’t have ordered it in the first place).

Bokksu did provide helpful customer service when I contacted them which is appreciated. The tasting box arrived early - a full 12 days ahead of schedule, so I think the large window is just to set reasonable expectations...

The box is just WONDERFUL. The snacks so far have been super fresh and not a single one was broken or disturbed, so they were maybe even I guess thoughtfully placed in the box ? They are incredibly tasty and thoughtfully picked out - a really good variety of flavors, textures, sweet, salty, hot, traditional, weird (appreciated) and containing both subtle and much more complex tastes than that half crushed bag of prawn chips from the boba shop. This is produced so very nicely. Well done, Bokksu ! 👏👏👏

Just to add I think this will last a while - I’ve already tasted a good number of things but the snack quantities are good enough and the flavors more interesting and filling enough too that - it should prevent eating the entire box in one or two sittings lol. We can hope. 😂

Is this something that goes across my forehead a decoration of some sort. not. Not my style but it's pretty so I tried to put it on my head and it just. Not only that it was made of utterly cheap metal and I had to fix it when it came out of the box. And even after fixing it it broke again. So I called customer service. They treated me is if I had the plague and I was a liar. They wanted pictures (which I don't mind but they wouldn't even talk to me until I sent them one) even after that I told him I want a refund I don't like this it's cheap and it's definitely not my style. So what do they do? They provide me with a return label (which I was surprised they even did that) and said we will refund you. however two weeks later I got in the mail another cheap pink pewter product. and they kept telling me they're handmade there of the highest quality and blah blah blah! Bullocks!! Even if the jewelry/hair peace would have fit it would have fallen apart inside 2 hours!! Cheap cheap cheap stuff that you can buy for a lot cheaper at the Dollar tree. Some of it's very pretty in ornate looking yes but don't be fooled! all I can say is if I was a company sending out a mystery package I would not send out my biggest piece of crap. I can only assume that everything else is built like that thing even though it was pretty it was meant to be a decoration not something used on someone's head. so be warned when they say it's a $69 value they MSRP on one piece a poorly made hair accessory is $19.99.
I must quit ipsy because of this I could not believe that ipsy was subletting such poor quality stuff. I don't know if this review will make it because I'm not a verified purchase order through Amazon. But I hope it does. title: Healthy Plants
text:
Just started my ‘tiny’ succulent collection of which I plant them in Pacific Ocean driftwood pieces I collect washed up on shore. I drill 1” holes and transplant them there. Important to note that I drill all the way through and place small gravel for drainage. They can’t tolerate moist soil beyond their watering day as it will cause the stalk to wither and consequently the succulent will die.
Each type/variety is unique for its leaf shape, color, texture and personality, if you believe plants have such a thing. It’s going to be exciting, my monthly anxiousness, to discover new varieties when the box is opened.
Speaking of boxes, each plant was individually and carefully wrapped in bubble wrap and arrived safe and healthy. I like the monthly program even if they are 1-2$ higher than your local retailer. I don’t believe your local guy has the variety that this does, not to mention that this outfit has succulent professionals to ensure a vibrant hearty and heathy plant.

title: the world's ugliest eyeliner
text:
I have gotten a lot subscription boxes over the last 15 years. I did the New Beauty test tube and I used to prepay for the Allure quarterly boxes- the giant ones that were like 50 dollars and had all full size products (I still have hairspray from these boxes). I have also done like Play, From the lab, Birch Box, Glossy Box , and some others that I can't remember right now.
This box featured an Olay whipped product as the gift for sign up. Okay, no-no SPF and no discernible benefits from this product. Olay might try next time. Some horrible mineral sunscreen. Just an SPF 30 and like super ashy on whatever your skin color might be. So, no. The lip balm was full size which is fine but it has a really strong smell. The sample size of the mask was probably two uses, the spray conditioner maybe like a week of usage, the Sunday Riley face oil is fine but the sample lasted 5 days (face, neck, and chest). There were only two makeup items in the box The Makeup forever artist pencil designed to used on eyes, lips, and cheeks, but in red this is strictly a lip pencil because how do you blend this into a blush? It's not soft at all so you can Beauty Blend this until until your face bleeds because this is still not a blush and red eyeliner doesn't work on anyone but, the cast of True Blood. Red eyeliner makes you look like a junkie with allergies. Last and least that car wreck of an eyeliner. The color name on this product is Royal Blue, but it's really a matte turquoise long wearing and full-sized ( it's terrible but the plus side is there is plenty of it!). The formula and wear seem solid though (yes, I wore it around my house for a few hours) it's the color. The color is like a crayon- it's simultaneously vivid and flat. Here's the thing, I have a ton of Urban Decay liners in a variety of colors and the way that color works best in liner is if there is metallic element that adds reflection and dimension. This is just the truth. Matte colors one-dimensional work best in black, brown, navy, gray, maybe plum. I get that these boxes are over flowing with black eye liners , but this blue isn't even a trend color. So, I canceled this box because everything in it was a total meh and I really hate the color of the eyeliner and I don't want anymore landfill fodder from any future purchases from whatever crank fiend Allure has curating this garbage box.

title: Skincare routine on *point* (UPDATED)
text:
I'm subscribed to the K-Glow box, and have been for over 8 months now. I've never been disappointed with a single order, and my skin is the most clean and hydrated than it's ever been! The sheer amount of variety in products you'll get in a $30+ subscription is incredible, masks and creams and cleansers and toners- this kit will have it all and then some. Each box comes with 4 masks and 3-4 skincare products that are majority sourced directly from South Korea and are always in perfect condition upon arrival. It's a skincare party every time, super easy to share with friends, and I've been recommending it everywhere!

10/10 will probably stay subscribed forever 🥰

//UPDATED ON AUG 1ST 2022//

Well I guess I jinxed it, because the box I was subscribed to no longer exists. It's been a good few months now, and yeah, they've discontinued the K-Glow line in favor of creating a bigger more expensive box under a different name with even less product/variety. I'm really sad about this as I loved my subscription and benefited massively from it, but I really don't see much value in the alternative they've put out there so I'll have to officially say goodbye to FaceTory. It's a real shame, but I suppose this gives me an opportunity to find something else to fill the skincare void in my life. Good luck everyone!

title: It's a new service, but so far so good!
text:
Just received my first record, London Calling. The one I received is a great pressing; dynamic, vinyl was flat and dead quiet, and the added mp3 download code was a nice touch. I own the CD of this album, but this vinyl sounds far superior to my ears. I am expanding my record collection, and if this album of the month is any indication of what's to come, I can't wait to see the upcoming months!

I do hope, however, as more months pass by that Amazon allows subscribers to trade a month's pick for a previous month pick (if we missed it--i just missed the deadline for The Wall last month and would love to add that to my collection as well) or maybe have a choice between two different albums in case we already have one of the albums already. This would be far more preferable that just skipping a month. Maybe a monthly newsletter for us that are subscribed so we know ahead of time what the pick of the month is?

I know this is a new subscription service from Amazon so it is bound to change and improve with more time under it's belt. I would love to see for the subscription to offer different genres of music packages as others have mentioned.

Looking forward to seeing this thing improve!

title: CultureFly good. Amazon fulfillment bad.
text:
I got the Heroes & Villains box for the tshirt. Which, was a mistake. The contents of the box are relatively top notch. The "reversible tshirt isn't really, because the deco is heat transfer and the prominent tag can't really be removed without destroying stitching. So, it's a novelty I might figure out how to hang, but will more likely simply donate to a thrift store for some one with a higher tolerance for ugly tags and sticky heat transfers.

Tshirt: D

Black Adam Plushy: Solid B.

Green Lantern/Sinestro socks: oh how I want to give these an A! This could have been the PERFECT item in this box, but they're too small for my size 10 feet. That isn't terribly one size fits most, folks. So, B, because I'll have to re-gift or donate, but some one will LOVE these things.

Rest of the box is over all A grade, but I'll be re-gifting all of it. But, that's what I kind of plan for when I roll the dice on blind boxes. But Heroes and Villains, because I ordered it for the tshirt, was a big miss for me. Sized smallish, too.

Rest of box, Darseid bust that I'm only gifting because I have a newly minted fan of the character who will love it more than I. Fancy Superman pin that isn't my style, Aquaman decals that are perfect for someone else, and flash journal? Well, another friend who is a flash fan. Oh, and Wonder Woman and Cheetah patches. Weirdly specific, but OK. I'll donate them with the socks and shirt. Some one will love the surprise. You've got to order these things with an open mind and the realization you might be gifting everything to find "your money's worth" in it.

title: I like it but don't love it
text: This is my first time getting the box and I like it but definitely don't love it.  I got 8 items.  One item had to be replaced b/c the original company went out of business due to Covid.  The original product was supposed to be eye cream.  They replaced it with eye liner.  Huge disappointment.  The eye liner was about half the price the eye cream was and I was really excited to get the eye cream.  I wish they would have replaced it with something similar-some sort of face product if they couldn't do eye cream.  The salt and pepper set it meh at best.  Mine came broken so waiting to hear it they'll replace it (they said on the sheet they will).  Even so I might use that once.  There were wipe and face mask spray.  Both those are nice, but I never would have bought on my own.  There was also some facial/hair products that I do enjoy.  I liked and will use about 50% of the products, but I think that's to be excepted.  I am going to try one more month to see if I like the next box better.  Otherwise, I can't justify a monthly subscription if I'm not loving more of the products.  However, overall the concept is great.  I love the anticipation of getting something.  Feels like I'm treating myself.  I love that I'm basically buying myself a surprise gift every month.  Its fun to plan out how to use the products I do like.  I feels like a treat, which is what part of the point of the box is.  So we'll see if the next box is a little better.  Hoping it is so I can continue b/c I definitely want to like it!

title: Good sets designed for fun homework practices.
text:
We have received some really cool stuff at reasonable prices. The price has changed each month, though relative to the product. Each item has offered multiple uses and fun for my 5 year old and his friends. Some of the concepts have been new/challenging for my son, though not overly complicated or hard to explain.

Magic school bus engineering lab - some pretty complex experiments for my son, more advanced than Pre-K. Each experiment has a one time use, so if you mess it up, you have to replace the supplies. Most of these supplies are general household or School needs. The solar generator was the best, and reusable.

Code and go robot mouse - this was and continues to be my son's favorite. He and his friend spent hours programing the mouse, though rarely used any of the prefabricated designs. Great for inspiration, creativity and adaptability.

Gizmo's building set - offered neat designs and ideas. We haven't spent much time with this set, but my son picked it up and built many creations on his own with little to no interaction or guidance from me.

Robotics pet 600 - more complex building than Gizmo's, though offers creativity and adaptability. My son was able to follow the directions with some guidance. It's like an early Lego Technics set. Caution-its fun to let it walk off the table and explode.

Probably going to take some time off, play with current sets and resume in a few months. Worth it, though.

text:
Initally the variety was not great, but it got better after a month or so.

The smartphone app seems to me to be just a way to con your data from you - and bug you endlessly to buy the pay version - but there's no way it can know, or even make an educated guess, on watering, so I removed it right away. So no value (and more than a little annoyance) there.
The plant sizes are a bit small, and need repotting sooner than I did, as they 'root up' pretty quick.
It was a nice way to 'flood' my house with small plants - and cost no more than local stores would have, and with more variety, I'd say.
But now I've enough of them, so called a halt to the subscriptions for the time being.
I'd probably re-order if/when I need more again.
I do wish they included soil/planting/watering suggestions with each plant - they seem to vary quite a bit in that regard.

title: Expensive for what you get
text:
I canceled this subscription today. There are a lot of mazes and puzzles which my son does love to do.
I had these set up as auto payments then today(we are half way through the 50 states) and i get an invoice in the mail to pay them their $20.60. It auto pay but they decided to not do that anymore and have me reset it up. Then i sat down and asked my self is this magazine worth $10?
No. In total to get all 50 states that costs $500 over the course of about 2 years to get all 50 states.
There are way better educational and fun things you can purchase for your child for that kind of money. Think of all the family passes you or museums you could go to for that $500. It really is a ridiculous price for what you get. A laminated name tag and magazine. If your kids really truly love it and you find it is a wise investment go for it. My son will be 7 soon and he would much rather go to museums and see actual exhibits. You can check out books about any state and attraction at your local library and watch online tours of state parks, monuments etc if you are unable to go yourself. Those are much more interactive in my opinion than these puzzles(though puzzles are great for brains). Purchase puzzle books for a few dollars or purchase state themed/natural wonders/monument themed jigsaw puzzles or board games to make learning about states fun and family oriented. There are way better and cheaper resources out there folks.

title: We love these boxes!!
text:
We just received our fourth box:
Box 1- summer popsicle box
Box 2- tye dye art box
Box 3- fall hedgehog box
Box 4- thanksgiving/autumn box

We loved the first box. The girls made popsicle magnets, watermelon piñatas, etc. The tye dye box was interesting. I loved the coasters but the package was flawed because it came with one set of tye dye paints for all projects. Dunno if the dye would have lasted a month in the fridge (my plan is generally to do one craft each Saturday), but we ended up doing the full box in one day. No biggie, but that was a lot of focus for a 4yr old and 2yr old. I’m not gonna lie, it got messy and I increasingly lost control of art time as the girls lost focus. But we enjoyed making everything and cleanup was easy (as usual)

We are half way through Box 4 and my 4yr old loves these. I love having screen-free activities that I don’t have to do any prep for. I want to emphasize no prep. I’m into art myself, but the no prep part was what sold me. I can come home after picking up the kids and we can do a project while food is in the oven. As a mama who hates to mess up our evening routine, I wanted something that would take up to 20min (including set up and cleanup). This box can’t be beat! Last night’s “owl turkey” was nice. The project took maybe 10min and she hung the final project on our Christmas tree

An unspoken benefit is that we now have plenty of colored pencils and glue! We add the extra supplies to our art box and break them out regularly.

I really hope this subscription is varied enough to continue for at least a year. I love that each activity is built for two. The little kids love it; my 13yr old niece loved the tye dye activity (she stepped in once the littles were done); and I love it too

I have never heard of the 2 hardback books I received. Plus, one of the books was from a series. They didn’t send me the first book in the series though.... Oh, no no no..... they sent me the 2nd book..... a flippin’ sequel!?!?! A sequel in a book series I’ve never even heard of!
I have a book account on Instagram, and so, I went and asked other readers who have subscribed or purchased a box from My Thrill Club and what their thoughts were on the boxes they received. Nearly all of the readers that I asked had the same feelings that had: we were unimpressed with My Thrill Club.
This was a gift from my lovely sister-in-law. It was an AWESOME idea for a gift, I just wish her money was wasted on a company like My Thrill Club.
I only have 1 more box coming my way, so, I’ll be writing an update after it arrives.

*First Review: December 30th, 2020*
My awesome sis-in-law got me a 3 month Subscription for Christmas and I was super excited about it. Well....I just received my first My Thrill Club box, and so far, I’m not that impressed. I’ve subscribed to quite a few Bookish Box subscriptions before and My Thrill Club is my least favorite. Like the website described, I received two hardback books, Hunger & Vampire stories. Thankfully, I’m happy about one of the books I received...even though I’ve read it before. I really liked the book but I had borrowed it from the library.... so now I have my own copy to add to my book collection. Other than the two hardbacks, the website also described that there would be an ebook, or a code to a selection of ebooks? I got no code. Which, after reading several other reviews, I’m not the only one missing the part of the subscription that was described. Bummer.
Will I be recommending this box to friends....I don’t know. We’ll see how it goes after I receive the next two boxes.
Huge thanks to my sister-in-law for the thoughtful gift. She did an awesome job...too bad My Thrill Club did not.

title: There’s 2 sides to this company-and I’ll tell u about both....
text:
Ok, I’ve had over bcA year of dealing with this subscription company-and I’d like to share a. Review from two viewpoints-the subscription department end & the product end of it.

Subscription department: I’ve had a subscription for over a year now, SOMETIMES TWO! How? Bc at one point they somehow started another one with my card information-( I think it was bc I tried to prepay for 3 months at a time.) One month I even got 3 BAGS!!! I had referred my mom to the club & at the time the reward they were offering was a free bag,-instead if adding a month on my pre-paid account-they just sent an additional bag for that month! So I got 3 bags of lip stuff I ended up not using!! Since it was a prepaid gift card, I wasn’t too freaked about canceling it & became amused at what exactly they were going to try to keep pulling with it as long as they were allowed. When they kept trying to charge me for a 3 month subscription I DID try to find where & how to cancel it, but it’s not obvious. I finally decided to just send it to their customer care department and it wasn’t ever acknowledged. As a subscription company I feel their customer service is non-existent. Unless you are subscribing you won’t easily find anyone to help you.

PRODUCT REVIEW: see subscription review! No I know I need to be more clear-there were a few good products that I got from them? But overall it’s a complete miss. I’m not the first to say this! The colors are either brown or bright pink or orange, and I keep getting repeats sometimes as soon as the month after! Plus it’s NOT 5 FULL SIZE products, it may be one with a full chapstick and some deluxe samples...or the lip pencil they send doesn’t match the lip color that they sent...and they love orange! I’m not kidding I thought it was a colored pencil it was so weirdly bright orange!! Orange! Not coral. I wish I had kept all of them I would have posted a pic of them...if I ever come across one that I didn’t just toss, I’ll post a pic.
Now you might say it’s bc I’m not hip on today’s colors, but I have 2 teen daughters,17 & 16, and uh nope! I can’t push it off on them either!
Oh and the flimsy pouches they send the product in? Boo!! (I guess I’m spoiled by Ipsy!)

So overall-please don't get mixed up with this company! Don’t even just try them for a month bc it’s a total waste of money. Instead just go out and buy one nice tube of your fave shade-AND USE IT! You will be 20 times ahead of all of us that wasted $$$$. Plus really-how many shades do you wear?

The average gal barely gets time to throw her face on, before she runs out the door to start her day anyways! So if you get the time to put on actual lipstick, you might as well wear what you really love right?!

****By the way, if you want to have a fun experience ithe a beauty subscription, get the glam bag or plus from IPSY...AS OF TODAY DO NOT GET THE Ultimate Glam Bag from them, they just don’t have their act together with it yet? But I’ve been a subscriber from almost their beginning & they are always there if there’s a problem, and I get two regular bags & a plus every month. Plus they have super discounted specials on different products everyday. Love them.

The lipstick is gorgeous and I think I can use the eyeshadow, but as a metallic silver, it might be more of a liner color for me. I have no idea what I would use the glitter for. The lip balm is super hydrating and feels good, but it is this mod light yellow shade that reminds me a lot of the concealer lip trend of the naughts. I like the company and looking at their website I do see some things I am interested in trying. Medusa's Makeup is a lot like Urban Decay where their overall aesthetic is edgy, but they have products for everyone. I will probably not do the subscription box again. I tend to wear natural looking makeup with maybe a pop of color in the lipstick or eyeliner, so I don't think this is for me. title: I was really hoping for a Pop! Rides Yoda Riding Luke! Not a disturbing dead-eyed head
text:
My Dagobah themed box was delivered today and the only item I like is the cute Yoda "mystery" mini. It's not really a mystery if there is only one design included in all these boxes.
As for the "Dagobah Face-Off" movie moment, I really hope it grows on me. Honestly, since I saw this "movie moment" in the actual movie in a theater when I was a kid, its image has disturbingly haunted my memory for many decades.
It's not exactly a wholesome scene, in fact it's a horrific experience for Luke. Who wouldn't freak out after seeing your own dead-eyed disembodied head in a scary cave. And now...it's been memorialized in physical form...by way of a Funko Pop Star Wars movie moment that I now possess.
I was really hoping the Dagobah box would contain a "Pop! Rides Yoda Riding Luke Skywalker". I would have loved that and I think that would have appealed to a broader audience as well. Another movie moment idea...Yoda Raising Luke's Ship Out of the Swamp.
Anyway...the sticker and the sticky note pad are meh at best. A total of 4 items. None all that thrilling. Definitely not worth the $30.00 plus tax I paid with my hard earned money. Why can't they lower the price of this subscription box to $20.00 each since that's closer to total value of what they contain.
Sad to say but the reason I'm continuing my subscription is "for fear of missing out!" And I'm not even a millennial!
I included a picture of the cute Yoda "mystery" mini. Please tap the button below if this was helpful. Thanks!

The Venom t-shirt is barely okay and could be improved in terms of the quality of the material used. Doesn't seem like this t-shirt is going to last a long time. It's a simple design on a cheap t-shirt.

Instead of the stress ball, tiny venom figure & sticker, I would have preferred something more useful...like a key chain, luggage tag, pen, etc.

title: Just received the second of the same kit in 4 months. Wazzup Amazon?
text:
I purchased the STEM Club for my grandson who is just turning 5. 5 is a problematic age ... just beginning reading readiness for most kids so they may have trouble with reading some of the STEM vocabulary. I am sure that it is difficult for Amazon to come up with items for this age, Pre-K. I have a bright but not precocious grandson, A lot of things which do not require reading seem to be too simple for him or, if reading is required, he has trouble with some of the vocabulary. I read the reviews for the first kit, the "Young Scientist Club The Magic School Bus Engineering Lab". Frankly the kit was disappointing because some things worked, some things didn't and the whole thing was "cheesy". Thin cardboard, poorly thought out sequences of "experiments" and the like. His mom suggested I save my money, or give him a $20 bill. I said we would give it a second chance and we are glad I/we did. The second unit was the "Learning Resources Code & Go Robot Mouse Activity Set" which was a (stored program) robotic mouse with a travel platform (durable), some instructions (which we read and figured out together), cards which were an aid to figuring out the steps for the program, barriers and pictures with which to build obstacle courses and a magnetic wedge of cheese. Eli mastered the entire thing in under a half hour. He knew the mouse was a robot and the objective was to find the cheese, but he got the grasp of programming the mouse without considering the steps as "programming", he was just telling the mouse what to do. He showed off his new skill to his his mom, dad and grandma when they each arrived. I was excited to watch him learn. It provided for great conversation/discussion. This one was a hit. We are all looking forward to the next kit.
The Gears! Gears! Gears kit we received in July was a hit, but we were all disappointed to receive the second Young Scientist Club The Magic School Bus Engineering Lab kit in 4 months. We hated it the first time, please don't send it again.

title: Had Barkbox for 2yrs. Stopped cause….
text: As stated I’ve had bark box for 2 years. The different themed ideas every month is cute, but honestly my dog could care less. I feel that’s more of the owner’s appeal. Initially, my dog enjoyed every bit of bark boxes, he started knowing what the box smell or shape was and got very excited when it was delivered. I would cut the box open and let him drag things out himself. After nearly a year he started playing with the toys less and less. I can see why, the toys were always stuffed with squeakers in the middle. There are options to change toy types, but those are more costly and I’d much rather get the exact toy type he likes at the pet store that’s going to last a lot longer. The treats were very helpful in finding out his likes and dislikes. I appreciate the variety they had, as did my dog. Now, after 2 years my dog just lets his toys pile up, he started giving them away to friends lol since there’s a mountain of them. The only thing I would get from barkbox is treats and I didn’t see the worth In that when I’ve learned my dog’s preferences. So I decided to cancel. I cancelled the annual subscription and auto renewal by online chat. My account even showed cancelled. THIS IS WHERE IT GETS STRANGE. Come time for my usual renewal, it charges me…I reached out in confusion, tried looking for a confirmation email-that didn’t exist. THEY DO NOT PROVIDE CANCELLATION CONFIRMATION. I even asked for one and they said they don’t do that. YOU MUST MAKE EVIDENCE FOR YOURSELF (screenshots, etc.). Cause they might try to charge you again. The agent was professional and did still give me my full refund without problem after trying to get me to stay. But I refused to continue the subscription. Hope people see this so they don’t think they’re crazy, when they clearly did cancel. Once I’ve gotten my refund back, I’ll be deleting my card info and account if possible. We had a good run Bark Box, thank you for everything.

I still ended up going ahead and temporarily canceling my subscription because my cupboards runnerh over with beauty products. So I would say give it a go try a month it’s easy to cancel.
———————————————————————
So I’ve been subscribing to this box for almost two years off and on, and I’ve enjoyed it. There have been amazing boxes that have introduced me to excellent products. And there have been mediocre months where I was just not impressed. Never in the time I’ve subscribed to this box have I felt ripped off. I have looked up retail values ensuring I was still getting a good deal and making sure I was getting a full-sized item. Never before have I felt that I needed to look up the prices to make sure I wasn’t getting ripped off. For the first time, I feel ripped off.

The nail polish (a $16 value) is nice, and the eye serum (which looks like a sample size but is a full-size item that retails at $60) makes the value. But I open a larger box that costs more and expect to see ”three full-size products,” and instead, I find a grab bag from a trip to the mall. I open a box, and it's half full, no packing material, and one product open and leaking on everything and I’m greatly disappointed.

I'm not canceling my subscription yet. I’m willing to stick it out through January, the last box of my current subscription, to see if the new price and box quantity starts to achieve some semblance of balance. However, I'm incredibly wary and am leaning towards not renewing.

I used to recommend this box to friends. Now I can't advise anybody to spend money on this box.

I'm assuming they are trying to move overstock, so why not give the subscriber a deal we can truly appreciate as an incentive? $15 iseems like a decent price for getting quality overstock records.

title: Fun, Worth the Money!
text:
My review differs slightly from some of the others here. I have a pretty extensive record collection and Amazon still finds releases I value and wish to add to my collection. If you're reading to figure out what kind of albums you'll get, here is what they've sent me so far: Miles Davis Bitches Brew, Pink Floyd Dark Side of the Moon, The Clash London Calling, The Who Sell Out and and Simon & Garfunkel Concert in Central Park. Most of these are 2xLP releases and come from recent high quality (and desirable!) represses. Sure, everybody has "Dark Side," but now I have a copy I can take the posters out of and put stickers that stick on stuff - not to mention an audiophile pressing of the album!
People going off about these albums costing less than their subscription fee: Sweet! Cancel your order for that month and go buy it there! This comes to your door and if there's a problem customer service will take care of you. People also going off about not being able to cancel in time if they don't want it - that is on you! Amazon drops it in your cart every month between 22nd and 30th and won't ship until at LEAST the first of the month. If you can't check your cart at least one of these days - as said - that's on you!
I like this service. I have a pretty big record collection but I never bought any of these "classic" releases they've sent me because the vinyl gatekeepers often have original pressings priced much higher than they are worth (especially with this uptick in the last 20 years) and the re-presses are often a similar story.
If you want to relive the Columbia House days of 10 albums for a dollar and their inferior materials and pressings I do suggest you keep digging in the bins - the very same ones I will be digging through as well - to find your copies of the classics.

title: Why ask if you don't intend to listen?
text:
I purchased the DC subscription for my son when this went on an Amazon discount. I expected a hodgepodge of whatever. But then I received the following email from the vendor:

Thank you so much for your order. Along with your selection of Marvel, DC or both we would like to know what characters you would like included in your Comic Garage box as well. While we cannot guarantee every character, we do have most and will curate your box around your selections.

I thought this was awesome and very proactive on their part. And even though they stated that nothing was guaranteed, I figured that since my son only likes Batman & Joker and the Flash, it should be doable. So I reply exactly that:

Thank you for taking the time to see what I would like!
This subscription is actually for my son. He loves anything Batman & Joker and Flash.

So, they subscription arrives a few days later and what do we get? No Flash. No Joker. 2 Batman. And a crap ton of Superman (which my son hates), obscure titles and a really raunchy, pornesque comic that I will not be giving to my child!
I completely get that you want to get rid of comics that aren't selling at other venues and you also want to introduce people to lesser known titles, I do. My issue is why bother asking what someone is interested in only to send everything but? I think I am more disappointed with the selection received because of being ignored. It wasn't like I requested 10 or 20 different characters. And when you're told this is for a child, don't send porn! Needless to say I canceled the subscription and went to B & N and bought Batman/Joker & the Flash. I wanted to love this. I wanted to surprise him every month with 24 new comics. But it wasn't meant to be.

I have to say I was a little disappointed with the September which was entirely of Natural Hair Care products. This would have been fabulous but I don't have natural hair. I will give the box to my niece since she is natural but it would be nice to have a variety of products (hair, make-up, skin care, fragrance) with each box. Looking forward to my next month!

title: First Impressions are just So-So
text: Received my first box - Shampoo and Conditioner Sample were too small (did not contain enough product for ONE use) for my "just-past-shoulder-length" hair.  The facial cleaner lasted a week, the body wash was enough for three showers.  The hand/body moisturizer lotion was enough for one good application to my legs and arms.  I really liked the consistency of the full size lip gloss, but the color (Berry-Purple) was WAAAAYYY off for me.  I'm a REDHEAD and I use earth tones, corals, melons, terra-cottas and occasionally a plum, but purple?  Oh, no, not for my mouth!  If you're going to send me that color lip gloss, then also put in a sample or two of a coordinating blush so I can see if I would like it.  Think these things through and COORDINATE things, ladies!!!  I'm going to give them a couple more months to see how things go.....but the one thing I do not like is that every company represented in this box is now sending me emails - and two of them are sending emails EVERY day!  This is not a free subscription, I'm paying for it - so I don't like being inundated with emails.  One or two would have been plenty,  links to their websites, etc, and then that's enough.  So, I'm giving them three stars now and will update again after the new year.

title: Pretty good value overall
text:
I have had a subscription for just about a year and I am generally very pleased with it. I opted for the toys-only version because my cats inexplicably don't like food treats (go figure!) so I can't comment on the quality of the edible treats.

Not every month is a total hit, but overall I think the toys have a higher success rate than the numerous toys I've bought at the local pet stores. It's a nice mix of catnip throw toys and something on an elastic string dangling from a wand, some more successful than others (my cats favor feathers and ribbons over something plain). The themes are cute, but are more for the human than the cat lol.

One thing I REALLY like is that the toys with noisemakers inside are NOT loud and annoying.

I'd rate this 5 stars except I do think it's pretty pricey. To me, it's worth it because of the variety and the surprisingly high number of toys that have been played with long-term, not just the day the box was opened. It's not much more than I would have spent in the local store anyway.

I wanted to love this so bad! I rescue cats and foster cats.

The first box came with a purple T-shirt that said “cat hair is my glitter.”. Which to me is tacky. Also came with a coffee cup you hand wash only and can not put in the microwave. And A tiny trinket holder and an extremely heavy obnoxious pen that hardly wrote. I seriously could’ve gotten all of these items at a dollar store for a total $10.
The second box contained only three items. A sweatshirt that had a picture of a weird black cat wearing a giant gold crown. It almost looked like graffiti type. It was hideous. I would never in a million years wear that lol. And it also came with a small planter with the ears broken off (again something I would never use Even if the ears werent broken) and a big fluffy black keychain that didn’t even look like a cat. Again, items I could find at 5 below or the dollar store for $10- $15 total.

The boxes just aren’t worth $35. Unfortunately, I will be canceling. Super happy that every box donates a little bit to cat rescues though. Cats need more love and help than they usually get.
I will say that customer service is superb, though. They are very quick to fix any problems with your box

title: Only 1 star for ease of cancellation
text:
I was excited at first for this box but ended up being mostly disappointed/not too excited. The May box being my first Allure box was JUST okay. It is now my last box. I cancelled when I opened my box. .Here's what I received:
Jean Lue oatmeal exfoliator something...idk it sucks: LITERAL TRASH. Bottle came half full which isn't even bad because it is the worst item in the box. Does not do a good job, not even the job it says it will do. I think it also made me breakout. This item actually made me hate the entire box which then further caused me to cancel.
-PacificAmore Youth Masque is okay for now, it's very expensive but i guess long term use would really tell me how good it is.
-Laritzy lipgloss -Dont know this brand so that contributes to the non excitement. The gloss itself smells great, like vanilla cake batter or something sweet. The formula is fine. Not sticky or goopy. Glides smoothly. Not my favourite shade. It's a tad too light for my skin tone but i can make it work.
- Eyelites - The swatch is pretty and it dried quickly. I cant speak to it actual performance on my eyelids as i have yet to actually use it. Will update when I do.
-Laneige waterbank moisture cream - I like this. Easily absorbs and feel nice. Extremity small sample though..
- Tanning serum: I love the smell of this. Smells fresh and tropical and absorbs nicely and makes skin feel smooth. BUT I'm black so I wont be using this for tanning since i do not tan. I'll probably just rub it on my hand one or 2 times cuz it smells nice. Which i dont mind that much. It came with a tanning glove for application which i will probably toss because I have no use for it.

There you have it folks. The May Allure box. I saw June box and July spoilers, I am still not impressed so I've kept my unsubscribed status. Not worth $15 to me so far. Hopefully August looks good...who knows

text:
I am just disappointed by the quality of the kits we've gotten. My son is 11 and this month we got a Snap Circuit kit. He received the same kit five or six years ago and loved it. Today, it's just not something he has much interest in. A few months ago, the kit was the Gravity Maze game.Again, it was something that he enjoyed a few years ago, but today he has little interest in it. I have returned a number of these but don't like getting charged for something that I would not have ordered, or approved, in the first place. Our "hit" rate is under 50%, so I am going to drop my subscription.

If your child is just getting into STEM toys and games, this is probably a great subscription. But having a self-proclaimed "nerd" as a son, and without a monthly choice to opt in or out, we end up getting a lot of things that he just isn''t interested in and which take up space.

title: All we've been asking for is Han in Carbonite for like 3 years
text:
I wasn't going to buy this box, but at the last minute I found out it was Han in Carbonite so I bit the bullet and decided to go for one more ride.

The movie moment isn't really what I was hoping for. It doesn't really scream "Cloud City" as much as something with Han and Lando. I had a lot of trouble getting the Pop out of the box. I ended up cutting the outer box OFF of the Movie Moments Pop box.

It looks decent enough. But, Movie Moments take up a lot of space and I probably wouldn't have bought this had I known that was what it was.

And, of course, we get a keychain and a mini Chewbacca as teh other two items in teh box. The keychain's of Lando, but why is the mini fig Chewbacca ? There are about 20 minor characters who would have been more fun.

And, yeah, it's still only 3 items. I didn't want a fidget spinner or another bandana in the box, but even I will admit that one of those "fluff" pieces they used to tell us we weren't going to get, would have been better than NOTHING. I mean, not even a pencil ?

I'm not getting the next one unless the price drops. Those 25 dollar boxes at Target are nicer for the price, and you know right away what's in them. There's one for Batman '66 and one for the Aquaman movie. Check them out, but don't buy through a third party. Get them from teh store or their own website.

title: Best gift for kids
text:
JuniorChefBox is the best thing you could gift your kid. I did not buy it through Amazon, but I can definitely vouch for its quality! The recipes in the box is simple enough for the kids to make with little to no help from parents. At the same time they are so delicious and tempting that the kids would just love to start making it.

The fun begins right from the moment the package arrives. The recipe and ingredients list comes in a nicely laminated paper for durability. The accompanying video that acts as a guide to make the dish is just awesome. The character Cheffy is amazing. My daughter loves the character and looks forward to seeing it every month! The narration in the video is also designed for kids to understand and implement the instructions easily.

I am super happy with the product and I am so glad that I was able to take my daughter through the baking journey in such an excellent way. It has kindled her enthusiasm for baking which I am sure will continue as she grows up!

Thank you JuniorChefBox!

title: Eh. Only get it if there is a sale!
text:
I have wanted to try this subscription service for so long. I love trying new toys and treats with my spoiled baby girl. I just could never bring myself to pay the price. So when they were having a sale on the subscription box, I couldn’t help myself. The box came very quick, I was actually shocked how quick. I was excited to open it up with my cat. But to be honest, the contents were a bit lackluster. I got the box for multiple cats. It included five or so cat nip toys, all the same. Most were the same brand and a brand I’ve seen at many retail box stores. My cat was excited to open the box up, but she didn’t take to any of the toys as much as she usually does. As for treats, it came with cat wine! I was really excited to receive this because it was another item on my bucket list to try with her. Other than that, it was okay for the 15 dollars I spent on it. But I would never pay 30 dollars for it. I don’t think it would be worth it and you could find cute toys at a local pet store. I could have received a dud box, but I would still not recommend it. It’s quite a lot of money for what you get.

EDIT: I live in a small town with only a few stores and one pet store, that’s why I wanted to try this out so badly. But today I went to a discount store and found two of the items I received for 3.99. It’s fine because I paid 15 dollars for the multiple cat edition. But I would be annoyed if I paid the full 30 for it. The box also came with 2 dollar catnip bubbles I already get for my cat at Walmart.
