title: Really great box..but...BEWARE of the treats if you have kitties with diet issues!!!!!!!!!!
text:
This box is great! My cat absolutely LOVES the toys that come in it! So far we have received two boxes. The first box was a safari themed box and it had some really neat things in it...about 4-5 toys and a little food/treat. The treat in the first box was a salmon flavored type of liquid/juice. We tried to give it to your kitty but she completely ignored it. Ended up throwing it away because she didn't give it any attention what-so-ever. The second box was full of a bunch of red colored toys...one was a heart, another was a cute pillow with a feather...general stuff like that. Really awesome! BUT...it was the treat in the box that was bad...

So, the treat in the second box really caused our kitty to have an adverse reaction. They were organic dental treats that did not go so well with our kitty. We gave her the recommended serving (like 3-5 treats) and all was well. The next day, our kitty came down with the WORST constipation and gas ever! It was so bad we had to bring her to the vet. They ended up helping her pass her issues with some fluids/medication. Suffice it to say, we have discontinued this package and picked up the toy-only package instead!!

As a side note, our kitty is 11 years old and she has had some dietary issues in the past...so, that can be a contributing factor...which is why I am NOT holding the company/service accountable for her issues at all. However, please keep this in mind if you have a cat(s) that have had diet issues in the past...you might want to rethink the package with the treats!!

Aside from that...absolutely LOVE this package and it is a great way to introduce a variety of toys!

title: Disappointing
text:
My expectations for this box were not terribly high, and I did order it on Prime Day at a reduced price, but I still feel like what I got was not worth it. To begin with the box wasn't even sealed properly. One side wasn't taped at all, and the box was warped and twisted in ways that led me to believe someone had been rooting through my kitty's toys. There was a card enclosed that listed the items, and they all were there, so that was a relief.

The toys themselves are definitely not of the quality I would expect from a subscription service that is normally priced at $19.99 for only 5 items. My box included a "martini glass", an extremely short wand toy, and three similar rectangular objects: a "suitcase," a "book," and a pretend powdered drink mix "envelope." The martini glass was the only item my cat showed any interest in, so I'm guessing it was the only catnipped toy. He licked it furiously for about ten minutes, then walked away, He looked at the other items, but did not attempt to play with any of them. The stick end of the plastic wand toy has a very sharp extra piece of plastic sticking out that I will have to remove before trying to entertain my kitty with it again.

Maybe some months are better than others, but the offerings from this particular month just didn't appeal to me or my cat.

title: Disappointed Human, Happy Cat
text:
I got this on sale price, because I wanted to trial it before committing to a full price subscription. I've seen so many advertisements for KitNip in the past year and I was really looking forward to trying it. I read the reviews before ordering and was surprised by the negative ones, but I figured if it was on sale, it would be worth it.
My cat got three small fabric toys, a bag of treats, and a wand.
The wand's handle is very short. It's uncomfortable to hold it when the actual fabric portion of the wand is about the same length as the plastic handle. My cat really loves wands, so he was pleased. Me and my partner, not so much. We prefer to use his other wands that we've bought.
The treats were freeze dried bison liver. My cat is very picky, so he didn't like them. No biggy. I tried my other cat who isn't as picky and he didn't care for them too much. The dogs though? They eat everything and wanted the treats for themselves. It's a small bag that I can purchase individually on Chewy for under $5.
The fabric toys consisted of a plain Martini shaped one, which my partner says looks like a UFO. It's not the most appealing design. My cat loves fabric toys but this is his least favorite. Again, the dog likes it more. The other two fabric toys have crinkle and a bell sound to them, so my cat prefers those more, especially since their shape and form is better than the martini one for him.
The toys weren't a wow factor for us. They seemed mass produced and cheaply made. They list the values for each item on a cardstock insert. But honestly, everything felt Dollar Store like. Nothing against Dollar Store toys. I've bought my cat toys from the Dollar Store before but if I'm paying a subscription price, I expect a bit more or better quality. Overall, if you can afford the full price every month and love your cat, it would be worth it. But if you'd rather just buy your cat toys yourself, then maybe skip on the subscription service.

text:

My only complaint is the amount of treats we collected over the past few months. Each box comes with a FULL bag of treats, not a sample size. Which is nice, but I don't plan on feeding my cat an entire bags worth of treats every month no matter how much she begs and it's the main reason why I cancelled. If they create an option to get everything but the treats, I would consider resubscribing.

UPDATE: 5 stars --> 3 stars. We adopted a second cat and decided to resubscribe after a year away. I'm pretty disappointed with the multi cat box. The items claims to be $4-$5 a piece but I call shenanigans. What we received is no where near worth the $30 price point in terms of quantity or quality. I'd pay maybe 20.00 for what we received, but no more than that. My primary complaint regarding the treats still stands. Even with two cats, we don't need a full bag of treats every month but I can understand why some would. I'd really like to see an option with either a sampler size amount of treats, treats every other delivery, or maybe no treats at all.

I was looking for product specifically for people with red hair, which is what this said it was. One of the items, a make up bag, mentions the gene related to being redhaired and claims to be worth $25, and there is nobody on the planet that would pay $25 for it. It literally is a dollar store quality bag. Additionally, all the women they showcase in their marketing materials have very dark red hair and a complexion that matches. Most likely, women that have dyed their hair red. For someone that is a traditional redhead like me, with super pale light skin and an orange-ish red color, even the products they sent that could be marketed specifically for redheads isn’t really what I’m looking for. The eyebrow pencil makes my eyebrows, which are normally a strawberry blonde color, look almost black. It looks completely ridiculous and unnatural. I’m going to give them one more chance, but then I’m going to cancel. Super disappointing. However, if you’re looking to start a business that caters to women with red hair, I think there’s a market that clearly this company isn’t reaching.

I love Valkyrie but it would've made wayyyyy more sense to have Iron Man as the 2nd exclusive pop! Come on! It's the most monumental, iconic, and recognizable aspect of the film! I would've been such a strong box if it had Cap and Iron Man, the biggest curtain calls for the film (Black Widow still has a chance in her solo outing).

The box really doesn't have much other things to offer. The shirt was cool..... and then I got coasters.....coasters????? I paid $35 for coasters???? They're cute but not $35 cute. Now there's no pins, nor other funko figures other than the pops (which are great but again, missed opportunity to better match theme). Just feeling like the exclusives are very basic items.

title: Kind of Lame
text:
The materials that come with the box are top notch. If you are just looking for an interactive version Clue, this is it.

If you were hoping for something with psychological, factual depth, and social intrigue, YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED. The actual crime story and content is super lame. Like, Scooby-Doo type lame. Every suspect is one dimensional, at best. Also, no one is likable. Everyone is egotistical, vapid, overly dramatic.

Our most recent episode features the supposition that one character poisoned a horse to death with an accidental overdose of 5mg of Diazepam. REALLY? No one could be bothered to look up the maximum dosing for horse anesthetic? Okay, maybe some of you don’t care about that.

The suspects are the only people who provide statements. No one else offers any information. The witnesses do not answer any questions. They offer a few cheesy paragraphs of “oh I am so amazing. By the way, this death is so tragic. Gosh I wish I could be more helpful.” They do not share any information about their relationships with the victim. They don't really share any information about the other suspects relationship with the victim. They don’t even share town gossip.

This town is so small it apparently does not have a grocery store. However, it does have a bar, restaurant, veterinary hospital, pharmacy, record store and school. Oh. And it takes everyone at least 30 to 40 minutes to travel 1 to 4 miles from one destination to the other.

If you like details. If you enjoy feeling connected to a mystery, don’t waste your money.

It’s a great concept. Bummer that they spend such a small amount of time on plot and character development. They need to pair down their graphics design budget and hire a couple of fiction writers.

title: Best beauty subscription box value for money
text: The vast majority of the one-star reviews seem to not understand that you can look up what will be in the box ahead of time and cancel it for the months you don't want. For example, I skipped last month, but this month got close to $100 in products I wanted, including a full sized MAC lipstick. Just go to the Allure website and check what products they'll have for the month you are considering. ADDITIONAL COMMENTS 3/3/107: Amazon just issued me (and I'm sure many unhappy customers) a refund for the first box plus a $10 gift certificate. Talk about a wonderful company! title: Update 3rd box purchased
text:
*april - 3rd box AND I AM NOT DISAPPOINTED. Came about a week or more earlier than expected, got 45 instead of 40! Some of the movies i got this time were ones i planned on purchasing but never wanted to pay what the seller was asking for "such old movies", but Annie (the original w/ red head girl), Hocus Pocus and The Neverending story came! They do a nice job of trying to give you some of each genre you say you like. Of the 45 DVDs, 3 i already owned and 2 they sent me this month they had sent me last month (the phantom of the opera and chicago). After ordering 3 months the only CONS have been
- getting 2 they already sent (but to be fair i got 45x3= 135 dvds from them so far)
- last month i got the dvd knockaround guys, but about 20-30 mins in it kept freezing and skipping so unfortunately that one isnt any good (but still not their fault and it was bound to happen).
All in all i highly recommend if you are looking to add to your collection w/o paying much per movie (less than $1). I truly believe i will order again, but due to lack of space may have to stop sooner than i would like

* got my 2nd box (2nd month in a row that i ordered). Kept my genre selections about the same as im mostly doing this to have a bigger variety of kidmovies. Chose 40 pacl, got about 43 or 44 dvds. THE COMPANY DID NOT SEND ME ANY REPEATS! SO THATS A HUGE PLUS. I would say 4-6 dvds we already owned, around 3 or 4 i previously owned (but had given away to make more space at the time). Several i had heard of before but didnt recall seeing (but these titles were supposed to be good). About 75% of the box was family friendly for all ages while 25% or even less was geared more towards older teens and adults, but that's ok with me because i was mostly trying to find things for my toddlers and if there was something myself or my teen liked then thats cool too.
*1st review-Ordered 40 dvd pack. Chose genres: kids 2-6, family, action/adventure, comedy, edu/doc/musical, suspense/thrllr, scifi/superhero, drama. *I swore I had narrowed down my genre options to 4 or 5 a couple days before it shipped. Maybe I didnt save it right or it was too late b/c they were already selected?* estimated arrival was feb 22. Well they came today feb 8! My box had 45 dvds instead of 40 s0 that was nice. About 3-5 of the cases got crushed and pieces broke off at some point, but I felt like I shouldnt complain too much about that as they are used dvds and i hav3 a few spare cases if i really need to switch them out. Out of the dvds they sent me, I only had 5 already. Around 50-75% i never saw or dont remember seeing. I submitted 4 pics of all the DVDs I received. The pic w/ 5 dvds is the ones I already had. Pic w/ 7 are ones maybe the whole family would enjoy together (parent w/ teen and 2 toddlers). Pic w/ 14 will mostly be enjoyed by the toddlers. Pic w/ 19 appropriate for teens and adults. I will definitely be ordering a 2nd box next month if I have the spare $. I recently gave up Netflix and prime video to focus more on free YouTube and other free streaming services, but we watch a lot of dvds at my house (always put a movie on for the kids if im on a phone apt, doing household chores, purging and reorganizing items of all kinds in my apartment). I really enjoyed the variety of movies the seller put together and appreciated the price and the fact they sent me a few extra and sent it out fast. Keep up the great work! The only con I could think of if ordering again would be getting more than 1 or 2 repeats

title: Not cool Facetory...Update
text:
Update: I received my Summer 2022 box a few weeks ago and I was surprised to find all items were repeats I had recently received in the last couple of boxes, so I thought it was just a mixup. When I messaged Facetory about it, they told me this season's box was a "greatest hits" theme of items subscribers requested to see again.
So we negotiated a 20% discount and I kept the box. I appreciated their willingness to accommodate. Now here's what I don't appreciate.... Why am I now seeing the REAL summer box on social media?? I mean WTH Facetory, you flat out lied to me! The real summer box had the Facetory products along with 7 masks and the booklet was back. So, why didnt I get what I subscribed to? I just dont understand this business practice and am truly disappointed. I loved this subscription even with its little issues. But, I just can't continue it. Thanks for the fun surprises and introducing me to new Korean brands but I will now go back to being my own curator. (See new photo of Summer box. Looks almost the same as the pic of my winter box. Sheet masks not pictured but they were also repeats.)

Just got my winter box but wondering why only 4 products? Subscription is for 5-6 full size products so I feel a bit ripped off. I've been getting these boxes for a year now and while I love most of the items included it seems Facetory doesn't really go by the season when choosing products. I mean this box includes cleansing foam and a cleansing balm. 2 cleansers in one box, for winter?? Not to mention cleansers are the cheapest product of any line. So was this box worth the $49.95 price tag? I don't kniw because this one didn't contain the product booklet they usually include.
Then there was a toning mist and peeling pads another two items that they've sent in almost every box so they could've passed on for this box. And NO moisturizer! This is rather disappointing. I tend to use products according to how my skin behaves during the year. Now, I will have to store a couple items again for use during the the appropriate season. The summer box also contained a really greasy massage/cleansing cream that I had to put away until the weather got cooler and my skin felt drier and needs more heavier creams.
Facetory should send everyone their fifth product. I've never received a box with 6 full size items so I don't know why they even put that in their ad. To cut the box short with no explanation and no price difference just seems crooked.

( the game was a spoon game that you used house hold spoons) You get 3 recipes,  a game/talking cards, a list of the ingredients and a patch. We got loaded potatoe bar domino shortbread cookies and a cornbread muffin recipe. I personally wasn't impressed by the baked potatoe bar recipe. I know my kid's won't a few different things on their potatoes. The recipes were printed on nice firm paper that was easy to wipe off messes and came in a nice envelope. When I bought the box it was 50% for the first box, I'm not sure I would have ordered at full price. In a way I feel like we could have gotten recipes off the internet for free but on the other hand sometimes having to many options are overwhelming. Bottom line my daughter really liked it and was able to cook it all with little to no help. The plus side it got her to try something maybe she wouldn't of had normally tried.

title: Boho Gal
text: I chose the Bohemian style box and overall very happy. In my box I received a pair of brass leaf earrings (the same as in one of the images above), a set of 6 stretch bracelets and a light scarf. The earrings are lovely and have nice detail on them. They are a little heavy(brass) but I didn't mind that so much, and I got a compliment on them the first time I wore them. The bracelets are your typical glass sparkly beads, but I really like them. They're all in the white/gray/green spectrum, which matches the scarf, which is a solid color best described as a sage tinged with teal. One bracelet is solid milky white, the others are a blend of the colors stated above and have unusual variations (most of the beads are bi- or tri-colored) which gives off a unique sparkle. Out of all the items, the scarf is pretty unremarkable but still a nice light scarf in a pretty color. Everything was packaged very nicely and overall wrapped in tissue paper. There was a little card on the inside of the box with a nice message on it and also a thank you card with jewelry care instructions on the back and a welcome card, with my name, explaining how the box "works". Shipping after subscription date was pretty quick. Also, you can cancel any time. Do I feel like the value matches the price? I would lean towards yes, the scarf might be the "cheapest" thing in the box but still much like one you'd buy for $40 at a AE or Hollister and it feels silky and soft. The brass leaf earrings are my favorite thing I received but a close second are the bracelets, and all 3 items are color coordinated which I like, especially since sage/green is a go-to color of mine.

title: CLASSY, TASTY AND FUN BUT NOT INEXPENSIVE
text: I waited until I received one year's worth (four) Classic Bokksus to write my review.  First, regarding the quality; the boxes, accompanying literature, and the wrappers of each individual item in the boxes are striking.  The boxes themselves are refined and as solid as paper boxes can be.  I never received a damaged box or box with damaged contents.  Not a single item ever arrived stale.  I receive an email from Japan every few months notifying me that someone has mailed something to my address.  I'm not 100% sure but these might be the Bokksus because they seem to arrive shortly thereafter.  Everyone who saw the booklets commented on how beautiful the photographs were.  As to the contents, there's a good variety of sweet and savory in each box.  I like the little cakes and pastries the most, followed by the different types of tea.  I'm not as enamored with the hard candies that often leaves me feeling that I'm sucking on a sugar ball colored with artificial dyes.  I guess I expected more punch with natural flavors.  As several others have noted, the cost is rather high for a box full of snack items one might find on the impulse buying racks at a checkout lane at a convenience store.  Having lived in Japan before, I can say that while they taste good, some of the items, especially the salty snacks are pretty inexpensive to purchase there.  Taking into account the cost of shipping from Japan and the need for profit margin however, I suppose this is understandable.  I find myself having a hard time keeping up with the arrival of the next box.  That is, a new one arrives before I've finished the previous one.  This would make an outstanding gift subscription for someone interested in Japanese food/culture.

title: Complete rip-off
text: I subscribed to Little Passports through their website because my daughter had seen so many ads for it and was begging me subscribe. All the ads show a cute little suitcase filled with goodies, but it's completely false advertising. Only the first month came with the promised suitcase. I thought the things inside were nowhere near worth the money, but my daughter was excited to get her own mail, so I was okay with it. However, the second month, there was no suitcase. Nothing but a big envelope with a couple junky cheap plastic toys and a poorly written booklet that was worth perhaps $3. My daughter was so disappointed and upset. So much for the fun of getting a little suitcase filled with goodies every month, like the ads show. Obviously you're supposed to cram 12 months of "educational" trinkets into one tiny suitcase.  I tried to cancel my subscription, but the company is forcing me to pay for 6 months before they will cancel. So I've just wasted a ton of money for an envelope of garbage every month. Please, parents, don't fall for the cute ads and all the hype. This is a complete rip-off. I don't normally leave bad reviews of purchases, but I really want parents to know this is a waste of money.

I love a good t-shirt and honestly, I have no regrets about subscribing to this T-shirt subscription as long as I did but all good things must come to an end someday. It's not that I mind spending a whopping $21.98 (including my Indiana tax rate there), it's that the shirt designs bore me. 😴 I don't know about you, but I never met any Harry Potter fan who wanted to wear Voldemort's face across their chest or a shirt full of snacks bought from Honeyduke's. I don't mind the Phoenix, but why couldnt it be the star of the shirt instead of one of several magical creatures on the shirt? Do I want a shirt that simply says "Gryffindor" across the chest? No. Are the shirts soft on the skin? Nope. Are the shirts stiff as f? Yup. Feel cheap? Yeah. Sorta. Do they shrink? No, not really.

I realize I could have easily returned these since this subscription does indeed permit returns, but eh. That's effort I'd rather not have to put in.

title: Perfect for fans of Funko and Marvel
text: I don't understand all of the one star ratings for this subscription program. 28% of the people to review this give it one star which really skews the overall rating. I've received four of these now and I've never been dissatisfied. But I knew that some months you would get things you really liked and some months you would get things that weren't that exciting. It kind of depends on what you are a fan of. If you are a Marvel fan, and if you are a fan of Funko products, you will love this. Every other month there's that excitement and anticipation to see what will be in the next box. I usually hang on to the figures and the t-shirts. Some of the smaller items I give to friends or my wife or my kids. They love the little tokens. My friend sent me a photo of his luggage with the Deadpool luggage tag. I don't understand why people who aren't fans purchase these items and then downgrade them when they are exactly as advertised. I wish there were more programs like this in Amazon.

title: Unacceptable Product — Hugely Disappointed
text:
Hugely disappointed with this product. Gifted my mom a three-month subscription, and two of the months the bouquets came nearly dead — many had to be thrown out from being either dried up, rotten or broken.

In fairness, after my first unacceptable delivery, customer service was fantastic and sent a gorgeous replacement bouquet. I was hoping that was just one bad delivery, and the next would be better. Unfortunately it was not. I think part of the issue is that according to FedEx, the flowers shipped from Ecuador a week before they arrived. That seems like an awfully long time to be in transit (with no water).

If I were rating the customer service, it would be 5-star. But I didn’t buy the product for its customer service — I bought it for three months of gorgeous flower deliveries for my mom, as advertised. Unfortunately this product didn’t come close to meeting those expectations.

I will not be purchasing again and I can’t, in good faith, recommend to anyone else either.

title: Subscribing on Amazon is the best way to get this box.  Period.
text:
Some boxes are amazing. Some have a couple nice products, and sometimes the products are truly awful. That is what's so great about subscribing through Amazon. I go on MSA to see the spoilers. It shows what items are in the box. If I like it, then it comes to me automatically. If I don't like it, I can easily skip that month through Amazon. You cannot do that so easily if you subscribe direct because you can't skip a month online. You have to call or email and they have a way of getting your subscription messed up when you do. Skipping with Amazon is super easy if you happen to hate that month's products.

It's nice not to worry about which variant item you are getting.

They usually have a good mix of makeup and skin care. Most of the products are sample size, but sometimes they will do a full size product. Overall, I like this sub a lot. The brands and value are usually pretty good.

title: Mixed bag - half of the plants died - not worth the price
text:
Was looking to bolster my living room with a few new plants and thought this would be a good option, but I was definitely disappointed. There were four plants included; but only two actual types of plants (one pair of each). It seems like it would have been really easy to swap out two of those plants for two different ones - they claimed variety was a part of this subscription, so I felt like that was a little misleading. The box came with very little, so if you don't know plants or how to care for them, you are on your own. This is not a box for someone who is bad with plants.

One of the pairs, the polka-dot plants (no names or information about the plants was provided), were wilted and weak-looking right out of the box. I tried my best to save them - proper sunlight and watering regimen, etc - but they both died within a week and a half anyway. I think they were too far gone by the time they got to me, as nothing I tried brought them back.

The other pair of plants was far heartier and are doing fine, but I also could have gotten a similar pair from the corner shop for about half the price.

So all in all, between the lacking presentation and the fact that 50% of the plants I got died, it's definitely not worth the price or your time.

I am usually finicky with what products I use on this face of mine, but I was impulsive and subscribed to this in May. Now, I have favorite serums and acids, but those usually just struggle to keep my skin where it is (which is okay because it's been worse before accutane and acid treatments).
5 months later I am in love and so is my skin.
I would like to note that I give away any citrus-based masks to my roommate as I found that is one thing I can't deal with i the slightest.
My skin is calm and clean most of the time. I learned to separate the masks into 2 piles: cleansing and calming because my skin is horrible during periods and the calming masks help a lot. The cleaning ones do great throughout the month.
Also, no maskne anymore . Just saying.
Besides that, I love knowing there is a mask waiting for me in a drawer after I had a hard day at work, I do them every couple of days and it lasts me for the month.

I recommend it, my skincare routine is now this box, and favorite cleanser and moisturizer. And it looks so much better overall!

text:
I have been subscribed to these boxes since the first box was released by Funko. Ever since Marvel Corps was bought by Amazon and distributed through them, the boxes contents have become more cheap. What used to be offered in every box was an exclusive Funko pop, exclusive t-shirt, an exclusive comic-book, and a few other small things. Some boxes are not worth the money spent for them but some are. I haven’t thought about ending my subscription because the boxes that I do like are totally worth it. I just wish the same amount of energy went into these that Funko used to when they distributed them themselves.

title: Value is questionable.
text:
So I got 18 pieces total. One was thinner than a pencil. The two I gave my pups so far did not last long at all. (Labradors).

Natrual chews go for 1-4 dollars in general. So let's say average of $2 a piece. For having 18 chews in the box at $2 a piece, that is $36. If there were only 15 chews (minimum amount they promised), you would just break even if each item was an average of $2. Now consider you can buy things like pig ears in bulk for less than $1.50 a piece. What I am trying to say is, I think the value of this box is just okay at best. It seems like you might break even.

What really buys me is they source in South America. Which, if you didn't know, South American cattle farms are causing a lot of deforstation. It's very profitable for them to cut down the Amazon and other forests and create a cattle ranch. While the farmers/ranch hands/cattle might be treated well, this does not mean it isn't causing a ton of enviormental destruction by supporting them. Obviously I cancled my subscription.

title: Great Value and Surprises with Each Box
text:
I just received my second box and I love this! $50 and I'd conservatively say the contents are worth about $200 if you ordered everything separately.
In this box- Sunglasses( I priced online at $135) , Harry's razor & 4 refills, Marlowe Bar soap, Fatboy Spray Putty(travel-size), Tani Underwear( $45 a pair. Received code to order free online, including shipping) Aftershave toner(travel-size), Charcoal-magnesium deodorant, Coppertone Clear sunscreen( Full size), Boka toothbrush( pretty cool- activated charcoal bristles), Travel toothbrush protector and Marvis toothpaste(travel size)

Only one $5 item I didn't really think I could use but, everything else was either something I'd see myself buying or am happy to give a shot. Even if I don't buy more of the products later, the value was there.

If you're open to trying new products then I don't think you can go wrong here. I've already made additional purchases on some items I liked which is, I guess, what they're hoping for.

title: Smells great and brings joy - packaging could be less clunky
text:
My boyfriend got me a 3-month gift package for this and at first I was so mad because it is never something I would ever buy for myself! But after using the Fall box for a few days, I all but fell in love. The rose gold oil and pumpkin whipped soap smell so good and I always make it a point to use when I shower! I hope they last me a while (I tend to use very little product so things last me a while). I received my 2nd box today (Lunar) and some of the products seem pretty cool, like a toner and a primer/moisturizer combo, there's a lot of products to wash my face this time.

The only thing I found slightly annoying is the huge amount of shredded paper in the packaging. I just want to see the products when I open the box, I don't like to have to get rid of all the paper first!

Also, all the packages come with a little motivational workbook (one month it was an internet detox book and this month it is a notebook about manifesting your values, etc). I haven't had the time to use them and just based on my personality it seems unlikely that I will. So I guess if you're not super into that, it could be a waste of money. The products are nice though. I don't know if I would ever pay the full price for the products that they list in the booklet (it seems like I could find some cheaper alternatives that do similar things) but I like them so far.

text: My wife and I decided to try a new game, we decided to subscribe to this 6 month series to which we started but then hit roadblocks and became bored while waiting for the new game each month. title: Not your typical murder mystery game!
text:

I'm not a huge fan of mystery but I thought, "why not?" and gave this box a chance. I figured, at the very least, it would be something fun for both of us to enjoy and a chance for me to try a new type of game.

This box did not disappoint. I was a little confused when it arrived in the mail, the packaging was very slick and professional. I was expecting a cardboard box… but then again I'm not very detail oriented and didn't look at any of the pictures, which would explain why I chose to play this game with my wife and not alone. This game ended up being way more fun than I expected! The content is engaging and I wasn't ever bored. It actually kept me interested the entire time we 'played' (I say 'played' because you are always playing, thinking about the clues and whatnot.) I haven't quite finished the first season but I'm already looking forward to the next season, and I'll probably check out their sci-fi adventures as well. title: Not worth anywhere close to $30. This is a scam.
text:
I should have read the description, that's on me. But how can they possibly say that 2 skeins of acrylic yarn, no needles, and a small sheet of paper is worth $30. This kit is for 3 squares of a 30 square blanket. So all in all it would be $300 for a pattern and a bunch of acrylic yarn that would cost maybe $30 at a craft store like Michaels or JoAnns.

I have been a knitter for 10 years and cannot fathom the audacity of this. I am floored that anyone thought this was a good idea. I feel bad for anyone who buys this at full price. $30 for a full blanket seemed reasonable for an acrylic blanket. But wow is this a huge miss. Go to Michaels, find a pattern online and some youtube tutorials.

title: This is a GREAT box for the feminine woman!

The toys are great and last a long time and that's something that's very valuable to me because I've spent a lot of money on toys over the years. 2. I have an obsession with "Dog Mom" things, sometimes so much so that my daughter complains about it. With this box, I get a lot of cute items related to being a dog mom. 3. This box is great for the girly/feminine woman, but I am not that woman. I am a farm girl and rarely wear makeup or anything other than jeans and leggings so a lot of what comes in this box I won't use, but it has made for a GREAT guest room basket for when we have company. So, I can't complain about it. Overall, I absolutely love this box and the only reason that I'm giving it four stars is because I wish there was an option for tomboys.

title: Fun Ways to Learn About Each Other
text:
My wife and I subscribed to this box on a whim, and it has been one of the best purchases we've made in a long time. So far we've gotten two boxes, one arcade themed and the other shark themed. Both were high quality and absolutely packed with fun activities. The types of games varied greatly from card games to board games, truth or dare, and even a small shooting gallery that had to be set up in a hallway!

While some of the games are just for fun, others are designed to help you get to know your partner a little better. After the shark themed date night box, I now know my wife has no fear of clowns but is scared of heights. We've been together for years, yet I never knew this, and these are the little things that draw couples closer. Other games encouraged you to talk about the past or to even open up some relationship secrets (i.e. "What's the worst thing that your partner has made for you?"). The questions and prompts never got too serious, which I've noticed is a complaint for some earlier boxes.

One of the best things about both of the boxes we've received is that there are more date activities than are used in the prompts. The arcade box included a deck of cards that had different date ideas on them; the prompt only used the cards, but never the ideas. They were a complete extra. The value for the money spent is incredible. We were hesitant to try Crated With Love out at $30 a month, but after one box we could tell that we were getting far more for our money than many other $30 date ideas.

We look forward to future boxes!

title: The Gift That Keeps Giving
text:
I gifted this subscription to my husband last Christmas, thinking we would only subscribe for a few months after reading some reviews that said all the boxes start to look the same after a while. Yes, every box has a tie and a pair of socks and often, a pocket square (not always), but there are five items in each box. Each box has a theme - a person who inspired it. You have to read the accompanying booklet to find out who it is if you can't guess. The first photo I uploaded is the most recent box, "American Rocker," which was styled after Lenny Kravitz. I also uploaded photos of my other favorites: "Rocketman" (Elton John), and "The Duke of Cambridge," (Prince William). The other photos show most of the contents of the eight boxes my husband has received so far. He has loved every box.

The cool thing about subscription boxes is that they give you the chance to try things you wouldn't normally buy for yourself. This box has really inspired my husband to try different styles, plus he loves getting a surprise each month. A couple of months after we subscribed, the price went up from $25 to $30 per month, but we still feel it is a good deal. The blue watch in Photo #6 arrived with a broken hand a week before we were due to move. I contacted the company's customer service, and they not only replied right away, they rushed us a replacement so we had it before we moved. They were awesome!

I cannot recommend this subscription enough. I think it may be the best gift I've ever gotten my husband (and I've gotten him some pretty cool gifts).

text:
We got a three month subscription as a gift. It was a "thought that counts" gift.

Pros: The themes are very cute, and at least one of my cats liked the small pack of treats each month.

Cons: The toys are tiny cheap crap, basically all made in China, and half were unsafe to leave with the cats unsupervised. Think tiny plastic wands with elastic your cat can chew through in about 10 seconds, some felt in a cute shape stitched together and filled with "catnip" that has no scent, misc tiny stuffed things, and maybe some more stuff with that terrible elastic cording that you don't want your cats to choke on. Bonus: it all comes attached to cardboard using about 85 of those plastic attachment widgets.

Of course the cats like opening the box, but I could literally fill a box I already have with crumpled paper from the recycling, and my cats would like opening that too.

Summary: purchase only if you need $20 of instagram props for a monthly cat photo. Half will probably be uninteresting to the cat after 5min, and the other half will have to be confiscated for safety.

We switched to an actually local subscription with high quality toys that last for many months even though my cats play with them pretty much daily.

UPDATE: I gave this shirt its first washing after wearing it on Halloween. I normally pick the washing and drying cycles based on the most delicate item in the load, e.g. if most require permanent press cycle but one item requires delicate, I wash and dry the entire load on delicate. For this shirt, I turned the shirt inside out and washed and dried using the delicate cycle to preserve the design. I placed the shirt over the newly received X-men shirt for size comparison. The shirt did have some shrinkage but did not lose its shape. It will still fit perfectly. Personally, this series is still a keeper.

text:
So I am subscribed to the H2O, cactus, and succulent small box. I received 2 H2O plants and one cactus/succulent. So a total of 3 plants but they came in small/medium containers, not super small, maybe 4 to 5 inches in diameter. The box contained the 3 plants, a small blue water cup, a sticker, and some information. The information does not tell you the name of your plants received, therefore I am unsure of the names of the ones I got. It gives general information cards on how to take care of them but on the card it also has a portion on the other side that you can fill out the name and birthday of them. All plants were in good condition after hearing my UPS guy throw the box on my stairs. The one plant with the red outline on the long narrow leaves did have 2 rotting leaves towards the bottom of them. They easily came out of the soil when I touched them. title: Perfect for a budding foodie/chef/home cook!
text: I was worried about a kid's cooking subscription being too young for my eager 11 year old who already has some decent skills (she makes pumpkin and meringue pies from scratch easily, etc) as most kid's cooking books are lacking real skills and variety but adult cook books may be too complex or sophisticated for a learner. Nope! This is perfect for a more serious kid or even casually learning some life cooking skills for any age. It might be a little pricey for some for what it includes, but the way the recipes are adapted to make self-teaching, or semi-self teaching easy is perfect for busy parents or parents that may not have a lot of from-scratch or varied cooking skills themselves and worth the price. The recipes have illustrations for the steps and are laminated and include information about the foods, the country of focus, and similar dishes from around the world making it educational beyond cooking. The recipes expand the palate without being too daunting to try. In my experience, one of the best ways to get kids to try new foods is by them being involved heavily in cooking it. This is perfect for that! It would be easy to cater the child's involvement for each recipe to the needs and skills of the individual. The ingredients are easy to find and the list not too long. Last night it was from scratch ravioli and tiramisu, with an antipasto recipe we haven't tried yet. This would be a perfect option for homeschooling especially as the kid(s) can be involved in the shopping where math and reading can be utilized, and naturally math is part of cooking as well as physics and chemistry. Glad I have it a try!

title: Not worth it -- even on sale
text:
Signed up during the late 2018 subscription box sale. Even with a cheaper first box, this was a regretful waste of money. The candies are worse than grocery store bulk bin selections for a frankly ridiculous price.

Sour box in general: Terribly misleading lies. Only 1/7 was described as sour. Another was "sweet & tart". The rest were all sweet. I'll run through all 7 (6 plus a bonus) in the November 2018 box:

Dorval Sour Power Strawberry/Apple Belts: This was the only content described as sour. Sour Patch Kids are more sour. The belts themselves were unappetizing and stiff. If you blindfolded me, I never could have guessed the flavor.

Arway Christmas Tree Pretzel: The pretzels were stale, soggy, or both. Mush coated in flavorless white chocolate.

Gerrit's Strawberry Licorice Wheels: Ridiculously bad licorice or nearly palatable wax? I honestly couldn't tell.

Arway Dark Chocolate Holiday Nonpareils: Generic dollar store dark chocolate that manages to make Hersheys look gourmet by comparison, managing to be both bitter and chalky.

Vidal Gummi Christmas Trees: "Sweet-tart" in the same way a tangerine is sour. The gummi texture was passable. The flavor was mild, which was deeply disappointing as one of two remotely sour items in the "Mostly Sour" box.

Albanese Gummi Snow Flakes: The one completely acceptable item in the box, with a texture similar to a Haribo shark and reasonable flavors.

Bonus -- Sweet's Peppermint Salt Water Taffy: As I eat this, I picture a tourist trap beach town. Not the taffy spun in the window at the fancy candy store. This is the taffy down the street, in between the airbrushed t-shirts, ironic snow globes with melted snowmen, sunscreen, and cheap sunglasses.

Even on sale, I feel ripped off and regret not heeding the other 1* reviews. Please don't make my mistake.

title: Cloud City Box was a total rip-off
text:
I have bough multiple Funko Boxes in the past, not just the Smuggler's Bounty Box, and have always enjoyed my purchase.
When Cloud City was announced, I immediately jumped on it, as it's one of my favorite scene(s) in the Star Wars movies. My brain went into over-drive thinking about how EPIC this box could be.I was thinking of Leia in her Besbin Gown, Han in Carbonite, A baseball hat (reflecting the colors and possible Ugnaught worker logo), Possible Comic of Dinner with Vader...
I could keep going! But, instead we got something so, so...MEH. Like it was from a reject pile.
We got the following:

Movie Moment- Boba gets his Bounty (This would have been better as a separate piece for another occasion)
Mini Mystery Figure - Chewie with C3PO on his back (Seriously?)
Keychain- Lando (So badly made. Garbage)

Was this the BEST you could do, Funko? I think you need to hand over your Star Wars Fan Creed, as this was a total slap in the face to us fans.

It’s supposed to be a lip bag but I got a mascara, some pot of I’m assuming a foundation because all it said on it is first step and a small pallet of four eyeshadow colors. title: Nothing Like Expected! Super Lame and Not Worth the Price!
text:
I didn’t order this through Amazon, but through the Lip Monthly website, and let me tell you... it was AWFUL!

The first month, I got for $5, because of the deal they had for new subscribers. It wasn’t even worth $5. I got two different lip glosses that were basically the exact same color and didn’t work with my skin tone, a clear chapstick from an independent company based out of Oregon (that one, I at least liked for supporting an indie brand, but it was still pretty dull for a lip subscription bag), and a black eyeliner... the bag was one of those cheap drawstring bags from China.

Still, I gave them another chance thinking maybe I signed up too late for the previous month and that was what was left.

A similar thing happened the following month, but at full price. Almost every color was the same and I was unimpressed... at least that month I got a cute zip pouch?

I went to cancel because the lackluster appeal of this subscription, but they gave me an incentive to stay by offering my next month at around $7, so I gave them one more chance.

Yeah... nope. That bag came with half eye products and I was out. (Especially considering it was ANOTHER black eyeliner included). I wanted a LIP subscription. I already have an Ipsy subscription I get for a variety of makeup products. I just wanted lip products through Lip Monthly (crazy concept, I know). It also would have been nice to have some kind of questionnaire to customize bags to customers based on skin tones, skin type and product preferences (ie, like liquid lip or lipstick, matte or glossy, moisturizing, spf, etc...).

Save the money on this garbage and go to the 99 cent store or Walmart and pick your own products you actually like and will use.

This subscription is a joke and a money grab, pass on it.

title: First bag, Loved it!
text:
After reading the horrible horrible reviews, I did really have my standard set too high. Surprisingly, I was satisfied with my first bag. Not only was the bag super cute, the colors selections were all ones I’d hand pick myself.

After some research, here’s what I found on my products...

1: Eggshsell highlighting pencil by So Susan. Not sure how this qualifies as a lip product, BUT the retail price on this thing is $19.99. It’s a nice, all natural, long lasting highlighter. The product itself has great reviews. Personally, I don’t think I’d really ever use it only because I’m not really into highlighting. BUT it’s nice to know I already received a product that outweighed the subscription price.

2: Satin lipstick by DLS. First and foremost, I’m a huge fan of DLS products. The shade I received is called “Naked” and this is definitely and everyday shade for me. The retail price in this product is showing $10.00.

3: Hydromoist lipstick by Sorme. This lipstick, I had to try on as soon as I opened it. The color is listed as “Private” and it’s a plum kinda shade. (Also one of my go to shades!). The retail price on this is about $12.00. I love his soft and hydrating it feels upon application but I can already tell this is going to be an every hour application kinda lipstick.

4: Ultra creme liquid lipstick by APPEAL. This product here is obviously bigger than the rest and shows a retail price of $21.00. I will say that this color is a little too light for my liking, but the quality of the product seems to be just fine. I like the shape of the applicator. Makes it super easy to get along the edges precisely.

Overall, I’m satisfied and can’t wait for my next bag!

2nd box: the box included the books: Aliens:bughunt and The Brink by James s Murray. The brink is a sequel in a series. I find it a bit weird to get a book in the middle of a longer story. Coffee was from the mahalo roasters. Same brand, but a different flavor from the 1st box. The first and second box include books that are the second book in a series of books. None if the horror examples for books on the website include sequels. Why not send out the first book in a series???

title: Eye Liner Broken, Face Scream Smells Awful and Burns, can this be returned?
text: Ordered the Allure Box for the first time.  The shipping time took a long time but it finally arrived today.  First, I tried the "Face Moisturizer" by Maapilim.  The smell is awful, like licorice, I tried a bit on my face and not only was the smell overwhelming, but it burned as well. I looked at the instructions on the tube, the product is made in Israel and it has a warning on it, "do not use if you are allergic to the following products".....so it went straight in the garbage can.  Next, I opened the Cargo Eyeliner in Black Sea.  Looks like a great product.  The actual eyeliner tip sticks out about 1 MM and I have been twisting and turning to get it to come out, but it is stuck.  It won't come out and I can't use that either.  Next there is a 25 ml sample of Aveda Botanical Repair Hair Conditioner, smells great, I will use that.  I have not yet opened the Akar Eye Restore. There is also a sample of "Chella" Eye Shadow, which I do not use and will give away, therefore, I cannot speak to that product.  Overall, this has been a waste of money. title: Great Idea, Poorly Administered
text:
To begin, I ordered my first BarkBox subscription on September 1st and didn't receive it until 2 weeks later on the 14th. I realize BarkBox is not affiliated with Prime membership, which I am, but 2 weeks to get delivery? - Nah. To continue, I purchased the largest box available (for dogs over 50 lbs) which turns out to be smaller than a shoe box. Inside the box, and I'm not entirely familiar with how this company handles monthly subscriptions, but there were two bags of treats, two toys and a protein bar; all of which was colored in this immensely tacky-looking (I'm guessing 80's themed?) light pinks and blues. Just looking at them I was immediately disappointed. I would share photos of the brochure and other paper items that came with it but they found their way to the garbage pretty quickly. Everything just looked like it was cheaply designed and made. Very tacky. The treats? - Had a cheap smell to them if that makes sense. The toys? - My 10 month old golden retriever has dozens of toys, too many in fact and she has never damaged a single one - she's ripped holes in both toys and its been 3 days.
Great idea and cool for dogs but bottom line not worth the $30 even if the quality was better. Hopefully this company improves or competitors come in.

title: Gotcha advertising (read the fine print)
text:
Saw the monthly promotion and my kids LOVE Jurassic park. Offer was for a free XL dino egg. For a $60 price I didn't think there would be fine print. There certainly wasn't any on the facebook offer. So to my surprise I didn't get the egg and when I asked why they explained it only came with a 6-12 mo subscription. That's fine... Until I saw the ad I clicked on again and it had no mention of the subscription requirement. So I get into chat, speak my case and offer my proof. They're not interested in helping and told me I had to pay more money to upgrade just to get it. Then got snotty when I told them I would like to just close my account. They offered me another toy for the inconvenience, To which I politely declined and explained the entire reason I got the box in the first place was for the egg toy. (not an uncommon toy type and its my dogs favorite)

Would I recommend? No! Two of the 'super chewer' toys have holes in them already. I have an australian shepherd so it's not a power chewer anyways.

title: Boxes full of miniature snacks for fairies, not people!
text:
I received the 25 snack box for the first time and was not impressed, the box came 1/4 filled, and the other 3/4 was empty space, what a ripoff for $40 per month. Everything was super tiny, I could fit several items in the palm of my hand. The snacks included 3 little bags of pretzels, various kinds of jerky, lots of energy bars, and two little bags of random chips. These things seem like stuff they couldn't sell at a grocery store and they just packed it up in box to resell for unsuspecting customers. I appreciate that the snacks are healthy but I think I can definitely get more worth of my $40 buying it from a supermarket, personally. Maybe if the cost of the subscription box was halved I would continue my subscription, but at the current price, it's best to look elsewhere for snack boxes.

I forgot to cancel my subscription so I got a second box, still full of the same little tiny pretzels, energy bars, and jerky. At least this time I got a small bag of cookies...It feels like this company really loves their pretzels, I have so many pretzels now instead of a variety of chips or crisps, how disappointing. To inform how little you're actually getting, I had combined both snack boxes together and there is still space for probably a third box of snacks. If the original box included twice the amount of snacks it had, it would be a better deal, and I would feel like it was worth getting, despite the lack in variety of snacks. As for the taste, I tried about seven snacks and they were OK, but not anything impressive, since they are basically your everyday snacks you could buy from a grocery in mini form.

Update:
SnackNation offered to provide some additional snacks for no cost for me to try due to me being unhappy with my previous boxes, and I accepted. They shipped me two mini boxes, which were completely stuffed to the brim (unlike my giant box of mostly empty air), but I can't say if this would be true for subscribers for their newer boxes, so I would reserve my judgement on this until I try a full sized box from them.

The new snacks they gave me were surprisingly bigger than what they had given me in the past, and again, I do not know if these changes will be reflected in their new boxes, but they had promised me they were changing their curations for future boxes, so I hope this is true for the sake of their subscribers. They included a variety of snacks which I hadn't seen before, and I would say I was happier with this selection that I received for free vs. the selection I had gotten when I paid for the subscription, but this might be due to the changes they were making to their boxes as they had mentioned to me. The snacks are still on the smaller side, but not so much as before, where you felt you got cheated somehow by the tininess of everything. I would say the new snacks are appropriately snack-sized for human beings to consume now, instead of for tiny fairies. But they also included some duplicate snacks between the two mini boxes I received, which could be either a bonus or a con, depending on whether the snack in question tastes good or not.

For example, they put the same bag of RIND snack in both boxes, and unfortunately, I have to say this snack is one of the most unpleasant things I have ever placed in my mouth. I've only gotten through half of the first bag and I will question my sanity if I try to attempt to finish the second one. I appreciate the RIND company for trying to come up with healthy snacks, but their versions of dried fruits is absolutely disgusting. The fruits included were dried pineapple, dried kiwi, and dried orange with the peel on. On the back of the snack bag, it encourages you to eat the peel since it contains a lot of nutrients, even more than the fleshy part of the fruit. So I tried to heed their advice and put the whole dried orange in my mouth, peel and all, and chewed it for three seconds and had to spit it back out. It was the most bitter thing I had ever tasted in my life, and I've had tried many bitter things before, but not to this extent. The dried kiwi was like dried extremely sour ??? covered with a very light coating of sweetness which was wholly unpleasant. Only the dried pineapple was passable, but honestly, it tasted like a vampire sucked all the juice out, chewed it a couple times, then spat it into the snack bag for us mere humans to finish.

However, the other snacks I have tried have been great so far, and I will post further updates as I go through my snack boxes. I am still undecided whether to restart my subscription, but perhaps I will give them another chance in the future if my finances allow. For now, I would bump my rating to 2.5 stars.

title: Good Combination
text:
The coffees are good and do show a nice variety. If you go by the standardized cup markings on the side of most coffee pots, I got about 18 "cups" out of each packet. It would probably be about half that number in coffee mugs. I use about a scoop for every two "cups" I make. If you like your coffee stronger, you'll get less out of packet. Despite the fact that they are pre-ground, I don't have any complaints about freshness. The bags are sealed at least as well as any commercial pre-ground coffee and are (according to the company) freshly ground a few days before you receive them.

Update: when this review was written, you got 2 packets, each with a different coffee per month and each packet made 18 "cups". A matched cookie was included for each packet. Now, you get 1 packet per month that makes about 36 "cups" and two cookies of the same type. It's the same amount of stuff you got before. But, the single larger quantity match may be more convenient for sharing.

The cookies are very good for a packaged cookie and have an interesting combination of ingredients, making them a bit more unique than a simple chocolate chip or sugar cookie. They seem to be a fresh baked cookie that is sealed in a plastic wrapper and then shipped. By the time they get to you, they have dried out a little, but they are still very good. As for size, they're just a little bit smaller than the rim of a plain white coffee mug. That's not huge, but it's more than adequate.

My only complaint is that it took a full 2 weeks after the date that Amazon placed the order for the package to arrive. For a company that seems to be trying to ship a fresh product, that's a little slow. I'm not sure how much this is impacting the freshness, but it is a concern.

Note that MY order date was even earlier. Amazon places the orders once a month, which means your order is also delayed until about the 14th of the month. I'm not complaining about because it doesn't affect the freshness of the product. (I gather it's made fresh AFTER the Amazon order is placed.) You DO have to be very aware of the total time frame if you're planning to make a gift of this, though.

title: Not Marvel or funko, 1 start TOTALLY for Amazon
text:
I am livid that this is at Amazon. This was the first box I was suppose to get since the subscription came here. I placed my order on 10/6. Other people placed orders after me and already have tracking information etc. It is misleading that the page leads you to believe that this will arrive and/or ship on the 28th of each month (some people in previous boxes had theirs on the 28th).
I spent ALL DAY chatting to reps about this and transferred between 5 different reps in one chat session alone. Yet I have to wait 24 Hours for the Marketing and Promotions Department (WHY? That is the weirdest department to handle this and may explain why there are so many problems) to get back to me.

For whatever reason Amazon does the following:
A) Lists this as a digital order (which causes confusion with the Non English speaking reps)
B) Will not allow you to use gift cards on this and says that its because Funko made that rule (seems like funko didnt).
C) Does not process the orders by who had the subscription the longest (i.e. I know one reddit user placed his order a full week after me and already has tracking info).

I will update this once Amazon fixes these problems. I love Marvel and Funko and this is NOT a slight to them in anyway shape or form (The boxes are quite awesome in general). Funko needs to reevaluate who carries these subscriptions and move this one to a brick and mortar store like how the Disney one is with Hot Topic. Amazon has no business dealing with this.

title: Best self-care gift I could have given myself!
text:
I first purchased TheraBox at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic. I was having a hard time dealing with isolation, and was not taking good care of myself. I stumbled upon TheraBox when browsing Amazon, and it sounded like a great idea so that I could get some self-care goodies to take care of myself during an incredibly difficult time. I also am really bad at picking out my own skincare items, because I can be indecisive, so this was a good way to get different types of self-care products to try.

When I received my first box (pictured) I was shocked at how much I got for the price! The products are full-size and I love the variety of items included in the box - skincare, nails, hair, body, and more. This has allowed me to try all sorts of things I otherwise never would have tried, and I have added a bunch of these products into my daily routine. I also love that it comes with a fun activity each time to help boost my mood.

I thought that I would only get TheraBox for a few months, but 9 months later I am still getting my monthly TheraBox and loving it as a nice surprise for myself each month! I highly recommend TheraBox for anyone who wants to try more self-care products, or even better as a gift for a loved one.

title: Amazon's Record Club is a Fun Idea that Needs More Work
text: I was really excited to join this Vinyl-of-the-Month club. As a music lover with a turntable working to build an incredible music collection, it seemed like a good opportunity to get some older albums I might have overlooked. It's focus on albums from the '60s and '70s sounded perfect. I participated for 5 months, but decided to call it quits. My primary issue is that I don't think Amazon has put enough thought into their selections. It started off promising with Credence Clearwater Revival's Greatest Hits, an album by a band I'd heard of but not heard. Then came The Who's The Who Sell Out, again, a band I'd heard of but never listened to. Then things took a bad turn. December's "album" (in quotes because it wasn't one) was Blondie's 12-inch single for "Heart of Glass." While Heart of Glass is a great song, this was a disappointment, since it's a single and not an album. For $25, I felt like I wasn't getting value. Then January and February brought two albums from the same band: Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon and The Wall. Great albums and classics for sure, but getting two albums from the same artist in consecutive months feels like whoever is choosing got lazy. I've now quit the club and will be curating my own list of classic albums to buy.

I love looking forward to this box of surprises that make anyone smile. I do feel it is reasonably priced for the amount and quality of the items you get. I really think the manufacturer puts a lot of thought into the variety of items that go into every box. Many of the items have been very clever and done in a way that is tasteful (like recipe cards! not TOO childish to use as an adult in my kitchen ;) and one great quality printed card stock). You WILL get items you may never use, but they make fun gifts that always get a laugh (like a mini pusheen desktop vacuum!) and are still very high quality. For the quality, presentation, variety, and quantity of items in each box, I have to give this 5 stars. Well done.

There is one pitfall I must say - the theme of the box sometimes can be off-season. I know my "fall" box came with Halloween items on November 2nd - I would have loved to have them during Halloween, but I just kept them for next year! Not a huge deal, but if these are "box exclusives" it would be nice to have them come before the holiday they might be themed for.

Also - to address other reviews saying they received the wrong size in apparel and rated it lower due to this - I wanted to say that the customer support of these boxes is amazing! They replace items without a fuss and are always very professional. I wouldn't worry about this at all.

text:
My golden, Toby, is 11. We've done subscription boxes for him before and he knows when the box is for him. When his BoxDog was delivered, he was very excited. We ordered the large for him.

It contained:
2 large, durable dogs toys - an adorable shark and a blue football-shaped toy. He played with blue toy for a bit, but the shark definitely won out. He isn't rough with his toys anymore unless he gets bored, but they do seem like they would hold up well, especially the blue toy.
4 large biscuit treats (2 frosted, 2 unfrosted): He's not big on the frosted treats from petco, so I wasn't sure if they'd be a hit. Spoiler, he loved them. All 4 of them.
Package with 3 types of smaller treats: He loved these as well. No complaints.
Small container of sunscreen: Not sure how well this works. It's already cold and snowy here, but we'll hold on to it.

I think it's worth the price once in a while. I feel like the value is there and it makes my boy happy. Probably not something I'd get every month since he only needs so many toys, but Amazon lets you skip months. I am considering picking up one of their larger boxes for Toby for Christmas.

title: The second month is a Photoshop mess placed on a Tshirt.
text:
First off, I love the Streets of new Capenna set. I'm a huge 1920's - 30's buff and appreciate the mobster, speakeasy, industrial, and art deco styles they incorporated. However this product was not something I would have even bought from a bargain bin.

The first month I received was great except they sent me the wrong size. This second month was a huge dissapointment. The material, though soft, seemed stretched. Like someone already wore it stretched. The smell was like dust and ink and not that new t-shirt smell. Also, the shirt stated it was coming in black and came in a navy blue. I feel the color choice was wrong, more on that next.

The image on the front is big and gaudy. Like someone painted it on the side of a van. The picture depicts the 5 mob bosses of New Capenna. I love these characters in the stories and also on Arena. However they don't belong crammed on a shirt. It's easily noticable that these are the exact images from Arena. They are photoshopped onto the chest and become a jumbled mess. The art is blurry, the contrast is flat, the lighting is dark, and the only thing that pops is the gold border and green glow from Jetmir the Cat Demon head of the Cabaretti.

The first month we received an awesome Blue Mana shirt done in the art nouveau style. I'm not a blue player typically but this thing was awesome! However it seems that this is a 50/50 chance to receive something good, so far. I will be getting next months shirt but if it's anything like this I will return it and not order another.

I feel that this particular printing didn't do the artists justice of who originally painted those characters. I believe it cheapened those pieces. Like a shirt you would find on vacation and you only buy to gift it to others.

I'm going to leave this at two stars because I did enjoy the softness of the material. Although loose fitting, the first shipment wasn't like this, it did feel nice.

title: I’ve tried them all & How To Be A Redhead is the best subscription box!
text:
If you are like me, you’ve tried so many different box subscriptions. I’ve tried everything from Ipsy to fabfitfun, to even smaller subscription comapnies and nothing or no one compares to how amazing How to Be a Redhead’s subscription box is!

Every single month I feel like the box caters to my exact needs. It’s SO REDHEAD FRIENDLY & great for my sensitive skin! They really put a lot of time and effort into thinking about their clients with each item they put in……. It’s very apparent. Plus, the benefit of all of it… is trying new things! I’ve spent thousands over the years trying beauty products from the regular store and end up wasting my money with products that either make me breakout, aren’t right for my skin tone, don’t match my red hair, terrible quality, have horrible chemicals, or a thousand other reasons!
I swear most big beauty companies have never talked to an actual redhead when they make their products…… some of the stuff they come up with is just a joke.

I’ve had my How to Be a Redhead box subscription for a while now and so many of the items I’ve received I’ve loved so much that I buy them on the regular now. Some of the items that How to Be a Redhead make themselves have been in the boxes & those are my favorite boxes! I’m legit obsessed with my redhead Bobby pins…. Show me which box subscription gives out a different color besides the black and brown Bobby pins? My updos have NEVER looked better!

Some of the reviews I’ve read on here are outrageous! I’m sorry, but it’s true! These boxes value is way more than you pay for them, it’s a great deal honestly. Like I said before, I would pay thousands to try a product out and I honestly have saved money getting these boxes and not wasting so much on buying the bigger chain store products that I don’t love. Rarely do I receive something in the box that I don’t love too! A lot of the products are cruelty-free, save on plastics, and don’t have those terrible chemicals in them!

I read one review that said it’s generic products and I couldn’t disagree more. Order from Ipsy one time and you’ll notice what’s generic! 🥴

I haven’t ordered their deluxe box yet, but I’m looking forward to it because if this box is GREAT…..I can only imagine how amazing that one is!

Lastly, I have a few friends with red hair and this subscription is a great gift idea…. Just saying!
God- I could go on and on…. But like you get the point I’m literally obsessed & my favorite time a month is when my red box is at my door.

title: Excellent Product
text: If you have a child who likes to solve mysteries and enjoys learning about history and other cultures, this is perfect for them. My son was hooked right away with the fun letter that explains the mission. We really enjoy the map that was included. This is not a quick activity book, there are so many different activities. We didn't work on it everyday and it took us about a month to complete everything and solve the mysteries which was perfect timing for when we received the next packet.  I am an early elementary teacher and was both pleasantly surprised and am impressed with the variety of activities to complete: search and find, matching, codes, opposites, critical thinking skills, etc. The reading level of the guide book is higher, I would guess about third grade and above, and the activity book would probably be upper second grade or higher. My son was able to read the activity booklet and I would read to him from the Top Secret Guide Book. It was a nice balance for shared reading. So, if you are wondering if this is at the right reading level and interest level for your child, I would say it is good from first grade (with help reading from adult or older sibling) to 5th grade. The older the student, the quicker and more independently they will be able to get through the activities. I highly recommend this.

I expect the rest of the items to have a similar mix of results, and I'll be sure to mark down the "good" ones and try to find them at my local Japanese grocer.

Even if every item were good, I think the regular box price would be on the 100% not worth it side of the scale. At 20-25 items per box, with some of those items being tiny, it comes to $1.56 to $1.95 per item. I typically expect more than your money's worth for mystery type boxes like this, and it's hard to see that being the case here. Needless to say, I won't be continuing my subscription.

title: Disappointed in this Subscription
text:
There is so much great artwork available for Dungeons and Dragons that i thought some of it would appear on the t-shirts. It was hinted at in the examples but never came through. The art was obviously "home grown" or inspired by classic artwork but not quite the same. If I was in my teens or twenties, I might have enjoyed these more but being somewhat older, I did not.
When the designs were awesome, they were cluttered up with unnecessary wording. I am not referring to the "Dungeons and Dragons est 1974" that appeared on many. I am referring to the "Detect Magic" that appeared on the shirt with that at the top, a really cool picture of a wizard casting a spell in the middle and the D&D est 1974 at the bottom, the Detect Magic was unnecessary. The Caves of Chaos Map with the dice over it was okay but it didn't need the words "never Split the Party" over almost the whole map in red. Most of the shirts, including the one that came last week, follow these examples.
Of the last year, there were 4 shirts I would wear regularly and the rest occasionally.
While I might recommend this for the younger gamer, I would not for an adult.
I have cancelled my subscription.
The shirts did come when advertised and there were regular updates when one shirt was "late" by coming on the last day of the month. The are comfortable and washed well.
This subscription had great promise, but very seldom delivered.

title: Good music, bad system
text:
If you like rock from the 60's and 70's, with broad interests in that genre, you'll like the selections. Pink Floyd, Simon and Garfunkel, Hendrix, The Who, Black Sabbath, The Clash, etc. represent recent selections. Also, the price is generally lower than if you just went and bought the album on Amazon (sometimes considerably so). Notice, however, nothing outside rock, despite what the club description might have you to believe. No Motown, Funk, Soul, New Orleans sound, blues, jazz, etc., at least during the year or so I've been a member.

One problem is I already have over 1/2 the albums that they have chosen for selections. Not a big deal in general, but Amazon does not send an order placed email like usual - I only get an 'item has shipped' email. So, I have no chance to see what the selection is and cancel it before the order is locked in a shipping status. That means I am returning an album most months of the year. Not only is this terrible for the environment (e.g., fuel and packaging costs both ways), but it is a hassle to me (and hurts Amazon profits!).

text:
I've been receiving meowbox for almost 2 years. I have five cats.
When we first started receiving it, the toys were all from different manufacturers. You could SMELL the catnip when you opened the box. My cats would go crazy. Most toys were enjoyed, a few hard toys were rejected. However, in the last 4 months, I've become quite disappointed. The toys are now all made by Meowbox (as stated on the card each toy comes on) and there is zero catnip smell. Last night we opened the "winter themed" box. Cute but except for the feathers on the toys, may cats had zero interest. I could tell they did not smell any catnip. They were more interested in the box (I believe Meowbox sprays the box with a catnip scent). We received about 5 or 6 toys and the cats walked away. They used to LOVE the toys that were soft and stuffed with catnip but the few stuffed toys we got yesterday, cats had no interest. Sadly, I'll be canceling now. $20 is a lot of money for my cats to care less and I throw it away in a month. I can go buy other toys at specialty shops for that. I wish Meowbox had kept to the small businesses that made super stuffed toys instead of going commercial dollar store like.

title: Value?  Yes!  [UPDATE] Maybe?
text:
UPDATE: 2nd Super Box Delivery

Much much worse than the first box. So many dollar comics! (11 to be precise) and 1 comic that if it was CGC graded 9.4 would be worth $22. Such a let down this month - I had never heard of 80% of the comics they included.

Third box will be the deciding factor if I keep this going. I'll post another update next month

*********************************************
I was a little skeptical and will really hold my opinion until I receive my second box. However the first box pleasantly surprised me.

1) You pick the characters you are interested in. My custom box fit pretty well into what I chose, no real deviation.

2) Grades - I would review all 11 comics at ~9.4 NM condition. All are unread and in pristine condition.

3) # of Comics - I received 11 instead of the listed 10

4) Value for money - If you divide the cost of the box by the total items, you pay ~2.70 per issue. Several issues are valued at $30, which includes the Spawn 11.

5) Variety - My box included 1992 prints all the way through 2017. All major titles and several #1 first print covers. a good mix.

If the boxes continue with this mix and quality - it is well worth the subscription price, and easily adds value to your collection.
