title: After 3-4 months, like this box more than Sephora Play!
text:
Review update 9/13/18:

I now I have a few more months of getting these boxes and I'm still very happy with them. Today I received the September box with all sorts of amazing items (Tarteist pro LASHES that are absolutely GORGEOUS) and Drunk Elephant Baby Facial to name a few. I ended up cancelling my Sephora Play subscription recently and I'm glad I did- I NEVER was terribly thrilled with any box I got but Allure has been awesome every month. Sure, there's a few things I may not use or aren't my cup of tea but for the most part there are some amazing products. One month that had a Kat Von D theme they had an amazing purse mirror that I'm a bit obsessed with.

All in all, I'm very pleased and have no idea why there are so many negative reviews. This is way better than Play even if it is $5 more.
___________________________________
I was skeptical about this box after reading the reviews but I have been really disappointed in Sephora Play for the last several months and have considered cancelling. Yes, this one is $15 vs. $10 but so far all the products are one or some combination of 1) something I've seen but have been curious about trying, 2) something totally new and unique, 3) good sized products (most are deluxe sample size but there's been full size as well). I have seen absolutely no repeats or similar products from month to month which has been my biggest complaint about Sephora Play. Everything has been fresh and not old, I'm pretty happy with this subscription box.

All wrapped up like there should be a plant in there, and NOTHING. I should note that I ordered another plant that came in the same box and was fine. The String of Hearts was EMPTY. Buyer beware.

To Succulent Box:

How dare you screw around with me 3 times!!! I wrote that in the previous email, but you instead perhaps decided to get even instead. You are completely fraudulent and in this latest situation possibly criminal in sending me a plant meant to be killed. Attached are the pictures. First you sent me a smaller/cheaper replacement that was at least healthy. I asked for a refund either in money for the difference in price of sizes, or additional plant material to make up the difference. The second, yet another empty pot arrived yesterday 07/27/22. Apparently this was the additional plant material I requested. But it was ANOTHER apparently empty pot. But with this one when I dug around in the soil I found the plant at the BOTTOM of the pot, DEAD. As if you intentionally turned the pot upsidedown so the plant was on the bottom and would arrive dead. Criminal intent right there. Your company is a disgrace. You need to be shut down. You intentionally sent me a buried plant!!! Is this some sick revenge??? I demand a refund of the amount of the price difference between the 4 inch plant you sent me of String of Hearts and the 6 inch plant I paid for. I have alerted paypal of this situation for their assistance in getting a monetary refund. I am also going to place this new incident on any review sites I can find. This is ridiculous.

text:

The big difference between this and TokyoTreat is that TokyoTreat has a bottled drink or two and has more mainstream sweet snacks. Bokksu seems to be dry teas and more savory snacks than sweets. It's also less mainstream stuff (ie no Pocky). They are both different so it depends on your tastes as to which is better.

Of course, what you get in the box is a lot less than what you'd get for the same money if you could buy it yourself, but that's true with any of these Japanese subscription services - you pay for the handling and especially shipping from Japan.

title: Great educational tool
text:
Outstanding experience for kids! The November box had two experiments, and the December box has just arrived. The way it is set up is that the first shipment has a starter kit - commonly used tools - and a first actual subscription items to make 2 experiments, while the second (and I assume further) boxes only have the next 2 experiments.

Our first box had the volcano and carbon snake experiments, both very easy to do and very impressive. Setup is great, there is a companion app you run on the phone which tells you what to do, and there is even a small set for the phone so you don't need to hold it while experimenting. Another nice thing is that they sent more materials than needed for a single try of experiment, so you can actually repeat 1-2 extra times.

Highly recommended!

text: Over the years, I have subscribed to several Japanese snack boxes and Bokksu is one of the best. The snacks are not the cheap daigashi (cheap candy) that many of the other boxes include. I like that they include allergen and nutrition information, because I don't like fish or shrimp, so I could easily avoid fishy flavored snacks. They also state if the snack is vegetarian, even in they classic box, so it is good for families that have member with eating restrictions such as vegetarian or halal. Good job, American Plant Exchange, you raised these plants well, hardened them off professionally and packed them up expertly, and I'm pretty sure they are both going to make it! ( No pictures, you do not want to see this plant right now! )

title: Ignore the people with no sense of fun. Pusheen Box is great.
text:
I have subscribed to the Pusheen box for a couple of years now. My wife loves Pusheen and every month is a new fun surprise for her. Before you purchase, you have to understand, not every box is an "A+". All of these subscription "mystery boxes" are a little bit .. uneven. Some boxes are "ok that's all cool" and then there are some (like the Fall 2020) that just arrived) that absolutely knock the socks off of the recipient. Fall 2020 was the best box yet.

I will say that the Fall and Winter boxes seem to be the best; I think that is partially because of the nature of the season. In Fall and Winter, you tend to get something warm and fuzzy like a hoodie or a blanket, etc. The Spring and Summer boxes are always good too but think about it.. They can't exactly send you a Pusheen bikini (sizing that for the general public would be impossible), so spring and summer tend to be more display items.

For $50, every month I get to see my wife light up like a kid again with fun little trinkets, clothes, blankets, shoes, you name it. I hope they keep going with this for years to come.

title: Great product. Why are y'all so grumpy with the reviews...
text: I do have some drawing/doodling ability, but I have trouble coming up with ideas for new things so I decided to subscribe to Artsnacks. I received quality art products in complementary colors. I got to try new types of art supplies, and more importantly, I got some boundaries to play in. I had these certain colors, and these types of supplies, and I just had to make something cool with them. So, I did. For all of the reviewers complaining about the cost of the products and stating that you could have found an item cheaper on sale somewhere: why don't you go and do that? You goal is to find the cheapest value, so maybe you would be happier searching online for a price that suits you. I have found the prices that Artsnacks lists to be in the range for what the item sells for. For those of you complaining about the randomness of the supplies: that's the point. You should subscribe to this if you want to try new (art) things. Anyway. I liked my items. I made a silly drawing. It made me laugh. I got to try a Copic marker. Was fun, but I think I liked the cheaper KingArt color brush pens much more than the Copic marker. The lead pencil was great, and Stabilo markers are always cool, but I use them for writing, so using them for art was new. So, maybe you should give it a try.

title: Do you need random trash in your life??!!?? Look no further!
text:
Are you a 40'ish year old man? Have you been in the market for a fake leather pencil case? Perhaps a tied-dyed lapel pin that says GQ on it with a smiley face? Maybe you've been looking for the perfect 2 month coupon for an online meditation class that renews at $69.99 after the two months are up? If this sounds like you, look no further than the *BEST STUFF OF GQ!!!!!

You know it's the Best Stuff of GQ because it says so right on the box. Some cheap pre-workout that has who-knows-what in it will be sure to greet you the moment you open this little cube of excitement. Dig a little deeper and you'll find a 20% discount coupon for some junk that you'd never buy in the first place! AMAZING!

Looking for the perfect twine to wrap around your neck given the current state of the US election? GQ has you covered as well! COCONUT flavoured dental floss is included so you can use it for whatever arts and crafts project you have while you're sitting on the floor doing online meditation (for only 2 months, mind you) while trying to fit the rest of the junk into your brand-new faux-leather pencil case!

Act now and you'll receive a coupon for a very feminine sheep blanket! It comes in every colour you can think of as long as you only want white.

And are you completely unmotivated????! The "Impact Cards" will take your motivation from a 0.00 to a stylish 0.00 in no time. Open the deck of playing cards, read the random "feel good" saying on the card, and then go right back to bed. See! It worked in no-time flat! AMAZING! It's GQQQQQQQQ! WOWZERS!

(*By "Best Stuff" we really mean we went through the amazon warehouse and picked out everything that hasn't sold in the past 5 years and crammed as much as of it as possible into this tiny black box. It's the BEST STUFF that GQ could possibly (probably) find for free, hanging out in a dilapidated warehouse on the outskirts of a very stabby, but extremely GQ'ish, town!)

Oh, the deodorant is useful for a man. And your wife/girlfriend/downstairs female neightbour will love the "replenishing masks" that comes with it that will be of no use to you!

DID I MENTION THERE ARE MORE DISCOUNT COUPONS FOR ADDITONAL TRASH!!?!!! ACT NOW!

All in all, it's well worth the $50 bucks to give the all children/women/trash cans in your life the random junk that comes crammed into this tiny little box!

IT'S AMAZING (ly a total waste of money!) Buy 3 to fill up all the refuse bins in your life!

title: So-so first box, hoping it improves
text:
I was a founder with the original MCC box when Funko was producing it, so I haven't missed a box yet. Now that Amazon has taken it over, I am optimistic that the box will get better. For those that are unfamiliar with the MCC Box, when Funko started it, each box was unique and had comic print on the inside of the box that corresponded with the box theme. The box also contained a contents card so you knew what was in the box, a pin, a patch, an exclusive variant cover comic, a shirt (or on rare occasions a hat), an exclusive Pop figure and several smaller Funko items.

With that being said, let's start off with the POSITIVES about the Deadpool box ....the Pop figure was nice and unique, and the luggage tag was nice. The NUETRALS are the taco truck 2 taco holder and the fairly unimpressive generic box. It is a different item that I never would have thought to sought out on my own. The NEGATIVES are the Pop keychain (not impressed), the lack of a contents card listing the items that are contained within the box, no exclusive variant cover comic, no wearable item, no pin, and no patch. I will stay subscribed at this point to see where Amazon goes with this, but if the quality of items doesn't increase....there are other things I can, AND WILL, spend my money on.

title: Bookshelf Lottery Ticket
text:
If you've ever bought a loot crate, you know what to expect. Personally, I'm chasing Funkos. I love having them in my office and a few around my house. Like Loot Crate, you have to get the right box at the right time to really feel like your investment in decoration or memorabilia was worth it. Otherwise, it's cannon fodder for a garage sale.

I've bought three of these Bounty Boxes. The first was the Jabba Skiff box. I was a little disappointed. Who wants a Klaatu funko - literally reselling for 99 cents plus shipping on Ebay? The Lando Skiff Guard is cool I guess, but not something I would buy. Luckily, I got some shot glasses to drown my sorrows. $24 for the two funkos, $6 for the shot glasses, really not a bad deal if you squint your eyes and like the funkos.

I meant to cancel my subscription but wound up getting the Dagobah box by mistake. Luckily, it has a pretty cool movie moment where Luke is looking at his own head in the cave. YES! This is what i wanted. $30 for a movie moment is what you would pay in retail. To get a keychain and a miniature Yoda bobble, gravy.

I bought my third box after it had been released for $39.99. I really wanted the "Boba's Bounty" movie moment. I think this may be my strategy moving forward. Pay $10 more and only get the boxes that I want. $40 is a steep price for a funko, but i think it could increase in value and even if it doesn't, it looks awesome and I have a few people ask where I got it, so bonus points.

text: Depending on what level you choose the items being provided could be hit or miss. I selected "Premium" and after two boxes of random provided items, I think about 35-40% I could use. For 175+ dollars a month I am likely going to cancel as you the customer have no real ability to select items you may want, it really depends on who is packing the specific month's item. If you are a military-retired individual I would hold off on purchasing this box as likely you could go to several sites and get the items for your weapon, personal survival set-up, and other tactical related gear which could be verified as "US made" and durable. I received two items of decent value, a good flashlight and a decent knife. The picture on Amazon gives the impression that each box typically has this much gear packed inside, this is not the cases for the second highest tier of boxes offered. I have the "Premium" level and it usually has one or two mid size items and a lot of smaller pieces of gear. If you seek the "Legendary" level you are spending 550 dollars plus shipping for a small crate but for that much I could select a number of decent scopes, gear, attachments for weapons, knives, etc. I think I will check my 3rd box coming in and if it is still not that noteworthy I will cancel my subscription. title: Poor Customer Service and My Children Didn't Like The Builds
text:
Fun idea, however, would not recommend.

Delivery was inconsistent throughout the year with my two annual subscriptions. But that wasn't why we cancelled our subscriptions. We have two boys that LOVE legos and building toys. We got an annual subscription for each of them. We thought this would be the perfect subscription for them, but unfortunately, the builds weren't very exciting or "fun", resulting in many boxes that haven't been touched or reluctantly completed.

Cancelling the subscription is very difficult and there is a penalty fee. Because of the lackluster appeal to my kids, midway into our 12 month subscription, I set our account to not auto-renew but apparently the system didn't record it. Because of this we incurred a penalty fee when I tried to reach someone to cancel our subscriptions. I cancelled in my subscription account online, but was charged anyway and then I got notification that my monthly subscription had shipped. Customer service was difficult to reach and they are not empowered to remedy the situation. My customer service representative was fairly difficult to work with, once I did find someone via email and unfortunately, my interaction with them was very negative. They were sarcastic and rude about how I couldn't figure out how to cancel my subscription - it came across via email after my request for cancellation was clear.

The only advantage of subscribing to Brickloot is the convenience of having a brick building surprise in the mail each month, however, the inconsistency of delivery and the unimaginative building toys that come outweigh the convenience and surprise.

title: Got this subscription for my wife, I am embarrassed
text:
Well....here’s the deal. I subscribed to this Marvel fan pack for my wife. She has always been an avid follower of The Marvel Universe and I figured this was the perfect thing to surprise her with. I had read thru all the less than encouraging reviews before her box got here and thought ,oops I may have made a mistake here. After reading about only partial boxes where not everyone got the same items and the less than thrilled attitudes of serious collectors I was worried . Well, I figured it was the first shipment after the Marvel/Funko merger, and she would be getting the next box and it should be much better right? Well, I kid you not, my wife not only did not receive the next collector box in the series (she was sent the Deadpool box), And, she was sent a box with only 3 fricken items in it.
A lot of people complained about the items they received and I agreed with most of them. But how about getting your first fan box which was to have 4-7 top quality collectors items in it and having only three things in the whole box!!!!, the main Deadpool on the unicorn, a key chain and a piece of crap taco truck.

I am flabbergasted and am leaving it up to my wife as to whether she wants to give it one more try or just cancel the subscription as an idea that was meant well but fell short.

I am so angry at this joke that I can’t figure out why anyone would want to continue their sub knowing what a farce Funko and Amazon have made out of this. Oh well live and learn.

What a rip-off!!! $30 for a $5 statue a .50 key chain and a plastic taco piece of trash that has no monitory value!

text:
I was gifting quarterly subscriptions to 13 kids (relatives and friends) of all ages for about 4 years. Generally, the book selection was good, and the kids (and parents) loved getting their boxes. The two drawbacks were that the boxes could not be tailored for gender and grade (only age), and since I was paying for the subscription, the advance notice of the default selection came to me, not to the parents, so it was difficult to manage any desired selection changes. And then, unfortunately, the quarterly option was ended abruptly, and Amazon cancelled my subscription with little notice.
I am disappointed that I can no longer participate. I hope that Amazon will reconsider the delivery frequency and will find a way to facilitate parental input when someone other than the parents is gifting the subscription!!

title: Only one toy and bag of treats for cats- nothing like pictured!
text:
I ordered this directly from RescueBox, not Amazon, but thought buyer should beware. I liked the idea of my purchase supporting rescues and shelters so I decided to try the cat box for my kitties after seeing the types of toys and treats offered for both dogs and cats. (Thought the dog toys looks way too flimsy for my hounds, but figured my cats would be fine with most any toy.)
I was sadly disappointed to receive our RescueBox today containing only one dollar store quality toy and a very small bag of treats (2.5 oz) I had signed up for the monthly box which costs $29.95! (Plus tax for a few states, which did not include mine, but was charged anyway.)

All the sample boxes showed several toys and treats and accessories with about 5 per box. It wasn't even sent in a box!!! (Which at least would have made another toy for the cats.) It was just a mailing envelope!

Thankfully I was home to receive it and accessed my account immediately to cancel any further shipments. (With one day to spare!) But beware, the box is nothing like advertised, and with long shipping times, it is possible that you would be billed again before even receiving your box if you sign up for a subscription. According to the website, they bill on the 12th of the month, so would have to be cancelled prior to that. (And our package came on the 10th!)
I'll stick to ordering toys and treats separately on Amazon and just make my donations directly to my local shelters and rescues.

title: Fast and (so far) yummy
text:
I just got my first shipment of the Original box and I'm so thrilled I couldn't wait until I'd tried all of them to write a review. I've been in a tea rut for a while, since the two loose leaf shops in my area both closed down within a year of each other and I was excited to try new things.

First, they shipped the October box in plenty of time for me to get it at the beginning of the month and since I just subscribed, that seems like a pretty good response time. The October box consists of four offerings and so far I have only gotten to try one of them, but I'm in love already and I'm super-excited about the other three. I brew my own kombucha at home so I fully intend to use the Fujian Black they sent for that purpose (although I will try it hot, as normal before I do, but plain unflavored black tea isn't generally my favorite, so most likely this will be used for my brew). The one I have drank at the time of writing this review is the Simao Spring tips and I like it a lot more than I expected to. The bag describes it as having "notes of sweet potato, caramel, nuts, fruits and spices" and that is not a bad description for this tea at all. I'm a huge fan of "Goguma" (sweet potato) lattes and this remind me a lot of those, especially when mixed with a bit of heavy cream. The third bag is Kathmandu Cosmos, which is described as being a chai blend. I'm addicted to chai so I can't wait to try this one. Last is a the Pacific Peppermint, described as an herbal tea. It will be nice to have some peppermint around again, especially with the weather starting to cool down.

I love the speed these came in and the amount I got for the price. I tend to be a bit picky when it comes to tea and I've paid more money for less product and sometimes gotten less enjoyment from some of those past buys. According to the literature in the packaging Tea Runners will be coming soon to Amazon Prime, so I'm hoping that means if there is a sample I like, I'll be able to order it in larger amounts at some point in the future.

I'll update this review if anything particularly funky happens with my test sips of the other three teas but if I haven't updated in a few days, assume the best. It's early, but so far I highly recommend this subscription.

title: Big Let Down
text: When I first saw the Marvel Studios box being offered I was pretty excited. I have never bought a box of any kind before this. The first 10 years were packed with many memorable moments and characters so I really thought something awesome was in store. Sad to say I was really let down by what came in it. Two mini Funko figures (gold colored..woohoo), a golden PEZ (again..woohoo),and a Funko box with a scene from Iron Man 2 of Iron Man fighting Whiplash. Really? That was the big item? Not Cap and Iron Man slugging it out from Civil War. Not any scene from any Avengers movie. Not even a scene from the first Iron Man (which kicked off the whole MCU) of Tony fighting Obadiah. Nope. Iron Man 2. Way to go guys. Of all the movies out there you went with that. I guess I should be greatful it wasn’t Iron Man 3 but still. If it’d came with a shirt or something maybe I’d have been more pleased but I just felt like the picks for this celebration of the first 10 years of cinematic history were a huge let down. I cancelled my membership immediately. Overall it is what they say. A box for $30 with a value of slightly more than that. Just don’t hope to get something you’ll actually be happy you paid $30 for.  Buy at your own risk of course but I’d be happier spending my money on something I actually wanted instead of a box of things I couldn’t care less about and will try to sell it or even give it away. What a shame.

title: Vegan but not healthy
text: I really wanted to give this a 5-star because I support all efforts to make a vegan lifestyle fun and easy! I felt the description of the snacks (when I subscribed) is misleading, however. I am very clear that vegan does not equal healthy, but I was in a state of disappointment to open our first box and find candy treats that had food dyes like Red 40 and lots of artificial flavor or “natural” flavors added. After reading the description I did think I was receiving a healthy box of fun snacks. I don’t think any packaged foods qualify as “healthy” by all means...of course they are somewhat processed and usually high in salt or oils...but fake colors, flavors, etc!?? That’s just gross and unacceptable. You could call any box of junk food vegan, for the most part: a lot of things are vegan, but I was under the impression that this would be a more natural and forward thinking curated selection of plant based snacks. Some of the things were great, but at least four items we just chose to throw out, which was a big bummer to me because then I was in a position to decide between not being wasteful, or not feeding my family garbage. I am sad because I thought this was a fun idea for our plant-based family! I love the idea behind it, and the support for the animals and companies pushing plant based snacks forward.

title: Poorly Designed Program
text:
This program design has many flaws, I have contacted Amazon CS several times and provided my feedback but they have just made it even worse. This program does not offer any flexibility in making a customer selects his toy, it's completely based on "random" system selection of a toy within a specific price range. It's so difficult to get to know what the system will "throw" at you till the order has been generated. Alternatively, Amazon should provide a specific number of toys (5 to 8) per month, out of which a customer can select one given the wide spectrum of what STEM can offer (I assume two toys for each category would be enough, as in 2 for science, 2 for technology, etc.) . The only option available at the moment is to cancel the order if the toy is not adequate - which occurred to me several times - and subsequently cancel your membership and re-join again in order to trigger the system order generation. I found myself working for the system instead of the other way around, it was quite mundane and boring to cancel and join several times to wish that the system will provide a proper and real STEM item.

Customer Service acknowledged that the system is still new and it might have some design flaws, however, the only thing they have implemented since I contacted them a couple of months ago is limiting the times a customer can cancel and re-join the program for reasons I am not aware of..

title: Great Fun, STEM Inspiration, and Learning
text:
The MEL Chemistry kit contains everything needed for the experiment including goggles. The starter kit also has VR goggles to use the excellent MEL chemistry app. The first month's kit has two experiments. The directions are simple and easy to follow. I like their version of the carbon snake experiment because it uses much safer chemicals than the version usually seen yet it it still spectacular.

The second month's kit involves tin metal. One experiment makes a dendrite, the other a hedgehog. Both are beautiful.

What I like most about the kit is the meticulous attention to detail. For example, the instructions direct the user to add sodium bicarbonate to the heating fuel to make the flame visible. This makes the experiment safer but also opens up a discussion about luminescence. The kit also includes thermostickers that can be affixed to all equipment that will be heated, eliminating the old saw that "Hot and cold glassware look alike."

title: Box contains toxic products! Please be careful!
text:
I have been a subscriber for a while and have generally enjoyed their products. However, after spraying the attached dental spray in my dogs’ mouths, I noticed the ingredient Xylitol. This artificial sweetener is HIGHLY toxic in dogs. When speaking with someone at Box Dog she informed me that there is recent research which suggests trace amounts of xylitol are not dangerous. This study does not appear to take into consideration diet or medical conditions (like unregulated diabetes, which would exacerbate the affects potentially making even trace amounts poisonous) and appears to be fairly new (only a few years old). I am disappointed that the company chooses to incorporate controversial ingredients without any sort of disclaimer. The risk they take endangering animals and not educating their owners is mind blowing. Even if one dog in 2500 dies it’s too many (she mentioned over 2000 dogs have used this without any reported issues). I’m not interested in subscription boxes so I can experiment with new studies in reducing plaque on their teeth. No part of that is worth the chance of the potential long term damage trace amounts do to the animals. My vet has advised 48 hour monitoring to ensure my dogs are not at risk. I have unsubscribed from this service and hope that they rethink the moral obligations the company has as a trusted provider of pet products. There are plenty of dental sprays with no xylitol. If they are cost prohibitive, please don’t cut corners to create diversity in your boxes. I would rather have another bag of safe treats with no medical benefits than be tricked into feeding my dogs something potentially harmful and understudied in this context. If you choose to include this product moving forward, PLEASE PLEASE include some sort of card that alerts owners to the presence and controversy and directs them to the study via a QR code or something. I will be spending the next 2 days in the emergency vet for something that is probably no big deal, but because this isn’t a widely accepted study or a “fact” known throughout the medical community, this companies disregard for transparency will cost me almost $2,000.

EDIT: my dogs survived, as expected, and never showed any signs of any kind of issues. My vet has advised to throw this product away or put it in a box “until more research is done and published”.

They give you three stripes a month. I thought this was perfect as I was getting back into crochet and needed something to help me relearn stitches, remember how to read patterns, and be a side project while I worked on a few other smaller things. The yarn quality is excellent. The design is diverse and interesting. You rarely do the same stitch twice. I often look at my afghan now to pick patterns for other projects! My only complaint is that the written instructions aren’t quite enough, especially at the beginning. You need to watch the videos. That’s not really my learning style so it was a bit hard at first, but certainly not a reason not to buy. I have subscribed to other Annie’s kit clubs since this (which was my first) and I love this concept and am so glad I did it. title: Very good, might try the same company for different subscription
text:
***UPDATE: I have to dispute some of the reviews here about cost per ounce. The pricing here is fair for the quality you are getting. A 30-second Google search can confirm this. As an example, I love silver needle white tea and this runs around $6/oz whether I buy from a high-end tea subscription or a specialty bulk shop.

I've tried a few different tea subscriptions and this one was very good. I decided to splurge on the Pure Tea collection for a little more money since I had a gift card, and do a three month trial. The teas are, as advertised, excellent quality, and despite what other reviewers have said, I think you get a pretty generous portion in the samples. I don't know if these people are making pitchers of iced tea or what, but I'm able to get 5+ cups from each sample, and there are four samples in the shipment. I've tried other services that send you a tiny packet, enough for 2-3 cups max, with 6 samples in the box. I guess it depends what you prefer.
My only complaint was the variety. Herbal teas and rooibos are my favorite, since I have to limit my caffeine intake. In 3 months (12 teas), I didn't receive any of these. All black teas with 2 greens and 1 white. In the second month, if I read the label correctly, I got two identical black teas - even grown on the same plantation/hill!- one "first harvest," the other "second harvest." In fairness, I have not brewed them side by side yet to see if there is a taste difference, but I have a feeling my palette isn't refined enough to notice anyway.
Now that I've established what a fussy old woman I am, I will reiterate the tea is excellent quality across the board. Based on that, I see this company also offers an non-caffeine subscription, so I might give that a try.

That said, I'm disappointed that the two teas I have brewed so far (the orange rooibus and Blue Lady Grey) had such strong scents when I first opened them and then taste fine; not great, not terribly flavorful. I don't typically drink oolong or green, and given that I strongly prefer black and herbal teas, I have a hard time imagining I would like the other two left in this box.

While I am very far from an expert on tea leaf grading, a general indicator of quality when it comes to teas, I looked at the remnants of the Blue Lady Grey and it seems to be broken leaf, which is on the lower end of loose leaf teas. Overall, I am happy I only spent $5 on this box, but I do not plan on continuing my subscription.

title: I'm a cook...and this is still worth it
text:
Can you find your own recipes for free on the internet? Yes. Can you go to Walmart and get your own utensils for cheap? Yes. Can you teach your kids to cook yourself? Yes. Of course you can do all this for pennies a month. This company doesn't deny that. But they still provide something unique.

Raddishkids changed how my 11-year-old daughter taught herself to cook. She wanted recipes she could understand HERSELF. She wanted to be able to cook an entire meal without me hovering around her, telling her what to do, and explaining the recipes she found online. The recipes are clearly explained, colorful, easy, and they TASTE GOOD. We have just completed a year's subscription and signed up for another year. She has become confident in her cooking ability.

You are not paying $24 for a spatula. You are paying for the company's ideas, tested recipes, ability to pick appropriate skills, etc. Each month my daughter can't wait for what RaddishKids sends her in the mail. This subscription will help your child become independent in the kitchen! That's worth $24 a month to me.

title: Stay away - xylitol!
text: I've been a box dog subscriber for a couple years, and while most of the toys don't stand up to my tough chewer chocolate lab, she's just a beast with toys. So I'm okay with the toy quality. However we just received our final box, the winter box, as it contained this dental spray. The ingredient list clearly states xylitol. And we are supposed to put this in our dog's mouths?! I've emailed them to confirm if this is correct, and I hope it's a misprint. But I'm just sick thinking of how many people may have ordered this box, got this dental spray, and didn't read the ingredients. And now they have lost their dog due to the toxicity of the xylitol. Stay away from this company. Because if I'm supposed to trust a company to provide toys and treats for my dog, I'd think they'd be well versed on xylitol being fatal.

title: This is what greed looks like
text: Not worth the money!  When the Allure Beauty Boxes were $15/month, it was a great deal and value.  But as is life, nothing last forever.  And, that means the Allure Beauty box, as those of us who were loyal customers can attest.  To me, the box I received at the new and improved price of $23.00 was basically the same as the $15.00 a month subscription.  The company went up a ridiculous $8.00 a box.  Let that sink in for a minute.  $8.00 a month increase and it was not any better or more,of a value than before the increase. It looked the same.  You are promised at least three (code for 3, no more) full size products.  Well, one of the full size products was a bottle of nail polish!  The other two products claimed full size, but the products did not appear as such.  Allure's premiere better than ever box was a big fat dud.  And, it was the premiere box.  Makes you wonder what the rest of the boxes will be like.  To me it screams GREED and no concern for their loyal customers.  Let's increase the subscription $8.00 a month cause other beauty box subs are getting that much and send the customer the same box as before, they will not know any difference.  Well, Allure, we do know the difference and you can keep your subscription box.  You just lost a long, loyal customer.

text: Absolute ripoff! I've spent over $230 on these "supply crates", and I've received maybe $50 worth of product. My last crate literally had loose toothpicks, a $2 first aid kit, and some toxic junk that you put on a fire to make the flames change colors.  The instructions on the package literally say to avoid the smoke because of the harmful fumes.  And I was charged for this crate after I told them to cancel my membership. The one I received before that had a burlap sack in it, along with an inflatable chair that can be bought from Five Below, a keychain, and a rubber ruler which was a duplicate item from the first box I got.  I've also received a cheap "tactical" flashlight and a camping stove which sells for $15 and is the only name-brand item I've received.  They charge $40 for shipping, and it takes a month to arrive so that you're charged for the next crate before receiving the current one. That way you always pay for an extra one after you receive the absolute crap they send and decide to cancel.  I know everybody has to make money, but they are going overboard to rip people off. The company they got all their "tactical" stuff from has apparently gone out of business. The website has been down for over a month. So I don't know what they're going to do now to trick people into signing up.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

title: Great customer service and quality!!
text:
This subscription was a gift for my mom for Mother’s Day and she received her first one in May. She doesn’t live nearby and loves to crochet so I thought it might be fun for her to get something new every month to work on. At first we thought some things had been left out of the package as we only saw one skein of yarn and found no pattern in the bag. We were wrong, but I’ll get to that part.

I sent Jenna a message providing my personal email address (spelled out with spaces) letting her know the issue and told her I’d be happy to send her a photo of what was sent so she could see what was missing if she wanted to email me there. This started a very interesting and fun (I thought so anyway lol) game of message tag where we both attempted to figure out how to fool the algorithm because Amazon removed the address from four different messages between us. I’m glad she has a sense of humor because my last one was a little ridiculous. 😂

Turns out it was a case of user error and the package had everything promised. The smaller skein was inside of the larger skein for a pretty presentation and the pattern was online...oops! 🙄

The fact Jenna was so willing to spend hours to do all of this messaging and then not tell me I should maybe try reading thoroughly before all of that just shows how awesome she is and how much she wants to ensure her customers are satisfied. The colors are beautiful and my mom is looking forward to using her yarn hooks and making something with it. If you are considering this subscription for yourself or someone else, you won’t find a better person or product.

Thank you so much Jenna!

title: Great Service and an Excellent Value.
text:
Dungeon in a Box?
Yes, please!
As a busy Dad and DM, it's sometimes challenging to put together an exciting adventure for our weekly family D&D session.
Dungeon in a Box makes it incredibly easy by giving you everything you need to either add it to an existing campaign or to follow the whole Dungeon in a Box one-year adventure arc.
The Box comes with a complex story campaign book; you can get in either 5e or the Pathfinder ruleset, foldable terrain, super detailed unpainted high-quality 3D Mini, excellent double-sided player maps, and their exclusive double-sided 2d (Skinny Mini) miniatures with elaborate characters and vibrant artwork.
Honestly, I can't recommend this subscription service enough, and I would be happy to answer any questions anyone has about the service.
It has already brought hours of enjoyment to our Campaign.

These are great activities to do WITH your child. Yes, with your child. We played the game together and the game board has a nice envelope on the back to store the pieces - teach your child how to gently put them away and take them out and it will last awhile.

title: mostly seems like a way for Amazon to clear out inventory
text:
If you are a new collector, you are better off digging for used and other deals. If you don't know a lot of classic, then this may be a way to gain some exposure but the value is not very good as many items are cheaper by a couple dollars if purchased direct from amazon.

For those with medium to large collections already you will probably return 80-90% of what they send you. I have only kept 2 or 3 of the 10 or so they have sent and had ~250 records. Returns roughly were based on 1/3 not being something I wanted, 1/3 being something I already had, 1/3 being overpriced.

Will probably cancel in another month or two but was holding out for Amazon to make some improvements based on previous comments. Primarily, they need to have set date each month to review what they are going to send and have a deadline to skip. Currently it is random and you have to login to amazon and view orders and there is ~24 hours or so that you may be able to catch it and skip. Way too random. Seems strategic of amazon to ship things banking on people not returning them if they have in hand. This seems shady and ultimately is some plan for Amazon to clear out inventory that isn't selling.

Another change Amazon still hasn't added despite suggestions, is a swap option. If each month there was an opportunity to swap for a few other choices, maybe I wouldn't be sending so many back. This could possibly still help them clear out inventory as greater chance of something I could actually want.

Given the value is poor many months, it is hard to recommend this for any collector. If you are disciplined about returns and have a convenient way to return amazon orders, then you have nothing to loose and maybe the continued loss in shipping expenses will motivate Amazon to implement changes. Maybe not as Amazon could just pass along the increased cost to consumers and continue poor ethics in how they handle employees.

Best thing you can do is buy from local small record stores. To my ears, these classics sound better on original pressings so buy used if you can. Some remasters from the original tapes are great, but the technology of the time was optimized for the vinyl format and sound the bands wanted. Clean copies of used records can be found for better prices than many of these Amazon record of the month classics.

title: Still Hoping....
text: Just to establish my bona fides, I have been to Japan multiple times over the years for periods of up to 4-6 weeks. So I know my Japanese snacks. I purchased a 3-Bokksu subscription as a surprise gift for my family to cheer us up during Covid quarantine. First box--the classic--was fantastic. Excellent array, interesting snacks, things you would not find at a Japanese market in the U.S. 100% recommend, thoroughly enjoyed. The second box....Well, it was sakura (cherry blossom) themed for spring. Which is completely appropriate and understandable. The thing is, cherry and plum blossom snacks are just not that tasty, especially to an American palate. Mayn things tasted kind of like cough syrup, very chemical. Others tasted less like sour ume (plum) and more like shiso leaf (not a fan). Rather than eyeing that extra piece left over after we'd divided up a snack in that box we all "graciously" urged the others in the family to take it, no, really, please. So I would give box #1 5 stars and box #2 3 stars...at best. Also, there were several items in the sakura box that I'm pretty sure I could've gotten for under $5 at my local Japanese market in the U.S. So....I guess will see how box #3 is. I hope for the best.  i can't say, though, that  I regret my purchase so far--everyone has enjoyed the anticipation of getting the snacks, opening them, going through the ritual of trying them even if they weren't that great--but I really hope the next box meets the quality of the first one!

title: Super fun way to learn to code!
text:
My kids have worked a bit with Hour of Code through their school and liked it, so when I came across Bitsbox, I thought it would be a great way to continue to develop their interest in coding. When I showed them the Bitsbox website and asked if they were interested, my 12yo was sort of "meh" about it but my 8yo was really excited. When the first box arrived, the 8yo built her first app "Doggleheads" where you can make a dog's head bobble back and forth on its body like a bobblehead. When the 12yo saw it, he immediately wanted to try it too. They spent the next two hours coding and giggling over the set of apps included with the first box. When they were done with their creations, we were able to scan the QR code on the screen to send the apps to friends and family.

The first box included a getting started guide, a guide for parents, a bunch of full-color cards with apps the kids can code, and an "Apper Keeper" binder where you can keep the app cards. All you have to do is go to the website included, type in a 4-digit code for the app you want to build, and then follow the step-by-step instructions for coding the app. I think the part I love the most is that it's super simple to figure out, but with a basic foundation kids can really go nuts and customize the apps to the limit of their own creativity. My 8yo was happy mixing and matching different dog heads and bodies while my 12yo figured out how to make the dogs run around the screen, sing Christmas songs, and even explode when they ran into each other (these were not part of the instructions!) My 8yo was slower with coding because you have to type in each command and she's not as confident using a keyboard. This is different from Hour of Code which mostly uses visual blocks of code that kids move around rather than type in. But my 12yo was very quick and liked the speed and freedom of typing in whatever commands he wanted. For both of them, having the program indicate where they made an error was really helpful, and this helped show them the importance of precision with code where even a missing comma can make the entire program not work.

Compared to the $400+ local in-person coding classes I was also considering, the monthly subscription cost of Bitsbox is a great deal and the kids really didn't need any help figuring things out on their own. The only downside was they ran out of new apps to code in the first few days so are anxiously waiting for the next month's box. We would completely recommend trying it out!

title: Disappointing and little bang for the buck.
text: Look at the example they provide that is allegedly "$50" value:  an exclusive Venom Pop ($12 or generously $15), a Venom-Pop t-shirt ($10-$15), a sticker ($2), a stress ball ($2), and a mini Venom ($1-$2).  If you really like every thing in the box, it's a reasonable value, but a) it's not an exceptional value and b) one probably won't be thrilled with most of the items included.  So unless you enjoy of bi-monthly surprise of getting stuff you wouldn't have bought given the choice, I recommend passing on this.  Spend the money on a Pop figure and a t-shirt you really want, and you'll probably be happier.  Don't worry about the fear of missing out with these boxes.  Unlike the original Marvel Collector Corps boxes that were shipped directly from Funko, you can't count on these Amazon boxes to include anything exceptional.

title: Not fun, and not buying another
text:
OK I've beaten several escape rooms but the riddles here ruin the whole thing. Referring to "Escape from Howling Hotel." There's a difference between making a mental muscle riddle and just showing off as a know-it-all, and this game fails that hands down. Out of the 6 major riddles, 4 were completely unsolvable without looking in the cheat book. Each one required some "ah ha" moment to deduce what the hell the riddle author was thinking, and if that moment just, like, doesn't arrive...then you're stuck in a infuriating dead end.
The first riddle all by itself is convoluted enough to make you want to quit the game before you even begin. You'd think the game would ease you in gently, giving you a softball to get settled in and feel the rush of early success...but oh hell no. Contrary to more compassionate view, the game throws a three part monster riddle at you. Except it never tells you its in three parts. Except each part relies on a singular inspiration of "ah ha" that just may not ever arrive. "Inspiration" and "deduction" are NOT the same thing. Anyone can deduce, where you just grind muscle and put in the time an eventually you'll get it. Those are fun. But "inspiration" is pure pass or fail. Either you have a Eureka moment, THREE TIMES, or the game crashes and burns on the very first level.
The other riddles were just as bad.
One in particular, mentioned by other reviewers (deservedly so, as its preposterous), concerns a grandfather clock, and deducing that the author has some obscure and arcane "pseudonym" for grandfather clocks, a "pseudonym" which he never bothered to tell the rest of us. A "pseudonym" that I immediately googled to see what the flip the author was referring to...finding nothing. Its nonsense, the author made it up completely and just hoped real hard the players could read his mind.
FOUR riddles were like that. FOUR riddles were completely unsolvable and unplayable unless you read the authors mind. Each one requiring outrageous leaps of mental illogic to get anywhere.
The last puzzle of the game is also wrong. You have to arrange guests at a dinner table to certain restrictions, except the solution I came up was more accurate than what was in the clue manual.
I've had it. To scour over a riddle, to watch the clock tick by as you're getting nowhere and have to take the mental compromise of reading the cheat book....it just isnt fun. I've seen it done better. I had little to no fun playing Howling Hotel and fully recommend everyone else stay far away as well.
Never buying from them again.

title: Experiment didn't work at all, despite repeated attempts.
text:
My son was sooo excited about doing a science experiment that worked properly. We had high hopes for MEL Science kits given the reviews and didn't mind the hefty price of the subscription as long as the kits worked. Terribly terribly disappointed because:

1) The kit took almost 8 weeks to arrive since the order was placed. This is a ridiculous amount of shipping delay for an order placed within the US (we're in the Bay Area, California and most shipped items arrive within a week). My kid was eagerly awaiting the shipment and impatient with the shipping delays.

2) The worst part was that the kits didn't work at all. The packaging was good and we were really hopeful given all the safety equipment that something exciting would happen but it was a complete dud. We followed all the instructions precisely not just once but twice. Same results.

3) When I reached out to the seller for a return label for the defective item, they didn't get back to me with one. I tried paying for shipping, which apparently costs more than the ~$43 I paid for the item itself, so returning the item seems pointless.

Disappointing customer service on top of a poor product :(

title: Won't get you started...
text:
First, what you see in the provided "example kits" picture is unfortunately all you will get. What you won't see is just how small those skeins of yarn are: Both easily fit in the palm of my hand at the same time. If you read the kit FAQ, it will say you need additional things to complete the entire project. When you get the kit, it will not iterate what those things are, so you have to keep referencing this listing to know. Also, all of those items will cost you more individually than what you got scammed into paying for two small skeins. You'll spend another $30-$50 to get the items listed. You can literally buy multiple pounds of yarn for the price of a single month of this subscription.

None of the squares in the blanket pattern contain anything special or unique, so there are a number of free tutorials (both video and blog-style) that can teach you the same techniques and more. This also means that if you are advanced or want to learn more/get ahead, you're stuck waiting for the next month as there is no enrichment provided or go out on your own anyway.

I totally understand it takes quite a bit of time to produce the videos, money to house them, etc. if you want to run your own system, but there just isn't enough value for $30/month/person.. maybe $10-15/month would be more reasonable with an option to do a minimum 3-month subscription to get all the items you need to actually get started.

text:
Pros

Cons
-Troubles canceling subscription, do not recommend see details on journey below:

Ordered direct from Basic Man as a single time gift. Once my order went through I immediately contact customer service to ensure that only 1 set of clothing total would be sent and got confirmation in writing from the customer service manager that subscription would not renew. Despite clear instructions that only 1 set of clothing should be sent; 2 sets of clothing were delivered and I was charged 2x as customer service told me I somehow have 2 accounts instead of the 1 I signed up for when I had to contact them a 2nd time. When I logged into the account page I noticed that customer service did not cancel or even mark my account for non-renewal after customer service had "verified" that account would not be renewed, so I went ahead canceled online and received a confirmation email. Contacted customer service a 3rd time to verify ALL accounts were canceled only to be charged for 2nd month. This was all done through 2-3 business day delays as you can only reach customer service by email. I've literally had gym memberships easier to cancel than this subscription.

title: For my brother who lives in a Full Care Facility.
text:

The great thing about SnackNation's subscription is that my brother gets a surprise regularly ... and from my side it is a great because this gift it is healthy. His greatest complaint is that living in a full care facility there is not a lot for him to look forward to ... His care givers report to me that when his snack box arrives he gets so very excited and happy and each day he takes a snack, eats it and feels that he is remembered. Personally I would think this is a great gift for loved ones who live in this circumstance as well as kids away at school...
My wife said little things like this can mean so much to your loved one. It is more than a card and food/snacks are always a great gift. She said remember that his stomach is quite close to his heart ... feed his stomach with a gift of food and warm his heart! Thank you SnackNation for helping Tony feel as if he is remembered by those of us who love him!!

title: Packaging can definitely be improved
text:
Here's what I like: The price and ease of purchase that comes with a subscription. I can have succulents that I can use as gifts for clients or friends and it's a nominal cost.

Here's what I don't like: I don't know if it's the packaging or the way the plants are positioned in the boxes or what - but so far I received 2 BADLY broken plants. In each shipment there is at least a little bit of leave dropping or breakage.

These photos are of 2 separate deliveries. I watched the "bring my plant back to life" video on the site and from there it is all about patience. The leaves will start to grow roots, and then you can replant them. For the bunny ear cactus (in the box), only one of the broken leaves grew roots and the plant itself seems OK. With this latest shipment and the broken Mexican Snowball, if those leaves root successfully I could have like 8 plants. That said, I think wrapping the whole planter and around the plant itself will do more to protect during shipping than just the little bit of wrap around the stem.

Because I like container gardening, I don't mind doing the repotting and waiting it out to see if the broken leaves grow - I also turn it into a lesson with my kids. However, I am paying for 2 plants to arrive by mail monthly, so the 3-stars is because I've received 4 shipments and 2 BADLY broken plants.

title: Is this really "Hunt A Killer" or "Hunt A Scam Artist"?
text:
Ordered Hunt A Killer for my parents as a gift for Christmas. Rather than getting the first installment of the game, they got a gift card for $33.95. They used the card, and found out they could only use $30 of the $33.95 towards the first installment of the game. After setting up her account and using the card to order, the website showed no orders on record for my mom's account. My mom contacted customer service by email (their phone number does not work) on 1/17, 1/28 and 1/30. The customer service was totally confused thinking that she was buying a card for someone else (despite explaining the circumstance in writing).

Here we are, 2/4, no game, no record of an order, mysterious $3.95 unusable on a gift card, no ability to speak with a human by phone... is this really "Hunt A Killer" or "Hunt A Scam Artist"?

Overall, this has turned out to be an embarrassing gift. I wish I bought them some socks or Yahtzee or something.

title: Hidden fees, pay to read one sentence, not solve a murder
text:
As I understood from the site, the box's purpose was to solve a mystery. Instead, we found the murder weapon in <5 minutes in one piece of evidence (coroners report with the attached items at the scene). That's not hunting a killer, that's reading a sentence. So we submit the murder weapon in <5 minutes (we're not geniuses, btw so it would take anyone <5 minutes) and we're right. So we get an email to order the next box to pay another $30 to guess the motive (which we also figured out in this box, so why would we pay $30 next month)?!?

We solved the entire mystery from the box but now we need to pay another fee for the next box to take a guess at motive, killer, etc. Why include 9 pieces of evidence when you only need one to solve each episode?

I would not have purchased this subscription had I understood it would be 4+ boxes or >$120 to solve a mystery. I would have gladly paid more up front to solve the entire mystery and not spread out over 4 boxes. Instead, I feel misled by the description and brand.

If you're okay with paying >$100 to hunt a killer, not $30, this might be for you. For me, it's a waste of money and dishonest brand.

Fretboard oil ? What if your guitar(s) has(have maple fretboard(s) sealed with polyurethane ? You'll never need nor use that product. You'd have to buy a guitar with a darker open pore fretboard. Does it even apply for a manufactured fretboard instrument ?

No thanks, I have all the things I need and they don't amount to a couple => several hundreds of dollars of retail priced guitar cleaning supplies. This is marketed for the parent or relative that knows little of guitar maintenance. Something like fetboard oiling is done maybe 1-2 times a year for Rosewood. title: i see a lot of potential for this club, if QUALITY and VALUE is sustained
text:
I liked the value and quality of the first item I received with this club: I got The Clash London Calling 2xLP, the 2015 European pressing. Good value because the item usually costs about $32, but I was only charged $24.99 through this Club. Good quality because I checked the online reviews for this pressing at Discogs and elsewhere, and it seems to be widely praised.

My expectation - not a "hope," this is what I *expect* - is that this $24.99 a month program will consistently offer LP selections that normally cost $30 or more at Amazon or elsewhere. I will be disappointed and feel taken advantage of, if I am ever charged $24.99 for an item that I could purchase independently for $25 or less at Amazon or elsewhere.

Also, I was disappointed when I received this LP because the packaging was insufficient to prevent a serious corner crunch (see photo). This is the first LP I've received from Amazon that uses the "Lil Packaging" brand of vinyl mailer. Usually in my experience, Amazon has been using a brand-less option, with "wings" inside the interior of the packaging, that have done a consistently excellent job of holding the LP securely, and there are exterior "flaps" that help cushion against corner impacts. I have already sent feedback to Lil Packaging directly to encourage them to improve the design of their vinyl mailers.

I hope that the Lil Packaging brand is not going to be used with Club shipments in the future, as receiving damaged LPs every month will not be worth $24.99, regardless of how easy it is to return them.

title: My kid likes it
text:
Hit or miss. Quality is iffy; both electronics items were defective. Determining whether you've made a mistake or whether the device is defective is always somewhat of a challenge. One, a sealed microprocessor module, was practically impossible to fix, so I exchanged it. Another, a motor for a windmill, had a disconnected wire that was not difficult to fix if you have a soldering iron and some understanding of electronics. At least dad had some use.

On the other hand, my 11-year-old always enjoys getting the toy, and that's a big plus. Building, creating, and debugging gives her a sense of achievement and an inner confidence to do that is priceless.

In short, I applaud Amazon for creating this program, but I wish it were better executed.

I'd like to believe the promo photo showing Led Zep, Queen, Iron Maiden titles was for real.  Great idea.  I'd love to see a service like this with greater transparency/consistency. title: Pass on this purchase- you will be glad you didn’t spend the money
text:
I just finished one entire game.
Here is my review: It is well put together and some of the evidence items are cool. At some point it is really fun and gets you engaged. I don't think its worth the amount of money you pay for it. When you add it all up you are paying a lot for what in reality is a board game you can only play one time. The actual mystery part is fun to try and figure out but its so basic anyone can figure it out. You have to eliminate a suspect each week. The photo or time stamping is the answer each week on the computer portion which makes the rest of the game kind of stupid to waste your time with. If the entire game came in one box and was $25.00 I would say it would be worth it. I cancelled and would not recommend this to anyone.
Also - the final elimination- when its down to two last people becomes a guess- there is no real evidence to convict either one- you just guess- weak ending- my group ended feeling like either one could have done it.
If you are looking to spend $30.00/ month for 6 months to solve a crime with a weak ending - this is the game for you.

My advice- pass

title: Love coffee? Tour the world of coffee from your kitchen
text:
I received a monthly subscription to Driftaway Coffee and it’s a perfect gift for a coffee lover like me, who wants delicious coffee and the chance to educate my palate while exploring coffees from around the world. Driftaway provides the monthly coffee samplers, virtual tastings led by an expert (Brewer’s Cup Champion, no less!), detailed information about each coffee and the growers/collectives, and an opportunity to provide feedback to Driftaway so they can tailor future explorer boxes to your tastes. They also provide guides and information online to help you make a great cup with any coffee maker, while growing your knowledge.

All that and everything in the kit is sustainably sourced, from the compostable packages to the fair pricing and support of the farmers. As an independent, self-funded business they are walking the talk in their relationships with the farmers, their staff, and their clear commitment to give their customers a world-class, globetrotter’s experience of great coffee every month.
If you love coffee, Driftaway is absolutely the best way to learn at your own pace, month by month, while sipping some really exceptional coffee. I can’t wait for next month’s installment!

My son could learn 10x as much from a single children's book at the library--without relying on such basic, stereotypical material. This is for 6-10 year olds! You might think "well, this is just to spark their curiousity". Not for the $20 I pay every month for this garbage! This is basically a scam. Good idea, terribly executed. Basically for rich people who have money to flush. Don't do it!

title: This is the gift to give YOURSELF!
text: I originally signed up for TheraBox as a once-a-month gift to myself after seeing the great reviews online.  I have kept it because it was so much more than what I expected!  Outside of the subscription box gifts that I expect and appreciate as part of a subscription plan, it has truly been a blessing to me and my mental health.  It allows me to build myself emotionally and mentally in a private way that is respectful of my faith without being faith-based.  I have been so encouraged by the care in the positive notes and activities and have seen a jump in my mental care and emotional growth.  This is the beauty of what this box was curated for.  I receive fun gifts to try and use monthly -and since I know another box is coming in thirty days I push myself to spend time using the products and take care of myself more often and better, inside and out.  There are a variety of products each time and I have found high-quality items mixed in with simple products -which is great because it meets my needs on a variety of levels.  This is the only box I have recommended to others and would do so again.  I justify the monthly cost because, well...it's cheaper than therapy but it meets my needs at that level.  This is not a box of "stuff".  This is mindfully put together to give back to other organizations (many of the products sent are from environmentally or socially conscience companies), to encourage the receiver to grow mentally/emotionally and to pamper the recipient.  The products are on-time and so far always packed well so nothing is broken.  Every time I read the pamphlet inside which explains the theme and products, but especially for a note from the  TheraBox Team which always begins with "Hello! Beautiful Soul" -just makes me smile.  Thank you to TheraBox for the love and care in your box!

- mini-bath bombs for manicures/pedicures
- honey sugar scrub
In addition to the products, there is also a "happiness boosting activity." In this box, my activity was a book of poetry.
The items in the box seem to be of good quality, and I have not had any issues/reactions when using the products. Also, the quantity/size is good. I appreciate that an informational pamphlet is included with information about the product and the company/website that makes the product. Also, I like that I can get a discount on a product if I want to order more of it from the company/website. Being my first box, I'm interested to see how future boxes compare. So far, I think TheraBox is a fun subscription box and could make a good gift!

UPDATE (October 2021): I've been receiving my TheraBox for about 6 months, and it's been such a fun surprise each month. At first, I was a little worried that I'd be receiving a lot of essential oils and face serums, but I've only received those items a couple of times. I really like the variety of items. I feel like the items in my box are things I would not normally invest in myself. I also think a TheraBox would make a great gift for a friend.

text:
EDIT: I took the 16 records I received from these goof-balls to my local used record store. He gave me $0.25 in store credit each for the ones that were not completely worthless. I just gave hime the rest in hopes that somebody someday might be willing to pay $1 for this crap helping my local record store stay open. Comically bad. WAY OVERPRICED!

Imagine yourself at a flea market. But not the nice kind with hippies, organic farmers and local artisans. I'm talking about the ones with meth addicts looking for arbitrage opportunities and purveyors of stolen goods. Now imagine you happen upon a stand selling used records. But not just any records... these are like from your Aunt Tonya's basement. You know, K-tel, K-mart clearance, really crappy Columbia House releases that Aunt Tonya got in 1973 because she was too lazy to send back her card and decline the monthly selection. Now imagine that she stored these awful albums in a vat of hobo-urine until the paper sleeves and covers were smelly and disfigured beyond recognition . Then, she used the vinyl as a rasp to file down her fugly toenails to a manageable length for trimming. Then upon her death, the records were improperly stored for 40 years in a 125-degree thrift-store warehouse on their sides, because the thrift store realized that these albums sucked so bad that nobody would pay $1 for them making these records useless but the volunteer workers were too lazy to actually properly dispose of them so there they sat until the meth head agrees to pay $10 for the lot of 500 crappy Aunt Tonya records and takes them to the flea market to sell. Now, if you can imagine all of this, you will have an idea of just how utterly terrible the music you will get in your box is. Run from these clowns, I repeat, R-U-N.

text: My order came more quickly than expected.  After a couple unimpressive experiences with ordering looseleaf tea through various vendors in Amazon, I was hesitant to try again.  While I am a moderate to heavy tea drinker, I opted with the Explore-Light box.  Well, I'm happy to report that my August box had me pleasantly surprised.  I received Rooibos Tea (Pistachio), White Tea (Candied Apple), Fruit Tea (Sweet Heat) and Black Tea (Ceylon), along with brewing instructions, woven tea bags, and a cute little container for the bags.  My only disappointment is that I'm almost out of tea after only a few days.; so, that should tell you how much I'm enjoying all the flavors.  My only suggestion is to nix the empty tea bags or sell separately instead of including in the subscription box.  I am thinking those who are likely to subscribe, are avid tea drinkers and have their own tea strainer(s).  Removing the tea bags leaves room for more tea in the box.  I also am hoping that the seller finds a way to have customers rate each flavor and perhaps customize future subscriptions, based on the customer's feedback.

title: Quality snacks yet deceptive price
text: The quality of the snacks is amazing. Some of the snacks I got only could be found at higher-end grocery stores like Whole-Foods and Trader Joe's. What is disappointing is how quickly I ended up using the number of snacks. I only received 11-12 snacks on average and within 2 weeks everything was gone. You cannot rely on this for your only source of snacks. However, if you want a consistent supply of higher-end snacks that are filling and nutritious, this is the way to go. You can find really unique items like nitrogen-infused coffee, bars made up of chia seeds, and dates. It is really impressive how diverse the variety of snacks is provided every month. It is really exciting opening up my box every month like a kid on Christmas morning. Yes, you can probably get more at the store with the same amount of money. However, I am not sure if the quality of the snacks will match SnackSacks. Most of it is unprocessed, and in my case, plant-based items curated specifically for that particular season. I just don't have the time and patience to go through that process on my own. So I really don't even mind the number of snacks I get per month. It is a treat that is well worth savoring in my busy life.

I was super looking forward to every month and even when the boxes weren't spot on, I felt like I was getting my $15 worth.  However, starting at the new year they've began shipping the subscriptions in these "makeup pouches".  First of all, both months the pouches have arrived broken.  That's not even a big deal because I have enough makeup pouches as it is.  My bigger issue is that this is such an obvious attempt at masking the fact that they're decreasing the value of each month's products under the guise of a free makeup pouch.  In these two months I've thought the products have been redundant (a vitamin C serum both months) and each product (on average) is about half the size of what I was receiving before.  I was disappointed after receiving January's box and thought maybe my observations were a one-off, but given the fact I was a hardcore fan of my allure subscription I decided to give February's box a second chance and was disappointed again.

text:
Can I add a couple more stars to my rating...5 just doesn't seem like enuf
This is for my grandkids. Boy age 10 and Girl age 12
It took us a couple of days to open this as a family...grandkids, their mom and grampa... we watched the opening video and before it was even finished, they were both 'chomping at the bit' to get started. I told them to have patience while we watched the video for the first lesson. We watched the first lesson together; although my granddaughter had already grabbed her chromebook from school and was through the first 3 lessons, successfully, before we finished the video. My grandson was so eager to get started that he could not sit still in his chair.
Needless to say they both fell in love with this in less than 5 minutes.
Additionally, after returning home the following morning from a sleepover; the first thing out of their mouths were; 'where is bitsbox?' My granddaughter is doing a 'row a day'; there are four stored programs in each row...so within 24 hours she had already created 8 programs...and they all worked. My grandson had a few challenges with wanting to experiment more than simply just typing in the provided code...but will a little help from Grampa he was back on the road to successful programming.
The first set of lessons is teaching them scripting syntax by rote...thru examples...but they are encouraged to experiment...to try to break it if you will...the mark of ALL good programmers...grin...these are two skills set needed for any programmer...the other is understanding logic and then in turn how to apply logic to programming...I imagine this will be discovered as they move thru the lessons...
FANTASTIC Program by Bitsbox...the grandkids were creating and destroying apps; literally within minutes... no wonder they were so eager to work with it.

title: Maybe the funko magic is fading
text:
Had a subscription prior to Amazon taking over the shipping. Wife got me a new subscription for Christmas and I was pretty excited to see what would show up.

First off I assumed that Amazon would speed up the shipping, but that's not the case as the box still takes about a week to show up, and when it does its a box inside of a box, inside of another box. Pretty excessive if you ask me.

The actual contents this month were underwhelming, maybe funko is running out of ideas. A Jabbas skiff could pack a bit more luster given the iconic scene from Jedi, but instead I got a "mystery" mini that was obviously gonna be Jabba based on the theme and packaging. toothpick holders, aka shot glasses,and a Boba Fett luggage tag which goes great with my Death Star tag from a few months back. I like getting two pops and was pumped to see Lando, but the excitement faced when funko decided that Klaatu (marked with parenthesis as a skiff guard, highlighting how forgettable of a character he was) needed to be included. I get the desire for exclusivity, but it just wasn't happening for me.

I'll hold out hope for the February box, but if the boxes remain underwhelming I'll likely cancel and go back to grabbing random pops as add on items to orders.

title: Quantity not as advertised
text:
I purchased the Pure Tea Box back in December as I was exploring a regular subscription for single origin teas and Tea Runner's offered an option that fit the bill. On their website, it was stated that I would receive 0.75-1 oz of each of the four teas. However, when I eventually received the box, some of the teas had only 0.35 oz (or 10g) - I have a habit of recording all my teas in the pantry to take stock of what I have. This honestly left me feeling quite cheated as this was too large a variation, and since I have tried other tea subscriptions who generally give MORE rather than less of what they say they will. I even sent an email to confirm the amount of tea I was supposed to receive, and they explained that certain teas are more voluminous and so I would receive less (but still.... tea is sold by weight not volume....).

This was a great pity as I actually loved the teas received. After doing some math, I figured it would be cheaper to just buy the teas of the month separately from their website (since they even advertise what teas you get each month). Even if I consider curation costs (actually you only receive one other card with a short write up, and all information on the teas are on the packets itself). All in all, I would not recommend the subscription but may buy their teas occasionally.

The first box game came with an activity card to explain what to do. You were to paint while eating a treat and and asking each other questions. The chocolate covered sun seeds tasted old and seemed more like a single serving than for two people. The conversational questions lacked depth or excitement. I could of bought all of it from the dollar store and spent 1/4 the cost. I could of searched the internet for better question.

The second box came with no instructions. It had a card game. The 2x3 cards have questions like "name 4 items in a bloody mary", or name "4 nicknames for penis" and a plastic 30 second-hourglass. One person gives a question from the card, and the second person must come up for 4 question before the timer runs out. We got bored and stopped after a few minutes. Instead of a treat is came with the smallest fondue set I have ever seen. It might hold maybe four tablespoons. I am unsure if the candle that came with it would of warmed anything. So I did not try it. It also came with a tea size candle, you know the ones you can get for 50 cents.
The last box I got before cancelling was the same as the first, more painting, with little supplies. It had a small bag of jelly beans for the treat. I did not even read the instruction card. Do NOT buy. Waste of Money and no valuable ideas.
