title: Not for us
text:
I was very excited when I ordered this subscription for my 10-year-old son who loves all things STEM. What a disappointment when our first shipment arrived. The product, a "Mechanics: Levers, Linkages & Structures" building set is accompanied by a VERY DENSE booklet explaining basics machines. At the very end of this book are a few building activities for basic structures. My problems with this are:
1) I don't know about most 10-yr-olds, but mine certainly doesn't want to sit down and read a textbook on levers. He just wants to build and play.
2) The suggested structures are the end of the book are a bit boring -- a seesaw, wheelbarrow, scale, parking gate, etc.
3) The book even includes a quiz -- if this doesn't scare kids off I don't know what will.
4) The pieces are really hard to put together.

After working together for about 10 minutes to build the seesaw, my son complained that his hands hurt, ran off and started doing something more interesting.

I'd save your money and choose STEM toys on your own that are sure to appeal to your particular child's likes and dislikes.

text:
I wanted to love this subscription, I really did. The idea of it was amazing. The wonderful people at Amazon curating the plethora of STEM toys and picking the right ones to send people. Great in theory.

Execution... not so good.

1) the toys were "barely" over the price of the subscription. Not much of a "deal".

2) they did not come every month. they came infrequently. I think we ended up getting 3 kits in about 6 months...

3) no creativity or imagination in what they sent out. i was hoping for them curating beyond what i could do with a quick google search -- not so much. But, the straw that broke the camel's back: At the beginning of March, my son got the Kids First Automobile Engineer Kit -- it was great. After two long months, he got his next kit... the Kids First Aircraft Engineer Kit. Basically the same kit. Where is the imagination? Where are all the smart Amazon people coming up with creative options?

So, we cancelled. Oh well.

title: Two Months in and LOVING IT
text:
So far, it's been AMAZING.

The first toy usually costs about $10 more than the subscription, and it's got multiple uses. It's an Engino product, dealing with Levers and Linkages that builds over 20 different "simple machines". We've built the Folding Platform and the Swing and both worked GREAT. No issues putting together/taking apart (though I do help him read the instructions). He's 9, and autistic, and he adores building these functional "simple machines". I, personally, can't wait until we build the miniature catapult!

The second toy is currently on sale...for about $12 more than the subscription cost. Normally, it runs $30 more. So I certainly can't complain about getting a $50 toy for $20! We haven't played with it yet (it's a little more advanced than he is right now) but it looks AMAZING. It's a SmartLab product that can make over 50 computerized "devices" - like a doorbell, light shows, etc. It has a microprocessor, Motion detector, a Light Detector, LED lights, and more. I'm sure that when he gets around to using it, he's going to love it.

title: Unrealized Potential
text:
The entire concept is definitely a great idea, and my son is well aware each month he's going to get a new STEM toy. Just seeing his excitement around what's coming for him is enough to keep the subscription going for now. At this age, we just want to make sure he's developing a love for STEM.

As a former science teacher, the quality of the actual toys/sets/kits selected could be so much better. The very first one was fantastic - it had three small "science fair" like experiments we did together in our kitchen, and each one had a sticker-like badge to give him upon completion. We were all excited about building a sense of cumulative growth by putting his badge stickers in his journal each month to see how many cool things we'd do. But alas, that great setup was only with the first manufacturer, and since then it has been a mix of items from many different manufacturers. Some are amazing, like a coding mouse + maze game. Others are pretty disappointing, like a big experiment kit that required buying additional supplies for every experiment. I'm hoping the quality of the monthly STEM Club goods increases soon. I'm not sure how long my son's (or my) excitement will last.

text: I had high hopes for this subscription. I have seen reviews where subscribers have received Pink Floyd's The Wall double album and a half speed master version of Rolling Stones Exile On Main Street. My first selection was fine: The Clash's London Calling double album. It was a nice addition to my collection. (That's the main reason for my 2 star review). The next month I received a David Bowie picture disc. Since one of my concerns is the quality of the vinyl pressing, and picture discs are notoriously noisy, I returned it for a refund. Still pretty happy with the service. The month after that I received a Van Haylen disc and this month I got a CCR double disk. Amazon sells these discs for 24.54 and 22.97 respectively. I am at a loss as to why I should pay more for an album through this subscription than its regular price. I have cancelled my subscription.

title: Fantastic experiments and learning
text:
I subscribed to this recently, and want to share my experience. I have 10yo old son. I got the first box with two experiments - foam eruption and snake. And this is really exciting! From my son's perspective, it's fun to conduct these experiments like a real chemist: mix powders, pour chemicals into flask, shake, set on fire. And the result is amazing: this funny reactions last for some time to really enjoy them.

I enjoyed detailed description of how the reactions work, ion/cation, formulas that I mostly forgot since school. I tried to explain some of this to my son: I'm happy that he now knows how water breaks molecules into ions. But most of these will be interesting for high school kids.

Description doesn't say it, but I liked that every experiment has enough chemicals to run it at least twice(!). More, I'm surprised that all chemicals are safe and can be found at home: soap, citric acid, baking soda, food colorant and etc. I wish the box to have matches in it, but I guess some regulations ban it.

title: Easy discounts. Service has potential.  No risk with free returns for records you don't want.
text:
So far, I've been in this for two months. First month was The Clash - London Calling. Second month was a Frank Zappa in New York live album. Not really a Zappa fan, so choose to cancel the order before it was shipped. It seems that each record can still be different month to month, as I saw The Clash and Pink Floyd for someone's July/Aug. Others got CCR instead of Zappa. Some people are getting duplicates, which really shouldn't be an issue and is on Amazon to make sure a month isn't wasted on a duplicate/rejected album.

I think to keep costs down, having a choice might not be an option. But I feel with a free return/cancel there's no real problem, outside of not getting a record, but at least you haven't paid for nothing. You have to be quick to cancel before an order is shipped, having the Amazon app helps out to get notifications when it is added to your orders to review prior to shipping and cancel. But even if I missed a cancel, I could just return the unopened record. Just requires a trip to the local Amazon approve shipping location, which takes some time out of my day.

Ideally, it would be nice to have a choice between 2-3 albums and/or having replacement for prior month ROTM. It would be nice to substitute a current month with a prior month's ROTM if you do not like it at a bare minimum. It would be nice to have genres of music to pick from at a later point to help with less choice rejections. There would be nice selections that can do 80's/90's as well.

title: Amazing audiophile sound from new pressings
text:
I recently built my dream stereo rig: Pro-Ject turntable and phono stage, Audio Research preamp, McIntosh 250wpc power amp, and Magnepan LRS loudspeakers. Just one little problem: My high-school era LPs were a little worn.

Since joining Vinyl/Month, I have brand new pressings of Dark Side OTM, The Wall, CCR, Charlie Mingus, Jimi Hendrix (mono but nevertheless sounds like he's playing RIGHT IN THE ROOM), and I substituted a Zappa for one month's selection.

The sound from these 180-gram virgin vinyl pressings is three-dimensional like I have never heard before. Growing up hearing "Fortunate Son" on my car's AM radio, I had no idea that the depth and resonance of John Fogarty's guitar licks could make my hair stand on end.

I am so glad I joined this. So much fun to see what's coming next!

title: Deceptive Billing, Lackluster Products
text:
I originally signed up for this subscription for a promotion they were offering and to check out what types of items they ship out

I placed my original order on January 3rd, 2020 for $38.75 and got it today. I have to say that for the almost $40 I paid, I got maybe less than half that in value of what was inside.

But that's not the only thing I got today. I also received the surprise of ANOTHER $40 charge on my card. Mind you, this is less than two weeks after my first "monthly" payment.

When contacting them about it it turns out that if you order on the 3rd, you also get billed on the 15th for a box (full to the brim of what I'm sure are the finest products China has to offer) that you won't receive for another month.

This information is provided exactly nowhere when signing up, and instead must be found in their FAQs section of their website. While perusing their FAQs selection, also be sure to read the part where they DO NOT offer refunds, explicitly stating that this is because they CAN NOT guarantee your satisfaction

All in all, you're probably better off wearing a blindfold and grabbing $40 in random accessories off the shelves of your local sporting goods store. Not only will you get more bang for your buck, but you'll also have better customer service and return options.

title: Great replacement to my old Marvel Teeblox subscription - for the most part
text:
** Edited ** - I need to add that the December short has been a disappointment since its a Christmas theme and it hasnt arrived and as of Dec 24, hasnt even shipped. Its estimated arrival date is now Jan 4th - so why bother sending a Christmas Themed shirt in January?? Its a bummer that the December delivery has been handled so poorly - no reason it could be shipped before Christmas in an attempt to have it for Christmas.

I used to love my Marvel TeeBlox subscription until they decided to drop the Marvel subscription for a bunch of lame generic shirts. I tried Lootcrates Marvel box and even the tee box subscription - Loot crate was okay 2 years ago, but they changed and seem to send lower quality items and the shirt designs are boring, and one shipment was the same shirt from a few months earlier in a different color - So I have been hoping to find a new tee subscription for Marvel gear - and I finally did.

I stumbled on this one while looking around Amazons monthly subscription services on tee-shirts and toys. Decided, Why not try this one for a few months - This is my third month and all three shirts have been great quality with equally as great designs. I like that they use any Holidays in the month to theme the shirt that is sent - The Halloween shirt was my first one and it was a great design. It wasn't Halloween themed directly, but since it had the Green Goblin as the villain it had pumpkins in the design. November was just X-Men, but a good design and great color shirt - December is Christmas themed with Deadpool (and a funny shirt overall).

Could you get a shirt you dont like? Sure - Its a blind box subscription and it will happen. I dont think this should upset anyone, you should know this when you sign up for a mystery type of service. If you dont like one of the shirts, you can always send it back - You cant do that will Lootcrate or other monthly mystery boxes.

In the end, its a great service to receive a monthly "mystery present" - but at least you know it will be a quality shirt and theres a good chance it will have a great design based on Marvel.

title: The Best Gift to Give to Your Enemies and Worst to Your Relatives.
text:
I bought Simple Loose Leaf Tea Subscription Box out of curiosity and interest, and after receiving the box, I just wanted to write an honest review to inform other potential customers what it's like to subscribe to a tea subscription service. I'm glad I did. Simple Loose Leaf Tea Subscription Box is just another poorly advertised subscription box that's filled with some pretty terrible loose leaf tea, and promises so much more than it actually delivers.
I tried the BLOOD ORANGE HERBAL TEA in one of my unscented metal mesh cups , brewed it using the Simple Loose Leaf Tea Taste Test Instructions. This tea was by far the most disgusting drink I have ever tasted. It was a putrid reddish yellow that reminded me of something I think I'd make if I had to drink juice from a disgustingly nasty kiddy pool. The taste, the smell, and the presentation made me wonder if Simple Loose Leaf is just another excuse to advertise a bunch of overhyped flavors and hope people will buy their tea and nothing else. The taste was a far cry from what I've grown accustomed to receiving from Simple Loose Leaf. I will say that as a daily tea drinker and enthusiast, I'd avoid this one at all costs.

title: Amazon Orders Don’t Include Apron!
text:
This box is actually really cute and has a lot of curriculum towards the theme of the box. That being said, I think they should lower the price $10. $14 would be a really fair price point for this but the current price is outrageous for a box of print outs. I would even be willing to pay that without the included tool, patch and box it comes in. Everything you need is packed into a small envelope in the box and that would be simple to ship. We got tongs in our box this month. They are of nice quality and definitely will be used but in no way were essential to our Swedish themed box or any of the cooking lessons. I would have rather paid a lower price and bought my own tongs. Also, it is not stated except in answered questions but when you buy this box on Amazon, it does not include the apron. Seriously? That apron is where you are supposed to put your included patches each month so at this point, I’m really not too interested in the patches.

I think I’ll try this one more month and cancel if I still don’t think it’s worth it. We do Green Kids and both of the Little Passports boxes which have similar price points but feel like they are priced fairly for what they include. Radish Kids feels like an envelope of print outs that you easily could find curriculum for online or in a kids cook book - although if they lowered their price, I would feel like it was worth the time I saved finding that curriculum.

title: Don't waste your time or your money
text:
I was gifted a six month subscription and was beyond excited for it. Having previously read reviews about how frustrating it was to have to wait for the next box; I waited until I had the full set before sitting down to "play" with a friend. To say I was disappointed would be an understatement.

The items sent in each box were generally a handful of printouts and a sprinkling of plastic garbage from a bulk retailer. The story often felt forced to bend around and include whatever random favor they threw in the box that month.

The clues in some instances required huge bodies of knowledge the average person doesn't have, or giant leaps to reach the expected conclusion.

Some examples:

1. A 1.5 inch piece of plastic thread taped to the back of an astronomy themed postcard. Apparently I was too know the postcard depicted Orpheus in constellation and the plastic tubing was also to indicate a link to Orpheus and his musical talents. What was the significance of Orpheus? Simply to let you know to continue looking forward. Irrelevant to the game's overall solution.

2. a postcard showing the name of a city. This was included to confirm the writer's previous claims of being from that city. How that confirms anything is beyond me.

3. A printout of some email correspondence between two people. This was too prompt you to email one of the parties yourself so that you could receive an automated response with more information. Because when I play a game that advertises "everything you need to solve the case is in the box" I automatically think about how I'm going to have to email fictional characters as part of the game play.

While playing it also became clear that things were missing. Some boxes lacked all the items they were supposed to come with. I ended up finding that out when I was finally able to locate lists of what each box should contain online. Furthermore, through research online, though this was supposed to be a six box story, it actually required more than six boxes. I didn't have two or three of the necessary boxes to solve the case.

As this was a gift I had no idea how insanely expensive it was until I had to start looking online to figure out what was missing from my packages. For the price, this is a total rip off. I would not recommend it for yourself or for a gift. Spend that money on a murderer mystery dinner theater, or an escape room. I guarantee you'll be happier with either of those options than with this garbage scam.

Honestly, the most satisfaction I got from this game was when I was able to dump it straight in the trash and clear off my table.

title: We Love It
text:
We really enjoy this company and their products. First, if you aren't familar, the idea is each season is 6 "episodes", and you get one episode per month. The premise is that a small town investigator doesn't have the resources to solve a murder, and they are enlisting your help (you being a more seasoned investigator). If you actually order through the Hunt a Killer website, you can expedite your boxes if you want to go through them faster. The Hunt a Killer website also has other seasons, entire box sets, and shorter non-subscription premiums of all kinds if you prefer harder mysteries, or science fiction, or paranormal, or family-friendly, etc. Many of the episodes have a goal of eliminating a suspect or two, but you shouldn't stop just at that. The people who finish each episode in 20 minutes must not be reading everything and finding all the clues. You should take notes and make timelines, as you will fill in time gaps and catch characters in lies or misinformation later as more evidence comes in with interviews and phone records, etc. You are piecing together a crime story with many characters, events, timelines, and items. The "small town investigator" sends you bagged evidence, interviews, autopsy reports, drug test results, maps, newspaper clippings, crime scene pictures, etc each month as they find them. There are website links to follow with surveillance footage, or recorded audio, or social media postings from the suspects, or high school discipline records. There are clues hidden in everything they send. There are ciphers to figure out. The attention to detail is unbelievable. Additionally, I can't relate to the people who said their customer service was bad. I emailed their website and had a response in a day. I posted a question in their Facebook group and was answered by one of their reps in less than one hour. Overall, it usually takes the two of us 90 minutes per episode (or box). I think $30 is reasonable for 90 minutes of entertainment for two people. We would spend that much or more if we went out somewhere for our entertainment instead. We recently bought The Woods box set of 5 episodes for $140 and the first box took us almost 3 hours! There were so many layers to it. It was so fun though because it was just like being in a horror movie (it was a paranormal story about witches summoning spirits). Overall, you get out of it what you put into it. If you are one dimensional and don't piece all aspects of the story together and only focus on eliminating one suspect, then you're not going to like it and you will sell the whole experience short. If you like challenging yourself and looking at all the angles, details, and storylines, you will love it too.

If you are considering it, I would recommend joining their official Facebook group. The reps will answer any questions and you can see how other people like it.

title: Tedious, boring, and no challenge
text:
Extremely easy. This is fit for middle school kids. Extremely expensive for a mediocre story.

You can actually solve every box instantaneously by simply checking the document provided in the database. They always make sure to explicitly call out ONE name in a piece of evidence with date and time that rules them out as a suspect.

Also, all the "puzzle solving" is just a series of shift cyphers. Over and over and over and over again. They usually don't even provide any useful information. You can usually just skip deciphering them and still get the gist of everything.

Extremely tedious, boring, and no challenge.

What I love:
- my kids LOVE it. (my 8 year old is the perfect age, she loves the fun stickers and just wants to create her own little apps all day)
- It's actually teaching them.... I've always been skeptical of how any subscription could actually teach coding to children.. but they've nailed it! -> It starts out slow by making them copy short sequences that get slightly more complex as you go, then it offers challenges where they have to figure out for themselves how to get new results. Brilliant.
- You get so many little exercises per box, so you can show your kids that they can recycle code from other projects and add it to new ones to do all kinds of things. It's fun and embodies everything I love about coding...

but mostly, I feel like a good parent because I'm actually teaching my kids a skill that will potentially give them a HUGE advantage in life... and they love it.

I cannot recommend this enough.

title: RaddishKids has impacted my kids culinary skills!
text:
We have received the RaddishKid box for six months now. While it does not include ingredients, I find the boxes we've received valuable. My daughters have prepared recipes they would not have created otherwise.

My teenage daughters will have a plethora of recipes to take into adulthood with them.

I find the boxes simpler to use than searching online or cookbooks. In the past, I have bought cookbooks for my daughters, and they did not prepare nearly as many recipes from them as they have from the boxes we've received. I believe it's because the recipes are selected and tasteful. Yes, the boxes are more expensive than a recipe book, but an unused book isn't helping us reach our cooking goals. Plus, most recipe books for kids we've purchased seem to use prepared ingredients versus cooking from scratch.

As far as the apron, you will receive it if you order a 6 or 12 month paid in full subscription from their site directly. The month to month box does not include the apron. We didn't need the apron so it's not a big deal. They do sell them separately on their site though.

We usually receive our box mid-month from Amazon. This works well for us because the recipes can be created at anytime.

If you're looking to get your kids in the kitchen without hassle, consider RaddishKids. It's a simple way for them to gain autonomy in the kitchen and learn some new recipes. They may also find their favorite meal in a box. My daughter cooks one of the recipes at least twice a month because she likes it so much!

title: BAM! Thwip! POW!

My husband & I loved comics as kids, we both still have all of our 70s classics (Archie’s, Marvel, Star Wars…)
But the pandemic, and Kevin Feige’s vision of the MCU, has thrown us back into the graphic novel world with a fervor.
I wasn’t sure where to start my journey, so when I saw the Comic Garage on here, I thought “Why not?”
10 months in…and each month I start to salivate when I know my next package is set to arrive. And now that I’m finding the characters and storylines I’m drawn to, I’ve requested more of that ilk, and less of the ones I found to be “meh”. The Comic Garage does not disappoint.

title: I feel bad leaving a bad review, I like Funko, but I’m disappointed..
text: It didn’t meet my expectations.  The Deadpool box was my first one, and I canceled my subscription the day I received my box.  The Funko vinyl was good, but the rest of the items really felt like they were an afterthought.  I did put the luggage tag on my bag, and it stayed on during my last trip, but it’s doesn’t feel all that secure or well made.  The small window area for my information isn’t very large and didn’t line up with the insert for my info.  The keychain was alright I guess, but again if feels flimsy and not well made.  The metal screw drilled into the top to hold the keychain on has split the plastic apart and it’s loose.  I’d be afraid to actually use it as anything other than a decoration.  Maybe it’ll become a Xmas tree ornament.  Last, and least, was the plastic school bus taco holder... I can’t imagine anyone actually using that for its implied purpose.  It’s not really washable without ruining the stickers.  Even used as a phone holder as some people recommended doesn't really make it a worthwhile item.  If this box had included a decent T-Shirt, or if at least one of the other items felt thoughtful and well made, I’d have been much happier.  The whole box didn’t exactly feel like a real value.  I feel bad leaving a poor review because I do like the Funko company, but I’m still disappointed, whether rightfully so or not.

title: Young Entry Level Music Enthusiast will Love this. Veteran Music Lovers Can pass on this one.
text:
Before I get into my review, here is what I have received so Far:

The Clash - London Calling
The Rolling Stones - Exile on Main Street
Diana Ross & The Supremes - Number Ones
Chronicle: The 20 Greatest Creedence Clearwater Rival Hits
Pink Floyd - Dark Side of The Month
The Who - Quadrophenia
Pink Floyd - The Wall (2016 Remaster)

First, the albums are without question great selections. For anyone just getting into vinyl, you’ll dig the selection. These albums are a great starter set.

However, variety of artists/bands and also omitting “greatest hits albums” would make this better. Veterans of vinyl or audiophiles can pass on this. I’ve gotten two Pink Floyd Albums so far. I’m not knocking Pink Floyd, absolute legends, but could we have picked just one album from them?

I haven’t received John Lennon, Aretha Franklin, David Bowie or Led Zeppelin yet. If you all provide feedback maybe this could be a 5/5 subscription. It just squeaks to an an average rating for me.

title: No real point in getting this

The records I remember them sending were: The Wall, Exile on Main Street, Dark Side of the Moon, Tusk, CCR Greatest Hits, Boots by Nancy Sinatra, London Calling, and I don’t remember the rest since I skipped several boxes. But I would not recommend signing up. You can of course return unwanted selections which is why I kept it for so long but it’s been months since I kept one.

title: Jury is still out
text:
I'm a newbie to vinyl collecting so this "club" seemed like a good fit. Joined in late November and got a record added to my cart a few days later, but it won't arrive until the very end of January. So a two month wait for The Who Sell Out...
In reading the other reviews it seems like not everyone gets the same record each month. Sounds like some people received The Who Sell Out a month or two before I joined.
So jury is still out... for a newbie with a starter collection like me this club could end up being good even if I get things people got months ago.
In doing more research after the fact it seems like this Amazon subscription (so far) is more basic than other monthly clubs. Nothing exclusive or special. The lack of transparency in selections (past, present, future) is odd and again makes me think we all don't get the same record each month.
The biggest concern for me is the other reviews saying that the monthly selection can at times be bought (on Amazon!) for less than the subscription price. If true that's pretty darn lame. Yes, there are remedies (like skipping that month's subscription and buying record for the lower price) but to have to jump through those extra hoops to get the best price on their own website just speaks to the level of effort getting put in on their side.
So again... jury is still out, but not off to a great start.

title: Love the serendipity, thoughtful design, and cool gear!
text: I’ve now received two monthly boxes from Cairn. It’s a super cool idea, and I love the serendipity of getting new items every month. In a time of social distancing Cairn has helped fill that void of not being able to wander the aisles of my favorite outdoor store and find cool new gear. I love the care given to the design and the thought put into the theme of every box. Can’t wait to see what comes next month!

title: Love This Company!
text: I've been a big fan of Cairn for a few years now and have always wanted to subscribe. Finally I was able to purchase my first box and I have to say, I love it. The sunglasses I received are badass and already proving to be useful as the summer quickly approaches. What I love about Cairn over other subscription box companies is that they really value our evnironment and doing what is necessary to limit their carbon footprint and help give back. Was just recently reading about their Gear Up Give Back program and it's programs like this that make me want to follow and be involved with a company. Thanks again and keep the awesome products coming!

title: Great Find!

title: Not worth the price.
text:
I was very disappointed with the box I received. I was expecting stuff from the show like in the pictures advertised. Like keys from the show and stuff like that. But all I got was like dollar store stuff with the logos on it. If the box was cheaper, it’d be fine but I paid over 60$ for this and I barely liked anything from this box. I don’t think it’s worth it to gamble another box and hope for the best to be disappointed again.

-The shirt is fine, I will wear it.
-The glass could’ve been better like the one I saw in a review: clear with the white anti possession symbol.
-The light box really set me off thinking this was some kind of joke. Like, again, if this was a cheap box I’d understand but like really? Some fairy lights that barely light up a basic image? I feel like there could’ve been something way better. Very disappointing.
-the lanyard is fine, sort of as to be expected.
-I have a collection of pins so I do like the pin. There’s one win.
-the Bluetooth speaker has got to be some joke. Like really? It is a very sad product that you can definitely get in a dollar store. Can’t believe I paid this much for this stuff.
-the bracelet is fine if that is your style which it isn’t mine. It’s nicely made but I probably won’t ever wear it.
-the rug is pretty funny. I am keeping it. It is very funny to think about. Like, what the heck.

But yes over all this particular box was NOT worth it to me. It is very easy to slap a logo on some dollar store items and I do not see how this box is supposedly worth over a hundred dollars. Very disappointing considering how excited I was. The pictures need to be taken down so no one else is led to believe they will get cool show items every time.

title: If you’re looking for a box, you have the wrong subscription
text: First few boxes were great. Higher value items, presentation box and bag added to perceived value. As the subscription continued, items became more gimmicky, but I hung with it. Last box was no where near the value of what was paid. And there was no box. Odd so I sent in a question. I was told there absolutely should have been a box and to send pictures of what I received. Sent above picture and then told they were trying to deliver in a environmentally friendly way. Since I always repurposed the box, and they stated it should have come in a box, I’m not feeling great about quality control. I will save the $170 for a company that at least has its story straight. So disappointing.
